Alongside the mystery of Tessa’s death, the novel examines marriage, political complicity, postcolonial inequality, and the human cost of treating African lives as expendable. Suspense grows through dossiers, interviews, and shifting perspectives as Justin moves from passive observer to determined seeker of the truth.
book-6696: After a family tragedy in 1940, twelve-year-old Lou Cardinal and her younger brother Oz leave New York City for the mountains of southwestern Virginia, where they are taken in by their great-grandmother Louisa Mae Cardinal on a small farm. In a community shaped by poverty, coal mining, and hard rural labor, the children adjust to a new landscape of church meetings, schoolhouse lessons, and mountain traditions. Their search for stability is complicated by grief, questions about their father’s past, and a legal struggle over land that powerful outside interests want to control. The novel combines family drama, regional history, and elements of mystery as it explores inheritance, memory, literacy, and the conflict between economic exploitation and a deep attachment to place.
book-6697: A lively farmyard romp unfolds in rhythmic verse as cows, pigs, ducks, horses, and other barnyard animals clap, stomp, twirl, and bow through a communal dance. Set in a bright rural barn and pasture landscape, the book follows a simple sequence of movement and sound, inviting very young listeners to join the action with bouncing, tapping, and call-and-response repetition. The central activity is not a plot-driven conflict but the gathering of animals into shared motion, turning bedtime or storytime into participation and play. Short rhymes, sound words, and patterned commands support early language development, while the humorous animal antics create a sense of celebration. Themes include music, coordination, social play, and the pleasure of rhythm, repetition, and physical movement in an everyday farm setting.
book-6698: A rural Minnesota soybean field yields a mass grave, and investigator Lucas Davenport joins the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to identify the victims and trace the killers before more bodies appear. The case moves from farm roads and small towns to bars, motels, and transient work camps as detectives piece together missing-person reports, forensic evidence, and witness fragments. Lucas confronts a predator who uses ordinary Midwestern landscapes as cover, turning open country into a place of concealment and fear. The novel follows a procedural hunt shaped by surveillance, interviews, and strategic traps, while exploring violence against vulnerable women, the difficulty of seeing patterns in scattered crimes, and the strain a prolonged manhunt places on police work and private life.
book-6699: After her husband’s sudden death in a hotel room, Tanya Dubois abandons her life and begins moving from town to town under stolen names, cash in hand, always watching for anyone who might recognize her. Motels, bars, bus stations, and temporary jobs form the shifting landscape of her flight across the United States. As Tanya reinvents herself again and again, the novel gradually reveals a history of deception, violence, and grief that makes both the police and unknown pursuers dangerous. The suspense turns on practical details of evasion—false identification, changing appearance, vanished records—while the mystery asks who Tanya really is and what she is escaping. Themes of identity, survival, female vulnerability, and the instability of truth shape this road-bound psychological thriller.
book-67: Set in Afghanistan from the 1960s through the rise of the Taliban and the years of war that follow, this historical novel traces the intertwined lives of two women, Mariam and Laila, whose paths converge in Kabul under the same troubled household. Through forced marriage, motherhood, displacement, and political violence, the story follows how private suffering is shaped by public upheaval. Streets, homes, refugee camps, and ruined neighborhoods form a vivid backdrop as Soviet occupation, civil war, and religious repression narrow ordinary choices. The central conflict grows from survival within an abusive domestic life while the country itself fractures around them. Themes of female friendship, endurance, family loyalty, grief, and sacrifice run through the narrative, alongside a sustained portrait of how war and patriarchy govern daily existence.
book-670: After a car accident leaves him in a long coma, Maine schoolteacher Johnny Smith wakes to find that physical contact gives him vivid visions of hidden facts and possible futures. His new clairvoyance turns him into a local curiosity and draws police investigators, desperate families, and strangers who want answers from the dead zone in his mind. The central crisis emerges when Johnny shakes hands with an ambitious politician, Greg Stillson, and sees a future of political power and mass destruction. Set in small-town and urban New England, the novel combines supernatural horror, suspense, and speculative fiction while examining fate, free will, public violence, disability, and the moral burden of acting on knowledge that no one else can verify.
book-6700: At a wealthy Florida resort town, privileged musician and notorious playboy Rush Finlay watches his carefully controlled life unravel when Blaire Wynn arrives with a pickup truck, a pistol, and nowhere else to go. She is the daughter of his estranged father’s new wife, and their immediate attraction collides with family resentment, class differences, and a house full of secrets. Told from Rush’s perspective, the novel follows his struggle between desire and loyalty as he tries to protect Blaire while concealing painful truths about their parents and his own past. Set in Rosemary Beach’s gated homes, clubs, and beaches, the story centers on forbidden love, grief, guilt, wealth, and the consequences of choosing honesty too late.
book-6701: On an alternate nineteenth-century American frontier shaped by folk magic, political rivalry, and Indigenous power, young Alvin Miller travels west with his brother Measure as rumors spread that he may become a maker who can heal, build, and remake the world. Their journey crosses the violent ambitions of William Henry Harrison, schemes for land seizure, and the visions of Ta-Kumsaw, a Native prophet struggling to unite tribes against white expansion. While Alvin is still only a boy, his gifts place him inside larger conflicts over settlement, prophecy, race, and nationhood. The novel blends wilderness travel, frontier communities, and supernatural talents to examine destiny, colonial violence, spiritual calling, and the competing dreams that shape an imagined early America.
book-6702: An alphabet quest unfolds through lavish fantasy illustrations in which each letter introduces a crowded scene built from alliteration, hidden objects, and visual puzzles. From “An Armoured Armadillo Avoiding an Angry Alligator” onward, animals, artifacts, and patterned backgrounds fill each spread, inviting close observation as children search for letter-themed details. Rather than following a conventional plot, the book uses the structure of the alphabet to move through whimsical habitats, surreal interiors, and dreamlike landscapes populated by birds, beasts, musicians, monarchs, and machines. The central activity lies in decoding language and image together: identifying repeated sounds, naming unfamiliar creatures, and spotting concealed symbols. Themes include wordplay, visual literacy, classification, and the pleasure of discovery, making it useful for early vocabulary building as well as independent browsing.
book-6703: In contemporary New York, rare-books librarian Beatrice De Novo is hired to translate a cache of medieval documents for Giovanni Vecchio, a wealthy and secretive patron whose household hides a dangerous supernatural reality. As Beatrice deciphers journals, letters, and histories, she is drawn into the politics of an ancient vampire family and a wider world shaped by elemental powers, old feuds, and carefully buried crimes. The central conflict joins scholarly investigation with personal peril: the manuscripts contain knowledge someone wants suppressed, and Beatrice’s growing connection with Giovanni puts both of them at risk. Blending paranormal romance with gothic mystery, the novel focuses on archives, language, bloodlines, secrecy, and the tension between human vulnerability and immortal power.
book-6704: Set in working-class Buffalo from the 1950s through the 1970s, this semi-autobiographical novel follows Jess Goldberg, a butch lesbian navigating bar culture, factory labor, street harassment, and police violence. Jess searches for language and community in a world that punishes gender nonconformity, moving through raids, love affairs, union politics, and shifting queer networks. As social pressures intensify, the narrative explores the difficult choices around passing, masculinity, hormones, and survival, without reducing identity to a single label. The book portrays lesbian and transgender history from the ground level of bars, shop floors, and rented rooms, and examines class solidarity, state repression, erotic life, and the cost of living visibly. Its central concern is how a person builds selfhood and kinship under sustained social hostility.
book-6705: After vanishing with her best friend and then reappearing alone, high school student Samantha returns home with no memory of the past several days. Cassie is still missing, and police, classmates, and Samantha’s family all want answers she cannot give. As she tries to reconstruct the night in question, she discovers that the life she forgot includes a cruel social circle, damaged friendships, and a long history with Carson Ortiz, the boy next door who may know her better than anyone. Anonymous messages and fragments of memory suggest that someone is watching her and that Cassie’s disappearance is tied to secrets Samantha once helped keep. Set in a suburban American school community, the novel combines amnesia, missing-person suspense, romance, guilt, identity, and the fear of learning who she used to be.
book-6706: Set in rural New Jersey in 1914, this historical mystery follows Constance Kopp, who lives on a farm with her younger sisters, practical Norma and restless Fleurette. After a wealthy factory owner crashes his automobile into their buggy, Constance refuses a quiet settlement and demands fair payment for the damage. The dispute draws the sisters into a campaign of threats, hired thugs, and public scrutiny as they face a powerful man used to getting his way. As local law officers become involved, Constance’s stubborn sense of justice pushes her beyond the narrow role expected of women in her era. Drawing on a real case, the novel explores gender, class, early automobiles, family loyalty, and the uneasy boundary between domestic life and the criminal justice system.
book-6707: Set in the world of professional ballet from the 1970s through the early 2000s, this novel follows Joan Joyce, an American dancer whose intense affair with Soviet star Arslan Rusakov alters the course of her life. She leaves the stage, marries a close friend, and settles into suburban family life, but the demands of art, memory, and desire continue to shape her choices. As her gifted son grows up under the shadow of dance and ambition, old loyalties and buried secrets resurface. Moving between New York, Paris, and Connecticut, the narrative examines performance, marriage, motherhood, artistic sacrifice, and the costs of devoting a body and a life to beauty. Ballet technique, rehearsal discipline, and backstage hierarchies give the family drama its texture and tension.
book-6708: A small boy brings home a pet fish from a shop after receiving one strict instruction: feed it only a tiny pinch of food. Curious and careless, he gives the fish more than he should, and the animal begins to grow at an absurd rate. What starts in a bowl soon overwhelms a vase, a tub, and finally the whole house, turning an ordinary home into a comic scene of splashing water and frantic problem-solving. Set in a simple domestic world rendered for early readers, the story follows the escalating consequences of ignoring advice and trying to hide a mistake. Its humor comes from repetition, visual exaggeration, and the contrast between a child’s good intentions and the chaos they create.
book-6709: On Masaq’ Orbital, a vast artificial ring world of the post-scarcity Culture, an old war still shapes the present. A famous Chelgrian composer arrives to conduct a memorial performance, while a Culture citizen and the Orbital’s artificial intelligence watch his visit with growing concern. Beneath the ceremonies lies a covert mission tied to the Culture’s intervention in a distant civil conflict, an act that left grief, political upheaval, and unresolved blame. The novel moves between habitats, diplomatic spaces, and machine minds to examine revenge, guilt, memory, and the moral cost of utopian power. Its central tension asks how a civilization dedicated to pleasure and freedom responds when its benevolence produces catastrophe, and whether mourning can become another form of violence.
book-671: During the First World War, convalescing officer Arthur Hastings stays at Styles Court, an English country house where family tensions simmer around the wealthy matriarch Emily Inglethorp and her much younger husband. When Emily dies suddenly after a night of violent convulsions, suspicion falls across the household: resentful relatives, servants, and a husband with an obvious motive. Hastings turns to Hercule Poirot, a Belgian refugee living nearby, whose meticulous methods transform scattered clues, wills, coffee cups, locked rooms, and contradictory testimony into a disciplined inquiry. Set in a manor crowded with secrets and wartime unease, the novel follows the unraveling of inheritance disputes, jealousy, deception, and performance, while establishing Poirot’s reliance on observation, psychology, and order in the face of chaos.
book-6710: After a school bus accident costs her a leg, high school track athlete Jessica must relearn how to move through daily life while grieving the loss of running, the sport that shapes her identity. Set in a contemporary American suburb, the novel follows her difficult rehabilitation, her adjustment to a prosthetic limb, and her growing friendship with Rosa, a classmate with cerebral palsy who understands disability in ways Jessica never has. Practical obstacles at school and on the track become the central conflict as Jessica struggles with pain, anger, dependence, and changing expectations from others. The story explores athletic ambition, body image, friendship, privilege, resilience, and the difference between being pitied and being truly seen, while tracing Jessica’s determination to return to competition.
book-6711: Set after the violent events of the Dark Duet, this dark romance thriller returns to the uneasy bond between Caleb and Livvie as they try to build a future from a history shaped by abduction, revenge, and coercion. The story moves through the aftermath rather than the original captivity, focusing on how daily life, desire, and loyalty are altered by trauma that does not simply disappear. Domestic spaces and private conversations carry the tension of the criminal world that formed them, while questions of trust, guilt, power, and forgiveness remain active in the relationship. The novella centers less on external plot than on emotional reckoning, examining whether intimacy can survive manipulation and whether damaged people can choose something other than violence.
book-6712: Driven by a sudden decision to run through the night, this memoir follows an ordinary professional and family man as he becomes an ultramarathon runner who seeks distances far beyond the standard 26.2 miles. The narrative moves through deserts, mountain trails, frozen landscapes, and city streets, recounting all-night training runs, extreme races, injuries, exhaustion, and the logistical demands of endurance sport. Alongside vivid accounts of events such as hundred-mile competitions and punishing heat, it reflects on work, marriage, fatherhood, diet, pain tolerance, and the psychology of persistence. The central tension lies between conventional adult life and a compulsion to test the body’s limits. Themes include discipline, obsession, resilience, aging, and the search for meaning through physical challenge.
book-6713: In 1890s Paris, a French intelligence officer rises through the army just as Captain Alfred Dreyfus is publicly condemned for treason and sent to Devil’s Island. When Colonel Georges Picquart takes charge of the section that uncovered the supposed evidence, he begins to find forged documents, hidden files, and signs that the real spy remains at large. His duty to the army collides with loyalty to truth as senior officers, politicians, and newspapers work to preserve a false verdict. Set in barracks, ministries, courtrooms, and surveillance offices, the novel follows the machinery of the Dreyfus Affair through espionage methods, bureaucratic secrecy, and anti-Semitic hysteria. Themes include state power, conscience, institutional corruption, and the cost of resisting an official lie.
book-6714: An account of the 1879 U.S. Arctic expedition of the USS Jeannette follows naval officer George Washington De Long and his crew as they steam toward the North Pole under the mistaken theory of an open polar sea. Backed by newspaper owner James Gordon Bennett Jr., the ship enters the ice north of the Bering Strait and becomes locked in a drifting pack for months, turning exploration into a prolonged test of endurance. Drawing on journals, letters, and naval records, the narrative traces shipboard routine, extreme cold, hunger, illness, and the desperate retreat across sea ice and the Siberian coast. The book examines nineteenth-century polar science, imperial ambition, leadership under pressure, and the thin boundary between confidence and fatal miscalculation.
book-6715: A New York murder case returns to public attention when a condemned man nears execution and new violence suggests the wrong person may have been blamed. A television journalist, still marked by the killing of his wife years earlier, becomes entangled in a fresh abduction that places his young son in danger and draws police, reporters, and a grieving family back into the old crime. Moving through city streets, apartments, courtrooms, and hidden rooms, the story follows a predator who watches his victims and exploits panic, routine, and trust. The novel combines mystery and suspense with family drama and a thread of romance, focusing on wrongful conviction, trauma, parental fear, voyeurism, and the lingering power of an unresolved murder.
book-6716: Peter Hatcher tries to survive another round of family chaos when his younger brother Fudge becomes obsessed with money. A chance meeting with distant relatives introduces the Hatchers to another family with the same last name, including a toddler nicknamed Mini-Fudge, and the coincidence turns ordinary life into a series of noisy misunderstandings and competitive antics. Set in contemporary New York and suburban family spaces, the story follows Peter as he balances school, embarrassment, and his role as the sensible older brother while Fudge dreams up schemes involving cash, names, and status. The novel centers on sibling exasperation, extended-family surprises, and the comic disorder of childhood. Humor grows from strong personalities, domestic mishaps, and Peter’s efforts to keep his patience in a household that rarely stays calm.
book-6717: In the isolated college town of Morganville, Texas, teenager Claire Danvers and her housemates live under a tense arrangement between human residents and the vampires who rule the streets after dark. This omnibus gathers two installments in which that fragile order begins to collapse. A powerful outsider vampire arrives and challenges the town’s established leadership, drawing Claire, Shane, Eve, and Michael into struggles over loyalty, resistance, and survival. As violence spreads through dorms, coffee shops, labs, and hidden vampire strongholds, Claire’s scientific ingenuity and her friendships become crucial defenses. The narrative combines young adult paranormal horror with small-town siege fiction, focusing on coercion, chosen family, unequal power, and the cost of trying to protect ordinary life inside a community built on fear.
book-6718: Set between modern London and a lightly magical version of everyday life, this romantic comedy follows a young woman whose private wishes begin to come true in ways she never expects. What starts as a fantasy of a better job, a better man, or a better future turns into a series of unsettling coincidences that force her to examine what she actually wants. Office politics, dating disappointments, friendship strains, and family expectations shape the conflict as luck and desire collide. The novel combines contemporary romance with a fantasy premise, using charm, misunderstandings, and comic reversals to explore fate, self-knowledge, and the gap between imagined happiness and real emotional connection. Themes include wish fulfillment, consequences, personal change, and learning to value ordinary life.
book-6719: In contemporary Tucson, shaman-for-hire Eugenie Markham battles creatures from the Otherworld while trying to keep ordinary humans safe from hauntings, possessions, and predatory spirits. Her work takes a dangerous turn when a teenage girl is abducted into the kingdom of faerie, forcing Eugenie to cross a boundary she usually avoids and confront courts ruled by bargains, glamour, and violence. As she tracks the missing girl through rival supernatural factions, she becomes entangled with powerful men whose motives mix desire, politics, and manipulation. The novel combines urban fantasy investigation with dark romance, centering on uneasy alliances, the cost of power, sexual threat, and the tension between human autonomy and the seductive pull of the supernatural realm.
book-672: Stranded by snow on the famous Orient Express as it crosses Europe, Belgian detective Hercule Poirot faces a locked-room murder in a train carriage full of wealthy, secretive passengers. The victim is an American businessman with a violent past, and the suspects are confined together in the luxurious but claustrophobic compartments of the halted train. As Poirot interviews conductors, valets, governesses, and aristocrats, he uncovers disguises, conflicting alibis, and hidden connections that reach beyond the journey itself. The investigation turns on careful observation of luggage, uniforms, timetables, and small physical clues, while the novel examines justice, revenge, class performance, and the tension between legal truth and moral judgment.
book-6720: At Keyhouse in Lovecraft, Massachusetts, the Locke children continue to uncover doors and enchanted keys that alter memory, identity, and the body. This volume follows Bode, Tyler, and Kinsey as curiosity about the house’s hidden mechanisms collides with a growing danger moving behind familiar faces. School corridors, bedrooms, and the old mansion become sites of possession, secrecy, and transformation, while each newly used key reveals another piece of the house’s unsettling logic. The central conflict turns on who can control these artifacts and who understands the cost of opening the wrong door. Blending supernatural horror with dark fantasy, the story explores grief, childhood vulnerability, family distrust, and the seductive power of magic that promises escape while inviting invasion.
book-6721: Amid the mansions, opera boxes, and drawing rooms of 1900 Manhattan, a circle of privileged young women and men navigate love, ambition, and scandal under the scrutiny of New York society. As engagements shift and family expectations tighten, secrets about marriages, affairs, money, and social position threaten carefully managed reputations. The novel follows sisters, heiresses, and suitors whose personal desires collide with the rigid codes of the old-money elite and the opportunism of newcomers eager to rise. Romantic rivalry, jealousy, and public gossip drive the conflict, while Fifth Avenue luxury and Newport-style excess frame the drama. Themes of class, female constraint, performance, and the cost of social success shape this young adult historical romance set in America’s Gilded Age.
book-6722: Beyond the ruined enclaves of a future America, Deuce faces a widening war as the Freaks—mutated, hungry predators once dismissed as mindless monsters—gather in organized hordes and threaten every fragile settlement aboveground. After the journeys of Enclave and Outpost, she returns to a landscape of patched walls, scavenged weapons, and uneasy alliances, where human communities must decide whether to unite, flee, or sacrifice outsiders to survive. Alongside Fade, Tegan, Stalker, and other fighters, she confronts battles that test loyalty, leadership, and the cost of mercy. The novel combines post-apocalyptic survival, horror, and young adult adventure while exploring violence, belonging, prejudice, and the question of what still separates humans from the monsters at their gates.
book-6723: Through weekly emails sent to an online mailing list, an anonymous narrator chronicles the lives of four young women from affluent families in Riyadh as they move from university into adulthood. Gamrah, Sadeem, Michelle, and Lamees pursue love, marriage, and work while facing strict social codes governing gender, family honor, class, religion, and public reputation. Courtship unfolds through chaperoned visits, mobile phones, and secret meetings, and each woman confronts the gap between private desire and the demands of Saudi society. Set in early twenty-first-century Saudi Arabia, the novel uses gossip, confession, and social observation to examine female friendship, romantic disappointment, divorce, double standards, and the pressures placed on women to balance modern ambitions with conservative expectations.
book-6724: A small chameleon visits a zoo and becomes dissatisfied with its own plain body and quiet habits. As it watches polar bears, flamingos, foxes, fish, deer, and other animals, it imagines taking on their distinctive traits: white fur, pink wings, bushy tails, fins, and antlers. The fantasy grows into a comic problem, because the more parts it adds, the less it can move, climb, swim, or catch the fly it wants to eat. Set in a brightly observed animal world, the story introduces zoological features while following a simple emotional conflict about envy and self-acceptance. Themes of identity, appearance, and appreciating one’s natural abilities unfold through Eric Carle’s collage-style picture-book format and repeated animal imagery.
book-6725: Denver late-night radio becomes an unexpected battleground when Kitty Norville, a small-market DJ and secret werewolf, turns her overnight advice show into a forum for vampires, lycanthropes, and frightened callers. What begins as anonymous talk-radio therapy draws attention from hunters, police, tabloid media, and the dangerous pack politics that already control her private life. Within her werewolf community, an authoritarian alpha and a rigid hierarchy leave Kitty trapped between obedience and self-preservation. As public curiosity about the supernatural grows, she must navigate rival predators, human suspicion, and her own changing sense of power. Blending urban fantasy, horror, and romance, the novel centers on identity, consent, secrecy, and the cost of finding a voice in a violent hidden world.
book-6726: Set in northeastern China from the 1960s into the reform era, the novel follows Lin Kong, an army doctor trapped between an arranged village marriage and his long attachment to Manna Wu, a nurse at his military hospital. Each year he returns to Goose Village to seek a divorce from his silent, bound-footed wife, Shuyu, but custom, family pressure, and local law keep postponing his plans. As the years pass, desire hardens into habit, and the long wait reshapes all three lives. The story traces intimate choices under a rigid social order, showing how bureaucracy, duty, and public morality govern private feeling. Themes of time, obligation, loneliness, marriage, and the cost of compromise run through this portrait of love deferred in Communist China.
book-6727: Set in 1920s colonial Burma, the novel follows John Flory, a British timber merchant who feels repelled by the smug racism and emptiness of the small expatriate circle gathered around the local European Club. His only close ally is Dr. Veraswami, an Indian physician whose position is threatened by the scheming Burmese magistrate U Po Kyin, a master of bribery, rumor, and political manipulation. When the newly arrived Elizabeth Lackersteen enters this closed world, Flory imagines a possible escape from his loneliness, but his hopes collide with the rigid codes of empire. The story examines colonial power, social exclusion, corruption, class anxiety, and the moral compromises that sustain British rule, while portraying everyday life in a teak-trading outpost with heat, boredom, and resentment.
book-6728: Set in 12th-century France during the aftermath of the Crusades, this historical thriller follows Hugh de Luc, a village carpenter who returns from war to find his home burned, his wife murdered, and his son taken by a powerful lord. Forced into flight, he adopts the disguise of a jester, using wit, performance, and anonymity to move through castles, roads, and courts that would otherwise be closed to him. His search for his child becomes entangled with a larger struggle involving feudal violence, church power, and a rumored treasure linked to the crusading world. The novel combines revenge, pursuit, and survival with themes of class injustice, faith, deception, and the use of performance as both weapon and shield.
book-6729: A suburban Chicago family struggles to function after the accidental death of an older son and the suicide attempt of his younger brother, Conrad. Returning to high school after months in a psychiatric hospital, Conrad tries to manage panic, guilt, and social isolation while beginning therapy with a psychiatrist who pushes him to speak honestly about grief and anger. His father, Calvin, wants to hold the family together, but his mother, Beth, insists on control, order, and silence, deepening tensions inside the home. Moving between school, therapy sessions, and family life, the novel examines depression, survivor’s guilt, emotional repression, and the gap between public normalcy and private pain. Its central conflict lies in whether family members can confront loss directly or remain trapped by denial and expectation.
book-673: A transatlantic story of love, migration, and identity follows Ifemelu and Obinze, teenagers who fall in love in military-era Lagos and imagine a shared future beyond Nigeria’s political and economic instability. When Ifemelu leaves for the United States to study, distance, immigration barriers, and unequal opportunity reshape both lives. In American cities and on college campuses, she confronts race as a lived social category for the first time and turns her observations into a sharp blog about Blackness, class, hair, and cultural code-switching. Obinze, refused entry to America, navigates precarity and illegality in Britain before returning home. As their paths diverge and later circle back, the novel examines diaspora, return, intimacy, ambition, and the tension between self-invention and belonging.
book-6730: A teenage girl enters the online role-playing game Coarsegold Online to escape school routines and try on a new identity as a fierce warrior. In the game’s colorful fantasy world, she joins a guild, learns the rules of raids and status, and is drawn into a conflict over gold farming when she meets a poor player in China who sells virtual goods for real money. The story moves between suburban classrooms, chat windows, and sword-and-sorcery landscapes, linking dragons and quests to global labor, economic inequality, and the ethics of online play. Presented as a graphic novel, it examines friendship, empathy, internet culture, and the gap between game systems and the human lives affected by them.
book-6731: In contemporary New Orleans, a forbidden romance binds two shape-shifters from enemy clans. Fang Kattalakis, a wolf Were-Hunter scarred by family violence and pack politics, has long loved Aimee Peltier, a bear Katagaria whose powerful family distrusts wolves and guards its own secrets. Their bond draws retaliation from rival predators, ancient powers, and the rigid laws that divide Arcadian and Katagarian breeds. As disappearances, betrayal, and supernatural attacks close in, the couple must navigate blood feuds, loyalty to kin, and the threat of war within the Were-Hunter world. The novel combines paranormal romance with urban fantasy and horror elements, focusing on shapeshifter society, interspecies prejudice, inherited trauma, and the struggle to claim love in a violent, rule-bound supernatural underworld.
book-6732: Set in medieval England, this historical adventure follows the outlaw Robin Hood as he moves through Sherwood Forest with a band of archers, woodsmen, and dispossessed commoners. He lives beyond the reach of royal officers and feudal lords, turning ambush, disguise, and woodland skill into weapons against corrupt authority. The narrative centers on clashes with sheriffs, churchmen, and nobles who misuse law and taxation, while Robin protects travelers, aids the poor, and defends his companions through raids and rescues. Courtly loyalties, local justice, and resistance to tyranny shape the conflict as much as swordplay and pursuit. Themes of freedom, inequality, fellowship, and the tension between official power and moral right give the legend its enduring force.
book-6733: A teenage carrier of a parasite that produces the legends of vampirism moves through New York City tracking the women he has infected, each now transformed into a dangerous predator with heightened senses, violent hunger, and a link to rats and underground spaces. As he works with a secret public-health organization to contain outbreaks, he tries to protect an uninfected girl drawn into his hidden life. The novel frames horror through epidemiology, treating monsters as hosts, vectors, and symptoms rather than supernatural beings. Alternate chapters discuss real parasites and animal behavior, grounding the story’s vampire mythology in biology. Set in subways, tenements, and night streets, it explores contagion, desire, responsibility, urban ecology, and the uneasy boundary between science and folklore.
book-6734: Across the kingdoms of Annar, the young Bard Maerad travels with her mentor Cadvan after escaping slavery and discovering a powerful gift tied to ancient songs and prophecies. Hunted by the servants of the Nameless One, she moves through ruined schools, mountain passes, and hidden courts while trying to understand a riddle that may point toward the fate of Pellinor and the balance between light and dark. Their journey brings political suspicion, secret histories, and signs that the old powers are awakening. As Maerad learns more about her lineage and her dangerous abilities, the novel centers on exile, memory, language, and the burden of knowledge, combining quest fantasy, music-based magic, and a coming-of-age struggle against fear, isolation, and encroaching war.
book-6735: At a secret school for the Real World’s hunted and hunters, teenage Dru Anderson tries to survive training, prophecy, and the aftermath of becoming something more dangerous than human. Vampires, werewolves, and djamphir politics close in as the schola fractures into rival loyalties, and her power makes her both a weapon and a target. Christophe pushes her toward the role others expect her to fill, while Graves and the pack pull at older bonds of trust and affection. As attacks, disappearances, and suspicion spread through the cold halls and guarded forests, Dru must decide whom she can rely on and what kind of leader she is willing to become. The novel centers on jealousy, betrayal, supernatural hierarchy, and the cost of survival.
book-6736: Spanning early lyrics, sonnets, and later meditations, this collection gathers Dylan Thomas’s poems into a portrait of a twentieth-century poetic imagination shaped by Wales, the Bible, the sea, the body, and the cycle of birth and death. The poems move through village streets, chapels, farms, bedrooms, and shorelines, turning ordinary objects—fern, bone, fox, rain, coffin, child—into dense musical symbols. Central tensions arise between innocence and decay, erotic vitality and mortality, spiritual longing and physical appetite. Formal patterning, internal rhyme, and incantatory sound drive poems that often wrestle with time, memory, grief, and the persistence of life in the face of extinction. The volume presents both celebrated elegies and difficult visionary pieces, emphasizing language, image, and cadence as the core of meaning.
book-6737: In contemporary Baltimore, Kate Battista lives in the worn routines of a difficult household, working at a preschool while managing the needs of her absentminded scientist father and her charming younger sister, Bunny. Sharp-tongued, impatient, and uneasy with social expectations, she has little interest in romance or domestic performance. Her life shifts when her father proposes an outrageous solution to a practical problem: marriage to Pyotr, his brilliant laboratory assistant, whose visa is about to expire. What begins as a family scheme becomes a clash of temperament, class, and cultural misunderstanding. The novel follows negotiations among obligation, desire, and self-respect, while exploring immigrant precarity, family dependency, and the pressure placed on women to become agreeable, useful, and easy to love.
book-6738: Set in the Seven Kingdoms nearly a century before the events of A Song of Ice and Fire, this graphic novel follows Ser Duncan the Tall, a newly knighted hedge knight with little money, no patron, and only his armor, horse, and stubborn honor. After taking on a sharp-witted bald boy called Egg as his squire, Dunk rides to a great tourney at Ashford Meadow hoping to win food, coin, and recognition. The gathering of lords, knights, puppeteers, and Targaryen princes draws him into a dispute far larger than his station, where questions of chivalry, class, oathkeeping, and justice become dangerous. The story combines jousts, camp life, road travel, and court politics while examining what knighthood means for a poor man in a rigid feudal world.
book-6739: In the mountain town of Carnal, Colorado, a shy librarian steps out of the background and pursues the local lawman she has admired from afar. Their romance unfolds against a close-knit small-town setting of bookstores, cabins, bars, and snowy roads, where gossip travels fast and private histories are hard to hide. The deputy sheriff carries scars from dangerous police work and resists intimacy, while she brings patience, intelligence, and a fierce attachment to the life she has built. As their relationship deepens, an active criminal investigation and threats tied to his past draw them into escalating danger. The novel combines contemporary romance with police suspense, focusing on trust, trauma, desire, courage, and the tension between domestic belonging and violence at the edge of town.
book-674: A New York book editor is devastated when the man she expects to marry abruptly leaves her and sends her a handwritten diary instead of an explanation. As she reads, the diary recounts the life of Suzanne, a warm young mother, her courtship with Matt, and the early years of their son Nicholas in a small coastal community. The alternating story lines turn a romantic relationship into a mystery, as the editor searches the pages for the reason her future has collapsed. Domestic scenes of marriage and parenthood stand beside grief, secrecy, and emotional withholding. The novel centers on love, betrayal, memory, and the hidden histories that shape intimate relationships, using the diary form to reveal how one family’s private record changes another woman’s understanding of the man she loves.
book-6740: A murder investigation draws Edinburgh detective Fin Macleod back to the Isle of Lewis in Scotland’s Outer Hebrides, the austere landscape where he grew up and long ago tried to leave behind. Sent to look into the killing of a local man whose death resembles a case in the city, he finds a close-knit island community shaped by harsh weather, religious strictness, old loyalties, and buried resentments. As interviews reopen memories of schooldays, family loss, and a formative expedition to hunt guga on a remote sea stack, the case becomes entangled with his own history. The novel combines police procedural and literary suspense, using the peat bogs, blackhouses, and Atlantic cliffs to explore memory, masculinity, isolation, and the grip of place on identity.
book-6741: In Victorian England, spirited heiress Daisy Bowman faces an ultimatum from her wealthy American father: secure a suitable aristocratic husband within months or marry Matthew Swift, the capable employee she has always disliked. Daisy prefers novels, wit, and daydreams to the rigid calculations of the marriage market, and London drawing rooms offer little freedom from family pressure, class expectations, and gossip. When Matthew reenters her life, no longer the awkward young man she remembers, their forced courtship unsettles her assumptions about duty, desire, and social ambition. The novel follows a convenience-minded engagement that becomes emotionally complicated, blending ballroom comedy, family interference, and sensual romance while exploring money, status, female choice, and the tension between romantic fantasy and real partnership.
book-6742: A newly divorced prosecutor, Emily Graham returns to the New Jersey shore and buys a Victorian house in Spring Lake, a place shadowed by an old crime. More than a century earlier, a young heiress vanished from the same property on the night before her wedding, and her body was never found. As Emily settles into the house and researches the unsolved disappearance, a second threat emerges in the present: women in the town have been attacked, and Emily may fit the killer’s pattern. The novel combines domestic suspense, historical mystery, and a restrained romance, moving between seaside streets, old family secrets, and police investigation. Its central tension lies in the link between past and present violence, and in the danger of uncovering truths someone still wants buried.
book-6743: Seattle succubus Georgina Kincaid tries to balance her infernal job, her bookstore life, and a new relationship with bestselling novelist Seth Mortensen, a man she cannot safely touch without feeding on his life force. Their frustrating celibacy strains both romance and loyalty, while Georgina’s circle of vampires, demons, and angels keeps pulling her back into supernatural obligations. When a series of attacks begins targeting immortals in the city, she is drawn into an investigation that exposes rivalries, hidden motives, and the politics of the underworld. Urban fantasy, paranormal romance, and light horror elements combine in a contemporary Pacific Northwest setting, with themes of desire, self-control, identity, friendship, and the cost of intimacy for a creature whose very nature makes ordinary love dangerous.
book-6744: Across the Sword Coast and the frozen North of the Forgotten Realms, old companions and old enemies move toward a new reckoning. Drizzt Do’Urden and his allies in Mithral Hall still live with the loss of Wulfgar, while the barbarian himself wanders in spiritual ruin, marked by captivity and rage. At the same time, the assassin Artemis Entreri and the drow mercenary Jarlaxle become entangled with Khazid’hea, a sentient magical sword whose hunger for violence corrupts every hand that grips it. The novel follows intersecting journeys through pirate ports, dwarven strongholds, and wilderness roads, balancing sword-and-sorcery adventure with questions of trauma, temptation, loyalty, and whether identity survives suffering. Themes of grief, possession, redemption, and the cost of vengeance drive the conflict.
book-6745: A courtroom drama in a small Tennessee town stages a public battle over a schoolteacher accused of violating a law against teaching evolution. As reporters, preachers, politicians, and townspeople crowd into Hillsboro, two celebrated lawyers turn the trial into a national spectacle: one defends biblical literalism and social order, while the other argues for free inquiry, science, and intellectual liberty. The action moves between the courthouse, the town square, and private rooms where fear, ambition, and conscience shape public rhetoric. Although rooted in the 1925 Scopes “Monkey Trial,” the play uses that setting to examine censorship, religious fundamentalism, democratic debate, and the pressure a community exerts on dissenters. Themes of truth, tolerance, education, and the cost of independent thought drive the conflict.
book-6746: A drunken wager sends a British comedian onto the roads of Ireland with an unlikely companion: a full-size refrigerator. Framed as a comic travel memoir, the narrative follows his attempt to circumnavigate the island by hitchhiking while hauling the appliance from county to county. Along the way, ferries, pubs, farmyards, roadside lifts, and small towns become stages for encounters with drivers, locals, and fellow eccentrics who react to the absurd challenge with curiosity and generosity. The central tension lies in whether he can complete the journey under the terms of the bet, but the book’s real subject is the texture of travel powered by chance meetings. Themes include improvisation, hospitality, national identity, and the humor that emerges when ordinary landscapes are disrupted by a ridiculous object.
book-6747: In a post-apocalyptic world overrun by the undead, Annah survives in a ruined city of narrow alleys, towering buildings, and barricaded streets, working among strangers while searching for the twin sister she lost years earlier. When a violent attack breaches the fragile routines that keep the city alive, she is forced to flee with Elias, a soldier burdened by duty and memory. Their journey carries them through abandoned subways, forests, and settlements where every gate and watchtower testifies to fear of the unconsecrated. As Annah moves closer to the sister who may still be alive, the novel centers on survival, family bonds, guilt, love, and the question of whether any safe home can endure in a landscape shaped by infection, isolation, and relentless loss.
book-6748: A comic travel memoir follows a celebrity comedian through a series of chaotic trips, with a central focus on a vacation in Africa that goes spectacularly off course. Moving between safari lodges, airports, hotels, and holiday gatherings, the narrative presents missed connections, cultural misunderstandings, heavy drinking, unruly friends, and family episodes as material for anecdote rather than introspection. The voice stays first-hand and confessional, but the book’s subject is the performance of excess: tourism, privilege, embarrassment, friendship, and the logistics of moving a large personality through unfamiliar places. Uganda, Botswana, and other destinations appear less as guides than as backdrops for mishap and observation. Themes include travel as disorder, adult friendship, public persona, and the comic gap between planned adventure and actual experience.
book-6749: A warning about a dangerous box of chocolate opens this middle-grade fantasy mystery, sending Cass and Max-Ernest into another puzzle tied to the Terces Society and the search for immortality. Set in a contemporary world where secret museums, coded messages, and hidden laboratories exist just out of sight, the story follows the friends as they investigate the Midnight Sun, a sinister spa and clinic whose elegant surfaces conceal alarming experiments. Their central challenge is to rescue a loved one while deciphering clues left by alchemists and confronting adults who manipulate desire, beauty, and appetite. Blending suspense, comic narration, and metafictional asides, the novel explores friendship, trust, temptation, and the cost of trying to preserve youth forever.
book-675: A secret government experiment leaves young Charlie McGee with a terrifying gift: she can ignite fires with her mind. After agents from a covert intelligence unit known as the Shop target her, Charlie and her father, Andy, flee across America, using Andy’s own chemically induced psychic power to evade capture. The pursuit turns into a violent cat-and-mouse struggle as the agency seeks to imprison Charlie and turn her ability into a weapon. Set in motels, back roads, laboratories, and safe houses, the novel combines paranoid thriller suspense with horror and science fiction. Its central conflict pits a vulnerable child and her family against state surveillance, scientific abuse, and the destructive force of power that cannot be easily controlled.
book-6750: A collection of essays examines American pop culture, media habits, sports, technology, celebrity, and consumer life through a mix of reporting, criticism, memoir, and comic speculation. The pieces move from ABBA fandom and football analysis to time travel thought experiments, reality television, airports, and the changing meaning of authenticity in a digital age. Rather than building a single narrative, the book studies how ordinary entertainment artifacts shape belief, identity, and public conversation. Its central argument asks why people care so intensely about cultural products that seem trivial and what those attachments reveal about memory, status, taste, and modern capitalism. Throughout, the prose treats magazines, songs, games, gadgets, and historical myths as evidence in a broader inquiry into nostalgia, attention, and the logic of contemporary American life.
book-6751: Two foundational American political documents set out the principles, structure, and tensions of the United States at its beginning. The Declaration of Independence presents a formal break from British rule, arguing that legitimate government rests on natural rights, popular consent, and the people’s authority to resist tyranny; it also lists grievances against King George III and frames independence as a public justification. The Constitution of the United States then establishes the national framework that follows, defining the powers of Congress, the presidency, and the federal judiciary, along with relations between federal and state authority and procedures for amendment. Read together, they address liberty, representation, law, sovereignty, and the practical problem of turning revolutionary ideals into a durable republican government.
book-6752: Framed as a dictated memoir to Spanish clerics after the conquest of Mexico, the novel follows Mixtli, an aging Aztec man, as he recounts a life spent moving through the cities, markets, temples, and battlefields of the Mexica world before Hernán Cortés arrives. His narrative traces childhood hardship, apprenticeship, trade journeys, court intrigue, warfare, sexuality, and religious ritual across Tenochtitlan and neighboring regions. The central tension lies between individual survival and the demands of a rigid imperial society shaped by class, priesthood, sacrifice, and political ambition. Through Mixtli’s voice, the story presents daily life in the Aztec empire in concrete detail, while the Spanish listeners’ presence underscores cultural collision, memory, conquest, and the loss of a civilization.
book-6753: Childhood friendship links two outsiders whose paths split between magic and technology in a near-future world sliding toward environmental collapse. Patricia grows into a witch trained in secret arts, speaking with birds and moving through hidden networks of spellwork, while Laurence becomes a brilliant engineer devoted to machines, inventions, and rational systems. Reunited as adults in San Francisco, they are pulled into rival communities that treat science and sorcery as incompatible answers to a planet in crisis. Their personal bond collides with larger struggles over power, responsibility, and survival as strange weather, social breakdown, and speculative devices reshape everyday life. The novel combines coming-of-age elements with speculative worldbuilding to examine friendship, loneliness, climate anxiety, and the uneasy border between wonder and control.
book-6754: A streetwise sewer tosher in Victorian London earns a hard living scavenging the city’s storm drains until he rescues a badly beaten young woman from two violent pursuers. The act pulls him out of the underworld of mud, alleys, and slaughterhouses and into drawing rooms, court intrigue, and the attention of figures such as Charles Dickens and Benjamin Disraeli. As Dodger tries to protect Simplicity and uncover why powerful men want her silenced, he moves between rich and poor districts where class privilege, crime, and politics meet. Set in a foggy, crowded capital of markets, sewers, and rookeries, the novel combines adventure and comedy with themes of social mobility, identity, justice, and the hidden machinery of nineteenth-century London.
book-6755: After surviving alone in the Canadian wilderness, Brian Robeson is asked to return as part of a government project testing survival methods for pilots and astronauts. He enters the forest with psychologist Derek Holt, expecting a controlled experiment in the same lakes-and-timber country where he once lived off fish, fire, and a hatchet. When a lightning strike leaves Derek unconscious, the plan collapses and Brian must improvise a rescue. He builds a raft, follows a dangerous river, and faces rapids, weather, hunger, and isolation while trying to keep another person alive. Set in remote northern woods, the novel centers on practical wilderness skills, endurance, and quick judgment, and it explores self-reliance, trauma, and the fragile line between preparation and disaster.
book-6756: In a nineteenth-century Transylvanian setting, five sisters keep their family manor and merchant business running while their father travels south for his health. Their refuge lies in the nearby Wildwood, where a hidden portal opens on full-moon nights into the Other Kingdom, a realm of dancing halls, enchanted creatures, and dangerous bargains. Practical Jena, the second sister, tries to protect both her siblings and the secret of the forest when their arrogant cousin Cezar arrives to control the household and press for an advantageous marriage. As winter closes in, the sisters face shifting loyalties, old family expectations, and the perilous attraction of the supernatural world. The novel combines fairy-tale motifs, household responsibility, romance, and questions of freedom, trust, and power.
book-6757: A contemporary family-centered romance unfolds around a woman whose carefully managed life is disrupted when someone from her past returns, forcing old wounds and unfinished bonds back into the center of her home. Set in an intimate domestic world shaped by children, marriage, and everyday responsibilities, the novel follows the emotional strain between loyalty to the life she has built and the pull of love that never fully disappeared. As parents and children adjust to a changed household, the story examines reconciliation, trust, memory, and the difficult work of forgiveness. The conflict is less about external adventure than about private choices inside kitchens, bedrooms, and family gatherings, where questions of belonging, responsibility, and second chances become impossible to ignore.
book-6758: A sequence of horror stories unfolds through haunted apartments, desolate streets, train compartments, and ordinary English rooms where the supernatural breaks into daily life. The volume opens with a framing tale about a fraudulent medium who becomes a living manuscript for the dead, establishing a world in which ghosts, occult forces, and bodily terror demand witness. Across the collection, killers, revenants, and monstrous presences emerge not from distant castles but from urban spaces and familiar domestic settings. The central tension lies between skeptical modern life and eruptions of violence, desire, and the uncanny that refuse explanation. Themes include the porous boundary between flesh and spirit, punishment, voyeurism, sexual fear, and the hidden savagery beneath routine social order.
book-6759: Set in a world where angels, fallen powers, and human loyalties collide, this paranormal fantasy follows Evie as her bond with the enigmatic Reed grows more dangerous and more intimate. Forces from Heaven and Hell press in around her, turning desire, prophecy, and duty into a single conflict. As hidden histories surface and supernatural factions maneuver for control, Evie must decide whom to trust and what she is willing to sacrifice for love and survival. The novel combines romance with horror-inflected menace, using visions, ancient debts, and violent confrontations to explore fate, free will, temptation, and redemption. Its central tension rests on whether personal devotion can endure when destiny seems already written and every choice carries consequences for both the mortal world and the realms beyond it.
book-676: In contemporary New York, Eva Tramell and Gideon Cross try to build a relationship shaped by intense desire, wealth, and the lingering damage of past abuse. Their bond deepens as they confront jealousy, secrecy, and the controlling habits that make trust difficult. Around them, family tensions, media scrutiny, former lovers, and a dangerous stalker keep private wounds in public view. The novel combines erotic romance with suspense, following two protagonists who are powerfully attached yet still divided by trauma, anger, and fear of abandonment. Corporate privilege, luxury apartments, therapy sessions, nightclubs, and security details form the setting for a story focused on consent, emotional recovery, possessiveness, and the effort to create intimacy without surrendering autonomy.
book-6760: Set in the tense weeks before the First World War, this historical thriller moves between imperial Russia and aristocratic London as British and Russian leaders negotiate a secret military alliance. Their talks are threatened by a ruthless Russian revolutionary known as the man from St. Petersburg, an assassin driven by political fanaticism and a private grievance. At the center stands a British noble family whose marriage plans, social obligations, and hidden past become entangled with diplomacy, espionage, and murder. Drawing on court politics, class privilege, police pursuit, and underground radicalism, the novel examines how personal betrayal intersects with international crisis. Themes of revenge, loyalty, political violence, and the fragility of peace shape a suspense plot built around a looming war and a single killer’s mission.
book-6761: After a tabloid scandal and the collapse of her glamorous career, Margo Sullivan arrives at the Templeton estate in rural Maryland with little money and nowhere else to go. Raised there alongside her friends Kate Powell and Laura Templeton, she takes refuge with the family who once employed her mother and begins rebuilding her life through a small boutique business. The central conflict develops as Margo struggles to exchange luxury and performance for work, self-respect, and independence, while her long, uneasy attraction to Josh Templeton turns homecoming into a romance shaped by old class boundaries and intimate history. Beneath the contemporary love story, the novel introduces the trilogy’s thread of old legend, hidden inheritance, and female friendship, with themes of reinvention, loyalty, and desire tested against pride and vulnerability.
book-6762: In a near-future New York City shaped by surveillance, wealth, and urban violence, homicide lieutenant Eve Dallas investigates a series of killings that look less like ordinary murder than calculated punishment. The victims are men whose private histories suggest brutal crimes against women and children, pushing the case into the uneasy territory between legal justice and personal vengeance. As Eve follows forensic traces, courtroom connections, and hidden networks of power, she faces a killer who believes murder can correct the failures of the system. Alongside the police procedural, the novel develops Eve’s marriage to Roarke, whose resources and emotional support complicate her fierce independence. The story combines detective work, suspense, and romance while examining trauma, retribution, corruption, and the limits of institutional law.
book-6763: A homicide at an elite New York school draws Lieutenant Eve Dallas into a case that begins with a respected teacher collapsing in his classroom after drinking hot chocolate. Set in a near-future Manhattan of police procedure, advanced technology, and entrenched privilege, the investigation moves through private academies, wealthy families, and old grievances as Eve and her team search for the poisoner. The inquiry tests assumptions about innocence, because students, parents, faculty members, and former lovers all carry secrets that complicate the victim’s polished reputation. Alongside the murder case, Eve’s marriage to Roarke provides an intimate counterpoint, grounding the novel’s blend of detective fiction, suspense, and romance. Themes include betrayal, hidden identities, class power, and the corruption concealed behind respectable institutions.
book-6764: Amanda Knox recounts the years surrounding the 2007 murder investigation in Perugia, Italy, where she studies abroad and becomes the focus of an international criminal case after her roommate Meredith Kercher is killed. The memoir follows police interrogations, arrest, imprisonment, trial, and appeals, while also tracing her earlier life in Seattle and the disorienting shift from student travel to confinement. It presents her account of the Italian justice system, tabloid scrutiny, language barriers, and the pressure of being publicly cast as either victim or villain. Family loyalty, media spectacle, memory, and the struggle to preserve identity under accusation form the central themes, as the narrative examines how crime reporting, courtroom procedure, and national stereotypes shape a contested story.
book-6765: In a comic fairy-tale kingdom of forests, towers, and court politics, a lonely boy named Christian grows up in the care of a reclusive troll inventor and watches Princess Marigold from a hidden window in the woods. Their secret connection deepens when Christian’s unusual mechanical skills and Marigold’s frustration with royal expectations draw them together. Around them, the palace is shaped by matchmaking schemes, family secrets, and a queen determined to control the future of the crown. The story follows mistaken identities, eccentric inventions, and a romance threatened by class divisions and hidden pasts. Themes of belonging, adoption, appearance, and the difference between social rank and personal worth run through this light fantasy for younger readers.
book-6766: Set in medieval Scotland and England, this historical romance follows an arranged marriage forged to settle clan politics and satisfy a king’s command. A Highland laird takes an English-raised bride whose sharp tongue, independence, and hidden vulnerability unsettle his expectations of obedience. As she travels into the rugged world of castles, feuds, and loyalty oaths, husband and wife must navigate mistrust between families, old threats, and the clash between courtly upbringing and Highland custom. The novel centers on the slow movement from duty to desire, with scenes of domestic negotiation, protective rivalry, and comic misunderstandings. Themes include marriage as alliance, the making of trust, female resilience, clan honor, and the tension between political obligation and private love.
book-6767: In 1950s rural England, eleven-year-old sleuth and chemist Flavia de Luce returns to Buckshaw expecting a solemn homecoming for her long-lost mother, Harriet, whose remains are said to be arriving by train. Instead, a dying stranger presses a cryptic message into Flavia’s hands, and the family’s grief opens into a deeper puzzle. As she investigates railway secrets, hidden identities, and old wartime loyalties, Flavia uncovers tensions within the de Luce household and glimpses a network of espionage and deception that reaches beyond the village of Bishop’s Lacey. The mystery turns on family history, concealed motives, and the gap between public mourning and private truth. Themes of loss, memory, intelligence, and belonging run through this historical detective novel.
book-6768: Set largely at sea and in the colonial Congo at the end of the nineteenth century, these two Joseph Conrad novellas examine authority, isolation, and the unstable boundaries of the self. In Heart of Darkness, sailor Charles Marlow travels up the Congo River to find the ivory agent Kurtz, and his journey through trading stations, jungle, and brutal imperial violence becomes an inquiry into conquest, greed, and moral collapse. In The Secret Sharer, a young ship captain secretly shelters a fugitive swimmer aboard his vessel while trying to command an unfamiliar crew, turning the ship into a tense chamber of divided conscience. Together the stories focus on seafaring discipline, colonial power, guilt, and the darkness that lies beneath civilized appearances.
book-6769: A weathered library copy of V. M. Straka’s novel Ship of Theseus frames a second story told through handwritten notes, postcards, maps, and inserted documents left by two readers. On the page, an amnesiac man is shanghaied onto a black ship and drawn into a shadowy struggle involving a ruthless captain, secret ports, and questions of identity and fate. In the margins, graduate student Jen and disgraced scholar Eric piece together clues about Straka’s hidden life, disputed authorship, and possible political conspiracies while danger presses into their own lives. Set between a dark, allegorical seafaring fantasy and contemporary archival mystery, the book explores interpretation, censorship, translation, memory, and the unstable boundary between reader and text.
book-677: An inquiry into distance running follows journalist Christopher McDougall from injury and frustration into the Copper Canyons of Mexico, where the reclusive Tarahumara, or Rarámuri, run extraordinary ultramarathon distances across cliffs, desert trails, and remote canyons. Blending travel narrative, reportage, memoir, and popular science, the book examines barefoot running, modern athletic footwear, human evolution, and the physiology of endurance. McDougall traces a network of coaches, scientists, and eccentric ultrarunners as they prepare for a little-known race in rugged terrain, asking why so many modern runners get hurt and whether people are biologically built to run long distances. Themes include resilience, competition, industrial influence on sport, and the contrast between commercial fitness culture and older communal traditions of movement.
book-6770: Set in Montreal’s downtown streets and shabby apartments, this novel follows Baby, a sharp, observant twelve-year-old growing up with her affectionate but unreliable father, Jules, a heroin addict who drifts between brief recoveries and collapse. As Baby moves through foster homes, hospitals, welfare hotels, and a city alive with artists, dealers, and runaways, she learns to read danger, hunger, glamour, and loneliness with unsettling precision. The central conflict lies in her effort to protect a child’s need for love and wonder while navigating neglect, poverty, and exploitation. Told in a voice that mixes dark humor with bruised lyricism, the story examines survival, innocence, addiction, urban childhood, and the fragile bonds between parent and child.
book-6771: A modern fairy-tale fantasy follows Mina Grime, a teenage descendant of the Brothers Grimm, as she confronts another wave of dangerous story curses. After surviving earlier trials, she hopes for an ordinary life, but the pull of the tales returns when a Snow White pattern begins to surface around her. Set in a contemporary world where enchanted forests, mirrors, poisoned plots, and Grimm family secrets intrude on school and home, the story centers on Mina’s struggle to protect the people she loves while untangling who can be trusted. Romance, rivalry, and lurking supernatural threats complicate her choices as she faces a curse that feeds on vanity, jealousy, and deception. Themes include fate versus free will, family legacy, sacrifice, and the dark underside of familiar fairy tales.
book-6772: مجموعة من الرباعيات الشعرية المنسوبة إلى عمر الخيام تتأمل الوجود الإنساني من خلال صور الخمر، والحديقة، والليل، والكأس، ودورة الفصول. تدور القصائد في فضاء فارسي تأملي يجاور فيه مجلس الشراب أسئلة المصير، فيصبح المشهد اليومي مدخلاً إلى التفكير في الزمن، والموت، والقدر، وتقلب الحظ، وحدود المعرفة الدينية والفلسفية. لا تقوم على حبكة روائية، بل على صوت شعري يواجه تعارضاً مركزياً بين رغبة الإنسان في اليقين وإقامته داخل عالم عابر لا يكشف أسراره. تعالج الرباعيات الشك، واللذة، وفناء الجسد، وعبث الطموح، كما تختبر معنى التوبة والإيمان والتمرد في أبيات قصيرة مكثفة. ويرتبط اسما محمدعلي فروغي وقاسم غني بالتحقيق والضبط النصي لهذه الصيغة المتداولة من الديوان.
book-6773: In a future society shaped by genetic engineering, pollution, and a virus that kills women at twenty and men at twenty-five, Rhine Ellery leaves captivity and returns to Manhattan in search of her twin brother and a possible cure. The city’s ruined neighborhoods, laboratories, and privileged households reveal how deeply wealth, medicine, and power are entangled. As she moves through a world of forced marriages, scientific secrecy, and social collapse, she must decide whom to trust among family, former captors, and allies who want different futures. The novel combines dystopian survival, romance, and political conflict while focusing on bodily autonomy, grief, class inequality, and the cost of hope in a culture built on treating girls as resources rather than people.
book-6774: Albuquerque private investigator and grim reaper Charley Davidson juggles missing-person work, ghostly clients, and a dangerous connection to Reyes Farrow, the supernatural convict who can appear in dreams, doorways, and locked rooms. While she tries to keep her detective business functioning, dead strangers continue to demand her help, and living people around her are pulled into threats that mix crime, magic, and revenge. The central tension comes from Charley’s attempt to maintain control of her powers and her personal boundaries while Reyes presses closer with motives she cannot fully trust. Set in a contemporary Southwestern city of alleys, bars, police stations, and haunted apartments, the novel blends paranormal investigation, black humor, sexual tension, and questions of fate, free will, mortality, and loyalty.
book-6775: Six Los Angeles teenagers from wealthy but distant families gather for their parents’ regular meetings and accidentally witness a human sacrifice, learning that the adults belong to a criminal cabal called the Pride. Alex, Nico, Karolina, Molly, Chase, and Gertrude flee together, forced to survive without the homes and privileges they once took for granted. As they hide in mansions, hostels, and city streets, each teen discovers unusual abilities, inherited technology, or family secrets that tie them to the conspiracy. The story follows their shift from suspicious acquaintances to reluctant allies while they decide whether loyalty to blood matters when parents are murderers. Set in the Marvel Universe but grounded in adolescent conflict, it explores betrayal, identity, friendship, and the fear of becoming what one’s family expects.
book-6776: Set in the world of Krynn during the ancient Cataclysm era, this fantasy novel follows Huma, a young Knight of Solamnia, as he rises from obscure soldier to central champion in the war against the Dark Queen. As dragons return to the skies and armies gather under evil banners, Huma struggles with the rigid codes of knighthood, the demands of honor, and the cost of loyalty. His path crosses with a silver dragon in human form, linking personal devotion to a larger battle over the fate of Ansalon. The story centers on warfare, chivalry, prophecy, and sacrifice, while exploring how courage and moral conviction endure amid political division, magical power, and the overwhelming threat of Takhisis and her dragon host.
book-6777: After his wife dies in a fall from a tree behind their house, a linguistics professor is left with grief, unanswered questions, and the one witness who cannot explain what happened: the family dog, Lorelei. Convinced that the dog saw the accident and may hold the key to his wife’s final hours, he turns to animal language, speech theory, and memory in an increasingly obsessive attempt to make her communicate. Set in contemporary domestic and academic spaces, the novel combines psychological mystery with literary suspense as it traces a marriage, private sorrow, and the limits of interpretation. Themes of mourning, secrecy, intimacy, and the human desire to force meaning from silence shape a story about love and the unknowable interior lives of both people and animals.
book-6778: At a boarding school in Paris, the smallest and boldest of twelve girls watches a troubling new neighbor arrive next door. Pepito, the son of the Spanish ambassador, delights in mischief: he breaks windows, torments animals, and terrifies passersby while Miss Clavel and the girls look on with dismay. Madeline refuses to be intimidated, and the story follows the clash between her steady courage and Pepito’s reckless behavior. Set among city streets, embassy gardens, and the familiar orderly life of the school, the narrative explores childhood defiance, discipline, and the possibility of change. When danger strikes, bravado gives way to action, and the book turns from comic nuisance to a lesson about empathy, responsibility, and earning forgiveness.
book-6779: Inside the Pendleton, a grand apartment building at 77 Shadow Street, wealthy residents expect polished marble, private security, and old-world prestige, but the halls begin to produce impossible sounds, shifting rooms, and glimpses of violence from other times. As elevators fail, cameras reveal inexplicable figures, and entire apartments seem to change shape, neighbors who barely know one another are forced into an uneasy alliance. The novel blends haunted-house horror with technological paranoia and science-fiction menace, treating the building itself as the central mystery. Its conflict turns on whether the Pendleton is merely cursed or part of a larger experiment or invasion, while themes of isolation, class privilege, surveillance, memory, and survival run through the escalating terror.
book-678: On Alice Island, a small New England community shaped by ferries, winter weather, and local gossip, widowed bookstore owner A.J. Fikry lives in deep grief after his wife’s death. His isolation hardens when a valuable first edition is stolen, threatening both his finances and his sense of purpose. An unexpected child left in his shop interrupts that closed-off life and gradually draws him into new bonds with a police officer, a publishing sales representative, and the town around him. The novel follows daily life in an independent bookstore while weaving in a modest mystery about loss and chance. It explores bereavement, parenthood, reading, and the ways books, routine, and human attachment can rebuild a life that seems to have narrowed beyond repair.
book-6780: Arthur Penhaligon returns to the House, a vast bureaucratic universe built from the Will of the Architect, and is drawn into the domain of Sir Thursday, a severe commander who controls part of the Fourth Key. When the House slides toward war, Arthur is conscripted into the Glorious Army and sent into the grim machinery of military camps, marching orders, and battle plans. At the same time, his position in the Secondary Realms and his fragile life on Earth remain under threat from the growing corruption released into both worlds. The story follows his struggle to recover another Key and survive a system that treats children and soldiers as expendable pieces. Themes include authority, obedience, identity, and the human cost of war within an elaborate secondary-world fantasy setting.
book-6781: Modern physics becomes a guide to cosmology as the narrative surveys parallel-universe theories, extra dimensions, and the possible fate of the cosmos. Drawing on quantum mechanics, inflationary cosmology, string theory, and black hole research, it explains how scientists argue for multiple universes beyond ordinary observation and how higher-dimensional space might unify the forces of nature. The discussion moves from the Big Bang and dark energy to wormholes, time travel, and the long-term future of intelligent life in an expanding universe. Rather than presenting fantasy, it traces the central scientific debates, the mathematical ideas behind them, and the tension between speculation and testable evidence. Major themes include creation, the structure of space-time, the limits of human knowledge, and the search for a final theory of reality.
book-6782: Using the biblical story of David and Goliath as its framework, this Christian self-help guide examines the “giants” that dominate ordinary life: fear, anger, guilt, loneliness, temptation, and financial pressure. It retells scenes from 1 Samuel in accessible language and links David’s conflict with modern situations faced in homes, workplaces, and churches. The central argument holds that personal battles are not won by size, status, or self-reliance, but by faith in God’s presence and power. Practical reflections, scripture-based lessons, and devotional applications encourage readers to identify the forces that intimidate them and respond with courage, prayer, and trust. Themes include spiritual resilience, dependence on God, emotional struggle, and the possibility of hope when daily problems feel overwhelming.
book-6783: After learning that she is mystically bound to a vampire, teenage Alice Bonham is pulled deeper into the secret world of Jack, Peter, and their undead family. Set between suburban normality and hidden vampire enclaves, the novel follows her struggle to understand a bond that feels more like coercion than romance. Jack insists that fate has chosen Alice for him, while Peter offers a gentler connection that complicates loyalty, desire, and danger. As Alice spends more time among immortals, she faces threats from rival vampires and from the possessiveness inside Jack’s household. The story centers on predestination versus free will, obsessive love, jealousy, and the cost of entering a violent supernatural community while still trying to hold on to an ordinary human life.
book-6784: Drawing on decades of work as a midwife, this childbirth guide presents labor and delivery as a physiological process shaped by the body, the mind, and the birth environment.
