The case points toward a hidden network of current and former officers who profit from bribery, intimidation, and murder, forcing Eve to confront corruption inside the institution she serves. As she follows financial records, witness statements, and covert connections, the inquiry tests loyalties within the NYPSD and raises questions about justice, honor, and abuse of authority. Alongside the procedural drive, her marriage to Roarke and her partnerships with Detective Peabody and other colleagues provide emotional counterweight, grounding the novel’s blend of police thriller, crime investigation, and ongoing romantic suspense.
book-7133: Set in the late nineteenth century, this historical novel follows Fanny Van de Grift Osbourne and Robert Louis Stevenson from their first meeting in France through marriage, illness, literary work, and far-ranging travel. The narrative moves between California, Scotland, England, the Adirondacks, and the South Pacific, tracing a partnership shaped by age difference, family strain, artistic ambition, and chronic poor health. As Stevenson pursues writing and fame, Fanny balances devotion, independence, jealousy, and the practical labor of sustaining a household and a career in motion. Their journeys by ship, rail, and carriage place private conflict against a backdrop of bohemian circles, colonial routes, and changing ideas about marriage. Themes include creativity, exile, desire, loyalty, and the costs of building a life around art and adventure.
book-7134: Ancient werewolf clans, dangerous magic, and teenage loyalties drive this young adult paranormal romance set between small-town America and the hidden world of the Romanian Canis lupis. Jen, a sharp-tongued human drawn into the Grey Wolves’ pack, faces the consequences of her bond with Decebel, a powerful beta wolf whose devotion collides with prophecy, rival packs, and political unrest. As enemies circle and supernatural threats intensify, the story follows struggles over trust, sacrifice, and the cost of belonging to a world ruled by dominant alphas, fae influence, and blood-bound mates. Horror elements come through violent attacks and predatory creatures, while the central conflict turns on whether love and friendship can survive ancient laws, pack duty, and the escalating danger surrounding those marked by fate.
book-7135: A restless young man comes of age in Depression-era Chicago, moving through cramped apartments, city streets, boardinghouses, and a succession of odd jobs, schemes, and mentors. Augie March narrates his own education as he is pulled by family duty, class pressures, romantic entanglements, and the forceful ambitions of other people who try to shape his future. The novel follows a picaresque series of encounters rather than a single fixed path, tracing his movement from urban poverty into wider American and international settings. Its central tension lies in Augie’s refusal to be fully claimed by any ideology, profession, or patron. Themes of identity, freedom, ambition, Jewish American life, social mobility, and the improvisational energy of mid-20th-century America run throughout.
book-7136: After a violent confrontation leaves a man dead, a young woman turns to Carter Reed, the one person she knows with the power to make the problem disappear. He lives in a hidden world of organized crime, old loyalties, and retaliatory violence, and his protection binds her to him in ways neither of them can keep distant. As police scrutiny, gang rivalries, and buried history close in, the story moves through apartments, nightclubs, safe houses, and criminal back channels where trust is scarce and every favor has a cost. The novel combines romantic suspense with crime thriller elements, centering on fear, survival, possession, secrecy, and the pull between ordinary life and a ruthless underworld that refuses to stay separate.
book-7137: A London television writer in his thirties sees his orderly adult life collapse when his marriage breaks apart and he becomes the main carer for his young son. As Harry Silver tries to manage school runs, office politics, money, and dating, the novel follows the daily strain of single fatherhood in a city shaped by work pressure and changing ideas of masculinity. His central conflict lies in learning how to be a dependable parent while grieving lost romance and shedding the selfish habits of youth. Mixing domestic comedy with emotional realism, the story examines divorce, father-son bonds, male friendship, infidelity, and the uneasy passage from carefree manhood into responsible adulthood. It presents contemporary family life through scenes of bedrooms, kitchens, nurseries, and television studios.
book-7138: Told as the imagined autobiography of Cleopatra VII, the novel follows the last queen of Egypt from her youth in Alexandria through dynastic struggle, political exile, and her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony. It places court intrigue, Roman expansion, and the religious life of Ptolemaic Egypt at the center of the narrative, using palaces, libraries, temples, and battle camps as its settings. Cleopatra presents herself as a ruler trained in languages, statecraft, and ritual, confronting rival siblings, Roman generals, and the steady erosion of Egyptian independence. The central conflict lies between personal desire and political necessity, as diplomacy, seduction, and war become tools of survival. Themes include female power, empire, legitimacy, cultural identity, and the costs of preserving a kingdom under foreign pressure.
book-7139: Former Justice Department operative Cotton Malone is drawn into a violent hunt for a secret tied to Thomas Jefferson, the early republic, and a long-buried struggle over presidential power and national security. Moving between Washington, D.C., historic American sites, and a widening conspiracy, the story follows Malone as he investigates coded documents, rival operatives, and a hidden mechanism of authority that powerful figures want to control. The plot combines contemporary espionage with historical puzzles, using Jefferson’s papers, constitutional disputes, and private networks of influence to drive the mystery. Central conflicts pit public law against covert action, scholarship against political manipulation, and personal loyalty against state secrecy, while themes of history’s unfinished business and the misuse of executive power shape the suspense.
book-714: An aging British king decides to divide his realm among his three daughters according to how eloquently they declare their love, setting off a struggle over power, inheritance, and loyalty. When Lear misjudges honesty as disloyalty and banishes the child who speaks plainly, the kingdom fractures into rival households, military conflict, and bitter family betrayal. Running beside the royal plot, the Earl of Gloucester is deceived by one son and alienated from another, creating a second drama of blindness, authority, and filial duty. Set in a harsh landscape of courts, castles, and storm-beaten heath, the play examines madness, justice, cruelty, old age, and the collapse of political order. Shakespeare presents a tragedy in verse and prose where private vanity and public rule become fatally entangled.
book-7140: Set between contemporary Winnipeg, small-town Manitoba, and clinics and apartments marked by memory, this novel follows two adult sisters whose bond is strained by one sister’s repeated desire to die. Yolandi, a divorced writer and mother, narrates with dark humor and practical worry as she tries to keep Elfrieda alive. Elf is a world-renowned pianist, brilliant, restless, and increasingly unreachable despite professional success and a loving family. Their Mennonite upbringing, family history of depression and suicide, and the aftershocks of childhood trauma shape every conversation. As hospital stays, travel, and family interventions accumulate, the story examines mental illness, caregiving, grief, sisterhood, and the moral conflict between preserving a life and honoring another person’s wish for release.
book-7141: Set during a humid New England summer, the novel follows Mabel Dagmar, a reserved scholarship student at an elite college, after charismatic classmate Genevra Winslow invites her to the family’s secluded Vermont estate. Amid old money, lakeside rituals, and the decaying grandeur of Bittersweet, Mabel is drawn into the rhythms of an aristocratic clan that seems to offer beauty, intimacy, and belonging. The invitation also exposes rigid class boundaries, shifting female friendships, romantic desire, and the subtle power games that govern the household. As Mabel becomes entangled in the Winslows’ history, she begins to sense buried tensions and long-kept secrets surrounding the estate and Genevra’s family. The story combines campus and country-house mystery with psychological suspense, focusing on envy, privilege, reinvention, and the cost of wanting entry into another world.
book-7142: Quantum theory emerges here as both a scientific framework and a challenge to ordinary ideas about reality. The narrative traces the development of modern physics from early atomic theory and relativity into the strange domain of subatomic particles, where wave-particle duality, uncertainty, superposition, and measurement upset common sense. Using the famous Schrödinger’s cat thought experiment as a guide, the book examines how physicists describe electrons, photons, and probability, and why observation seems entangled with physical events. It also places key figures and experiments in historical context, showing how debates over causality, determinism, and the nature of matter reshape twentieth-century science. Themes include the limits of knowledge, the meaning of scientific models, and the philosophical consequences of quantum mechanics.
book-7143: In a remote keep in the Romanian Alps during the Second World War, a German army unit occupies an ancient stone fortress and begins to die in brutal, inexplicable ways. As officers search for a saboteur, local villagers whisper about a presence sealed inside the walls and the old bargain that once kept it contained. The mystery draws in a Jewish scholar with expertise in folklore and history, while a stranger arrives with his own knowledge of the evil awakening there. Set between Nazi occupation and older Balkan legends, the novel combines wartime suspense with supernatural horror. Its central conflict pits human violence, skepticism, and ambition against an inhuman force, exploring confinement, forbidden knowledge, survival, and the persistence of ancient darkness beneath modern war.
book-7144: Starting sixth grade feels like entering enemy territory for Rafe Khatchadorian, a restless, imaginative boy who finds middle school crowded with rules, bullies, and adults who seem determined to crush fun. To survive, he turns the school rulebook into a private challenge, trying to break every regulation while sketching cartoons and commentary in the margins of his days. His rebellion collides with strict administrators, a tormenting classmate, and growing trouble at home, where money is tight and family tensions simmer. Set in hallways, classrooms, and a cramped apartment, the story follows Rafe’s mischief, embarrassment, and anger as he tests limits and faces consequences. Themes include authority, creativity, friendship, family strain, and the uneven path between acting out and being understood.
book-7145: Lilith Iyapo awakens after nuclear war to find herself aboard an alien vessel, held by the Oankali, a species that rescues the last humans from extinction. As they prepare to return people to Earth, the Oankali insist on a biological and social partnership that promises survival but threatens human autonomy. Set in sterile ship corridors and the ruined future of Earth, the novel follows Lilith as she is trained to guide other survivors while confronting terror, distrust, and her own dependence on her captors. The central conflict turns on consent, hierarchy, and what it means to remain human when another species can alter bodies, reproduction, and destiny. Themes include genetic trade, power, gender, adaptation, and the destructive persistence of violence.
book-7146: Drawing on reporting about Silicon Valley and the search industry, this account traces Google’s rise from a Stanford research project to a dominant force in business, media, and technology. It follows founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin as they develop a search engine built on link analysis, confront technical demands of indexing the web, and shape an unusual corporate culture around engineering, speed, and expansive ambition. The narrative places the company within the dot-com era, online advertising, and the growing struggle over access to information. Central tensions include innovation versus commercialization, openness versus corporate control, and the pressures created by rapid growth, competition, and public scrutiny. Themes include entrepreneurship, data, internet infrastructure, leadership, and the transformation of everyday life by search technology.
book-7147: Set in Berlin during the Second World War, this historical novel follows an ordinary working-class couple who turn to quiet resistance after the death of their son at the front. They begin leaving handwritten postcards in stairwells and apartment buildings, urging strangers to oppose Hitler and the war, and their small acts draw the attention of the Gestapo. Around them, neighbors, informers, petty criminals, party loyalists, and fearful citizens reveal the pressures and compromises of life under Nazism. The narrative traces surveillance, denunciation, police procedure, and daily hardship in a city shaped by rationing, bombings, and suspicion. Its central conflict lies between private conscience and totalitarian power, with themes of moral courage, isolation, complicity, and the fragile dignity of individual action.
book-7148: In the desert nation of Miraji, a skilled young sharpshooter named Amani Al’Hiza wants to escape her dead-end town, an arranged future, and the limits placed on girls. After a shooting contest goes wrong, she joins forces with Jin, a mysterious foreigner on the run, and becomes entangled in a growing rebellion against the Sultan. Their flight carries them across dunes, caravan routes, palaces, and legendary landscapes where djinn, skinwalkers, and other creatures from local folklore are real. The novel blends adventure, court intrigue, and romance as Amani learns that survival depends on hidden identities, shifting loyalties, and dangerous magic. Central themes include freedom, self-invention, political resistance, and the cost of choosing one’s own fate.
book-7149: In a near-future United States shaped by short, brutal resource wars, physicist and former soldier Julian Class works with “soldierboy” technology, a system that lets troops control combat machines through direct neural links. The same interface begins to suggest a far wider use: shared consciousness that could alter politics, religion, labor, and war itself. As governments, corporations, and military factions struggle to control the technology, Julian and those closest to him face sabotage, fanaticism, and the threat of escalating global violence. Set in laboratories, city streets, and distant battlefields reached by telepresence, the novel examines militarism, class division, media spectacle, and the ethics of technological integration, while asking whether greater human connection leads to peace or to a new form of coercion.
book-715: A traveling salesman in postwar Brooklyn faces the collapse of the dream that has shaped his life. Willy Loman measures worth by charm, popularity, and material success, yet his dwindling income, exhausted marriage, and strained relationship with his sons expose the gap between hope and reality. As memories, regrets, and present disappointments mingle onstage, family arguments reveal long-standing betrayals, impossible expectations, and the pressure placed on ordinary Americans to perform prosperity. Set in a modest house shadowed by apartment buildings and the demands of modern business, the drama examines aging, work, masculinity, and the cost of self-deception. Through domestic scenes and fractured recollection, it presents a tragedy rooted not in kings or warriors but in debt, sales calls, and a father’s desperate belief in personal greatness.
book-7150: In near-future New York City, homicide lieutenant Eve Dallas investigates the killing of a fellow police officer, a case that quickly points toward professional discipline, hidden loyalties, and corruption within the NYPSD. As Eve follows financial records, departmental rivalries, and carefully staged alibis, the murder inquiry widens into a conspiracy that reaches through police ranks and into elite social circles. Roarke, her powerful husband, provides access and perspective, while the personal cost of the investigation tests Eve’s faith in the badge and in the people sworn to uphold it. Combining police procedural, romantic suspense, and thriller elements, the novel centers on institutional betrayal, the ethics of power, and the tension between public duty and private allegiance.
book-7151: Dreams, myths, religious images, and modern art become evidence in an introduction to analytical psychology for general readers. Written by Carl Jung and several close collaborators, the volume explains how symbols arise from the unconscious and shape emotions, behavior, and personal development. Chapters examine archetypes, the process of individuation, the role of dreams, and the recurring figures that appear in folklore, fairy tales, alchemy, and clinical case material. The central argument holds that rational modern life often ignores symbolic meaning, leaving inner conflicts unrecognized, while attention to images and fantasies can restore psychological balance. Across examples from everyday dreams to cultural rituals, the book explores the relation between conscious identity and the deeper layers of the psyche, with themes of self-knowledge, religion, creativity, and transformation.
book-7152: Set in western New York and the American frontier of the 1820s and 1830s, this historical novel follows the rise of the Latter-day Saint movement alongside the fortunes of a fictional family drawn into its orbit. Farmers, merchants, and preachers move through villages marked by revival meetings, land hunger, and intense sectarian debate as reports of visions, scripture, and new religious authority spread. The central conflict turns on faith, skepticism, and the cost of conversion, as family loyalties and community ties strain under persecution, migration, and competing beliefs. Blending domestic drama with religious history, the narrative portrays Joseph Smith and other early church figures while exploring revelation, discipleship, social upheaval, and the search for spiritual certainty in the burned-over district.
book-7153: A young stonekeeper and her companions cross the dangerous skies of Alledia in a fantasy quest rendered in graphic-novel form. Emily, her brother Navin, and their allies travel by airship toward the city of Cielis, hoping to find help against the Elf King and the growing war that threatens their world. The journey brings mechanical dangers, pirate attacks, giant creatures, and uneasy alliances, while Emily struggles to control the powerful amulet she carries. At the same time, Navin faces military discipline and the costs of resistance. Set among cloud cities, ruined landscapes, and elaborate machines, the story centers on courage, loyalty, leadership, and the tension between personal power and the wider conflict surrounding the siblings.
book-7154: A lonely Los Angeles writer shares his small, orderly life with Lily, the dachshund who is his closest companion and emotional center. When he discovers a mysterious octopus tightening its hold on her, he turns a devastating medical diagnosis into a fantastical enemy he can name, bargain with, and fight. The novel moves between city walks, beach days, dinner parties, and the narrator’s sharply comic interior monologue as he confronts grief, denial, aging, and the limits of control. Humor and whimsy sit beside veterinary visits and memories of past love, creating a story about the bond between a man and his dog, the stories people tell to survive loss, and the painful work of accepting mortality.
book-7155: After a failed Senate campaign exposes his role in the Vietnam War, John Wade retreats with his wife, Kathy, to a remote cabin on Minnesota’s Lake of the Woods. When Kathy vanishes, the novel turns into an investigation shaped by testimony, conjecture, and fragments of history rather than a single clear solution. The narrative follows the search for what happened to her while probing John’s buried memories of combat, his obsession with secrecy, and the strain inside the marriage. Set between the northern wilderness and the lingering violence of Vietnam, the book combines mystery with historical fiction and psychological study. It examines trauma, guilt, political performance, the unreliability of memory, and the ways private lives are altered by war.
book-7156: Set in Victorian England, this historical romance follows Poppy Hathaway, a practical young woman from an unconventional family, after a chance encounter places her reputation in danger and forces a sudden marriage to Harry Rutledge, the wealthy, secretive owner of a grand London hotel. Their union begins as a bargain shaped by scandal, social pressure, and Harry’s relentless determination, but married life exposes deeper conflicts of trust, class ambition, and emotional control. Within the bustling hotel and the orbit of the eccentric Hathaway clan, Poppy must decide whether security and desire can coexist with independence and honesty. The novel centers on courtship after marriage, family loyalty, sharp social comedy, and the tension between passion, respectability, and genuine intimacy.
book-7157: Ancient prophecy, Indian mythology, and a love triangle drive this young adult fantasy as Kelsey Hayes returns to India with the cursed tiger princes Ren and Kishan to confront the magician Lokesh. Their journey moves through temples, remote mountains, and supernatural realms while they search for sacred objects needed to break a centuries-old curse and prevent a destructive war. As battles with demons, divine tests, and courtly rivalries intensify, Kelsey must choose how far she will go to protect both brothers and what kind of future she wants. The novel centers on loyalty, destiny, sacrifice, reincarnation, and romantic conflict, blending quest adventure with mythic creatures, gods, and magic rooted in Hindu legend.
book-7158: At the U.S. Open, a missed putt by golf star Linda Coldren is followed by a far more serious crisis: her young son Chad disappears, and sports agent and investigator Myron Bolitar is drawn into the search. Moving between country clubs, locker rooms, suburban homes, and police interviews, the novel follows Myron as he navigates celebrity pressure, media scrutiny, and a web of old grudges surrounding the Coldren family. The central conflict joins a kidnapping case to buried secrets from the past, including violence, loyalty, and personal betrayal. Blending private-eye investigation with sports-world detail, the story explores class privilege, family protection, and the hidden damage beneath polished public images, while Myron’s persistence and uneasy alliances drive the inquiry forward.
book-7159: A contemporary romance unfolds between Molly Somerville, a successful children’s author with a reckless streak, and Kevin Tucker, the disciplined Chicago Stars quarterback she has loved for years. Set in Chicago and around the world of professional football, the story begins when an impulsive night leaves Molly pregnant and Kevin determined to keep emotional distance. Their clash pits her messy warmth and hunger for family against his control, ambition, and fear of entanglement. As they navigate celebrity scrutiny, team loyalties, old resentments, and the practical demands of impending parenthood, the novel balances comic mishaps with sharper conflicts about trust, responsibility, class expectations, and forgiveness. Themes of chosen family, vulnerability, and second chances shape a romance rooted in sports culture and urban domestic life.
book-716: In coastal Beaufort, North Carolina, a comfortable bachelor’s life begins to shift when Travis Parker’s new neighbor, Gabby Holland, moves in next door. Travis prefers boating, friends, and a future free of serious attachment, while Gabby is disciplined, ambitious, and already involved in another relationship. Their clashing first impressions give way to a deepening connection that forces both of them to confront what they want from love, loyalty, and adult commitment. The novel follows a contemporary Southern romance shaped by small-town routines, waterfront settings, family expectations, and the pressure of life-changing decisions. Its central conflict turns on emotional risk: whether to follow the safe path already chosen or to make a harder, more uncertain choice in the name of lasting love.
book-7160: Set in a contemporary world shaped by Greek gods, daimons, and the training compounds known as Covenants, this young adult fantasy novella follows the fallout after Alexandria Andros vanishes. Told from Aiden St. Delphi’s perspective, the story centers on his search for Alex while war gathers around the Hematoi world and the god-driven bond linking Alex to Seth grows more dangerous. Battles with daimons, political pressure inside the Covenant system, and the demands of duty sharpen the central conflict between loyalty, desire, and survival. The novella expands the series’ mythology while focusing on grief, obsession, and the cost of trying to save someone marked by prophecy. Themes of forbidden love, fate, sacrifice, and control run through a tense supernatural setting of training halls, hidden strongholds, and ancient power.
book-7161: A successful middle-aged geneticist begins a secret affair with a stranger after a chance encounter in Westminster, stepping outside the ordered routines of her family life and professional status. Set in contemporary London, the novel moves between private obsession, office politics, and the formal scrutiny of a criminal court. As the relationship deepens, a violent incident pulls her into a legal case that exposes hidden desires, compromised judgments, and the fragility of respectability. The narrative follows her voice as she reconstructs events for an audience already prepared to judge her. Part psychological thriller and part courtroom drama, it examines consent, power, class, female desire, self-deception, and the gap between public identity and private risk.
book-7162: A remote island near Cape Horn becomes the stage for a high-risk salvage operation when a wealthy collector finances the recovery of an enormous meteorite, believed to be the largest ever found on Earth. An elite team of engineers, sailors, and logistics specialists, led by the secretive strategist Eli Glinn, must cut the object from a treacherous cliff and move it across violent seas on a specially designed ship. As the expedition advances, technical failures, human rivalry, brutal weather, and the stone’s unsettling physical anomalies turn a feat of engineering into a survival crisis. Set in polar waters and aboard a heavily modified freighter, the novel combines scientific speculation, maritime suspense, and adventure while examining obsession, greed, risk, and the limits of control.
book-7163: Set in New York’s high-pressure investment banking world, this contemporary romance follows Kate Brooks as she balances a demanding career, a serious relationship with Drew Evans, and the vulnerabilities that come with trusting someone who thrives on charm and competition. When work obligations, distance, and old habits strain their bond, Kate must decide what commitment means beyond chemistry and banter. The novel shifts attention from office flirtation to the harder questions of fidelity, communication, ambition, and forgiveness, while keeping a brisk comic tone. Through sharp dialogue, boardroom negotiations, family expectations, and emotionally charged misunderstandings, it explores how two confident, stubborn professionals try to build a stable partnership without sacrificing pride, independence, or the lives they have fought to create.
book-7164: In an alternate Victorian London where werewolves, vampires, and inventors share drawing rooms with queens and spies, a pregnant Alexia Maccon navigates supernatural politics, household scandal, and a new threat linked to her unusual soulless nature. As a preternatural woman whose touch can cancel supernatural powers, she occupies a volatile place between human society and the paranormal aristocracy. Domestic comedy collides with occult investigation when murders, poison, and questions about loyalty unsettle London’s carefully managed balance. Tea tables, airships, laboratories, and pack strongholds form the backdrop for a plot that joins manners and espionage with monsters and gadgets. The novel explores marriage, motherhood, class performance, female independence, and the friction between rational inquiry and supernatural power within a steampunk fantasy mystery.
book-7165: An affluent young teacher from eastern Canada leaves family comfort for a classroom on the western frontier, where distance, weather, and rough living test her resolve. In a settlement shaped by ranch work, mining, and scattered homesteads, she meets children marked by hardship and adults whose practical habits challenge her sheltered expectations. As she adjusts to a plain boardinghouse, unfamiliar labor, and the social codes of a small community, she begins to reconsider class assumptions, vocation, and what Christian service requires in daily life. A developing romance adds another layer of uncertainty as she weighs duty against personal desire. Set in nineteenth-century Canada, the novel centers on faith, courtship, education, and the transformation that comes from crossing cultural and geographic boundaries.
book-7166: Set between New York City and a string of high-end travel destinations, this contemporary romance follows Holly Brennan, a successful food executive whose size makes her a target for public ridicule, and Logan Montgomery, a celebrity personal trainer known for sculpted bodies and tabloid attention. After an embarrassing incident throws them together, Logan offers Holly fitness coaching, and their arrangement shifts from wary friendship to attraction. The story centers on Holly’s struggle with body image, privacy, and trust as sudden visibility disrupts her carefully ordered life, while Logan confronts his own vanity, family expectations, and shallow reputation. Humor, media scrutiny, luxury hotels, and fitness culture frame a conflict about self-worth, desire, and whether intimacy can survive class differences, public gossip, and competing ideas of what a woman’s body should look like.
book-7167: Set in medieval Britain, this historical romance follows Lady Johanna, a young English widow whose first marriage leaves her wary of power, intimacy, and court politics. When the king arranges a new marriage to Gabriel MacBain, a formidable Scottish laird, she is drawn out of the English court and into the rugged Highlands, where clan loyalties, border tensions, and household rivalries shape daily life. The central conflict turns on trust: Johanna must navigate the dangers of male authority and the expectations placed on noblewomen, while Gabriel learns that protection alone cannot secure a marriage. Humor lightens scenes of culture clash between English refinement and Highland directness. Themes include healing after cruelty, the meaning of loyalty, female resilience, and the uneasy overlap of love, family, and political obligation.
book-7168: At Ramsay House in Victorian England, Leo Hathaway, titled, restless, and determined to avoid marriage, faces a family ultimatum: produce an heir or lose control of the estate. The most exasperating obstacle in his path is Catherine Marks, the competent governess who manages his sisters with sharp intelligence and little patience for his charm. Their skirmishes of wit and will conceal a powerful attraction, but Catherine guards private fears and family secrets that make any match dangerous. As pressure to marry increases and outside threats draw closer to the Hathaway household, the novel follows a battle between duty and desire. Themes of trust, class expectations, inheritance, emotional healing, and the disruptive force of love shape this historical romance, with humor woven through domestic chaos and verbal sparring.
book-7169: Set in mid-century American academia, the novel follows Timofey Pnin, a Russian émigré teaching at a small liberal arts college while trying to build a workable life in exile. His accented lectures, muddled practical affairs, and comic misadventures with trains, landlords, and faculty politics give the narrative its humor, but the book also traces the quieter costs of displacement. Pnin carries memories of pre-revolutionary Russia, loss during war, and an unhappy entanglement with his former wife, all while moving through a campus culture that never fully becomes home. Beneath the satire of college routines and intellectual pretension lies a portrait of loneliness, dignity, cultural dislocation, and the fragile ways a person preserves identity through language, habit, and memory.
book-717: Set in the dystopian world of Panem, this illustrated companion documents the making of the film adaptation of The Hunger Games. It presents photographs, concept art, costume and set designs, storyboards, and production notes that trace how the Capitol, District 12, the arena, and key visual symbols move from page to screen. Interviews and behind-the-scenes commentary from cast and filmmakers outline choices in casting, performance, makeup, props, and visual effects, while still anchoring the material in the story’s central premise of a televised fight to the death among teenagers. The volume focuses on adaptation, world-building, and film production, offering a reference to the movie’s imagery, characters, and themes of surveillance, spectacle, inequality, and survival rather than a retelling of the novel’s full plot.
book-7170: On a version of Earth where supernatural offices govern reality, a gifted young singer named Orb seeks independence from her powerful family and tries to build a life through music. Her voice has literal magical force, drawing her into bargains with spirits, dangerous lovers, and the hidden politics of the Incarnations who personify Death, Time, Fate, War, and Nature. As her personal desires collide with cosmic duties, she becomes entangled with the role of the Green Mother, the embodiment of fertility, wilderness, and the living world. The novel moves between concert stages, haunted landscapes, and occult power struggles, combining fantasy, science fiction, and horror elements. Major themes include free will, sexuality, responsibility, environmental balance, and the costs of power within an ordered but morally unstable universe.
book-7171: A girl named Meggie and her father Mo, a bookbinder with a dangerous gift, become entangled with villains and wanderers who can bring fictional characters out of books by reading aloud. The story begins in contemporary Europe among old houses, hidden libraries, and traveling performers, then moves into the Inkworld, a medieval fantasy realm of castles, forests, robbers, fire-eaters, and tyrannical rulers. Across the three novels, the central conflict concerns the power of language to create, alter, and end lives, as characters struggle with exile, revenge, loyalty, and the cost of changing a story. Recurring themes include reading and storytelling, the bond between parents and children, responsibility for imagined worlds, and the porous boundary between ordinary life and fiction.
book-7172: In imperial St. Petersburg, a low-ranking copying clerk named Akaky Akakievich lives in poverty, routine, and near invisibility within the Russian bureaucracy. His threadbare coat, mocked by colleagues and no longer repairable, becomes the focus of his savings, hopes, and fragile sense of dignity. When a new overcoat briefly changes how others see him, the garment exposes a world governed by rank, indifference, and petty cruelty. The story follows the collision between a humble civil servant and an administrative order that values status over human need. Through winter streets, office hierarchies, and urban loneliness, it examines social humiliation, material desire, bureaucratic absurdity, and the thin protections that separate a vulnerable person from despair and erasure.
book-7173: Set in early seventeenth-century Japan after the Battle of Sekigahara, this historical novel follows the young warrior Takezo, a ferocious village fighter who survives defeat and begins a long transformation into Miyamoto Musashi, the legendary swordsman. As he travels through rural provinces, castle towns, temples, and dueling grounds, he confronts rival schools, political disorder, and the violent code of the samurai. The narrative traces his discipline, wandering apprenticeship, and encounters with figures such as the monk Takuan and the independent Otsu, while a parallel rivalry grows around the refined swordsman Kojiro. Against a backdrop of civil reconstruction and rigid social rank, the novel examines honor, self-mastery, ambition, Zen practice, love, and the uneasy relation between martial skill and moral growth.
book-7174: Approaching her twelfth birthday in the town of Willow Falls, Rory Swenson keeps a long list of freedoms and milestones she expects to unlock at last: babysitting, sleeping over, shaving her legs, wearing makeup, getting her ears pierced, and other long-delayed privileges. Once the birthday arrives, nearly every plan goes wrong in messy, comic ways, from awkward social situations to small disasters that expose how little control she actually has. As Rory moves through school, family rules, friendships, and first crushes, the story follows her effort to sort out which parts of growing up matter and which are only fantasies. The novel centers on middle-school embarrassment, changing expectations, and the gap between wanting independence and being ready for it.
book-7175: Set in Ford County, Mississippi, this collection of linked stories follows ordinary people caught in legal trouble, family strain, old grudges, and sudden moral tests. Lawyers, small-town residents, inmates, and aging neighbors move through courtrooms, cotton fields, nursing homes, and back roads, where class, race, money, and reputation shape every decision. The conflicts are intimate rather than epic: a prison visit, a funeral trip, a disputed inheritance, a dangerous secret, a chance to settle scores. Across the stories, suspense grows from recognizable pressures in rural Southern life and from the gap between public respectability and private desperation. Themes include justice and revenge, loyalty and betrayal, economic decline, and the consequences of choices that seem minor until they turn irreversible.
book-7176: Set in Catholic Madrid, this Gothic novel follows Ambrosio, a celebrated Capuchin monk whose reputation for holiness masks pride, repression, and dangerous susceptibility to temptation. As desire, deceit, and ambition breach the walls of the monastery, the narrative moves through convent cells, aristocratic houses, crypts, and prison chambers, linking his downfall to parallel stories of forbidden love, family secrets, and persecution. Apparitions, bleeding nuns, banditti, and agents of the supernatural give the novel its horror atmosphere, while public piety and private corruption drive its central conflict. The book examines religious hypocrisy, sexual obsession, abuse of power, anticlerical anxiety, and the porous boundary between virtue and vice in late eighteenth-century Gothic fiction.
book-7177: Minnesota investigator Lucas Davenport is drawn into a string of brutal killings when his adopted daughter, Letty, spends time with a loose band of young drifters traveling by truck and on foot across the Midwest. Their countercultural camp life, marked by panhandling, campfires, and shifting loyalties, makes them vulnerable to predators who move unseen along highways and rural back roads. As one woman disappears and bodies begin to surface, Lucas follows a trail through small towns, roadside camps, and isolated properties, trying to identify a pair of violent offenders before more members of the group are taken. The novel combines police procedure with a manhunt, and centers on transient communities, exploitation, family protectiveness, and the collision between freedom on the road and extreme danger.
book-7178: Set in Seattle during the Depression, this historical novel follows twelve-year-old William Eng, a Chinese American boy raised in the Sacred Heart Orphanage after his mother is said to have died. On an outing to a local theater in 1934, he sees a glamorous film star named Willow Frost and becomes convinced she is his mother, Liu Song. The story moves between William’s search across the city and earlier years in 1921, tracing Liu Song’s life as a young woman caught between poverty, racism, illness, and the demands of survival. Streetcars, Chinatown alleys, vaudeville stages, and charity institutions shape a narrative about family separation, reinvention, memory, and the pressures placed on women and immigrants in the early twentieth-century Pacific Northwest.
book-7179: A grim homicide in Reykjavík draws Inspector Erlendur and his team into an investigation that reaches far beyond a single crime scene. An elderly man is found murdered in his apartment, and the few clues—a cryptic note, old records, and a photograph—lead police into buried histories of assault, illegitimacy, and family shame. As Erlendur traces connections between the victim and people on the margins of Icelandic society, the case opens onto questions of heredity, medical research, and the uses of genetic information in a small, tightly linked nation. The novel unfolds in contemporary Iceland through police interviews, forensic work, and Erlendur’s brooding private reflections, combining procedural detail with an atmosphere of cold streets, social isolation, and the long afterlife of violence.
book-718: Set in Jefferson, Mississippi, across the years before and after the First World War, the novel follows the decline of the once-aristocratic Compson family through four contrasting sections. Faulkner presents the same household through fractured interior monologue, shifting chronology, and sharply different voices, including the disabled Benjy, the tormented Harvard student Quentin, the bitter Jason, and a final section centered on the Black servant Dilsey. The central conflict lies in a family’s moral and financial collapse as obsession, resentment, sexual anxiety, and grief gather around the absent figure of Caddy Compson. Themes include time, memory, class, race, disability, Southern honor, and the failure of language to impose order on experience. The atmosphere often turns claustrophobic and disturbing, giving domestic ruin the pressure of horror.
book-7180: A Manhattan murder investigation leads forensic criminologist Lincoln Rhyme and detective Amelia Sachs into the rarefied world of stage magic after a woman dies during an illusion and the prime suspect seems to vanish from a locked theater. As clues point toward a killer who uses misdirection, trapdoors, rigged props, and the psychology of deception, the case expands from backstage workshops and rehearsal halls to old grudges inside the magic community. Rhyme analyzes fibers, burn marks, mechanical devices, and timing, while Sachs works the streets and follows witnesses who may have seen only what they were meant to see. Set in New York City, the novel centers on the conflict between forensic certainty and manufactured illusion, exploring performance, obsession, revenge, and the dangerous power of controlling perception.
book-7181: After a violent incident leaves her separated from her mother, twelve-year-old Carley Connors is placed in foster care with the Murphy family, a bustling household filled with warmth, routines, and three boisterous boys. Used to sarcasm, self-protection, and disappointment, Carley struggles to trust the affection and stability around her, even as Mrs. Murphy’s patience begins to unsettle her guarded view of family. Set in a contemporary small-town community of schools, basketball games, and crowded dinners, the novel follows Carley’s effort to navigate loyalty to her mother, fear of abandonment, and the unfamiliar possibility of belonging. The story examines foster care, child abuse, resilience, and the complicated meanings of home, while balancing painful emotional conflict with moments of humor and everyday family life.
book-7182: Drawing on ministry at the Brooklyn Tabernacle in New York City, this Christian memoir and devotional account argues that prayer and the Holy Spirit, rather than programs, charisma, or strategy, renew a church and change lives. It traces the growth of a struggling urban congregation into a thriving community marked by prayer meetings, worship, and outreach among people facing addiction, poverty, and family breakdown. Personal anecdotes, testimonies, and pastoral reflections present the central claim that spiritual vitality begins with repentance, dependence on God, and a willingness to seek divine power. The book addresses church leadership, congregational renewal, and individual faith, while exploring themes of revival, surrender, evangelism, and the tension between human effort and spiritual transformation in modern ministry.
book-7183: Set in Victorian London and on a remote tropical island, this young adult historical horror novel follows sixteen-year-old Juliet Moreau, who struggles to survive after her family falls into disgrace. When she discovers that her vanished father, a notorious surgeon, may still be alive, she leaves the city with Montgomery, the former servant she once trusted, and travels to his isolated estate. There she encounters locked laboratories, strange animal behavior, and humanlike creatures that suggest brutal experiments in vivisection and transformation. As Juliet investigates her father’s work, she faces divided loyalties, buried family secrets, and a growing fear of what science can justify. The novel explores bodily autonomy, cruelty, class, forbidden attraction, and the tension between reason and monstrosity.
book-7184: A series of brutal murders turns the fantasy of a romantic getaway into an international investigation as newlywed couples are killed in luxury hotels and famous cities across Europe. FBI agent John O'Hara, working with his former lover Sarah Brubaker, pursues a pair of elusive suspects whose crimes are staged against glamorous backdrops in Paris, Rome, and other tourist destinations. As the body count rises, the case grows more personal and more complicated, pulling in tensions between duty, desire, and betrayal. The novel combines police procedural detail with pursuit thriller momentum, using first-class resorts, airports, and crowded urban landmarks as settings for a hunt shaped by obsession, revenge, and the dangerous illusion of perfect love.
book-7185: Set in contemporary Boston, this romance follows Alexa Holland, a young woman still marked by her family’s public collapse, as she confronts Caine Carraway, the powerful businessman she blames for her father’s ruin and death. She approaches him intending to expose his cruelty, but instead becomes his employee and is drawn into the hard, controlled world he has built around himself. Their combative attraction unfolds against corporate rivalries, old betrayals, and the unequal balance of money, status, and secrecy. As Alexa learns more about Caine’s past and his connection to her family, the central conflict shifts from revenge to trust. Themes include class resentment, grief, power, emotional self-protection, and the risk of intimacy after damage.
book-7186: A collection of short comic essays, notes, and verbal riffs surveys everyday American life through George Carlin’s skeptical, abrasive lens. The pieces move from childhood memories, religion, language, and etiquette to war, politics, consumer culture, and the absurd rules people accept without question. Rather than offering a linear memoir, the book presents stand-up style observations on words, euphemisms, hypocrisy, aging, and the machinery of modern society, often turning on lists, redefinitions, and attacks on official pieties. Its central argument is that common institutions and habits—churches, governments, media slogans, polite speech, and public morality—deserve ridicule because they conceal confusion and manipulation. Themes include free expression, distrust of authority, the comedy of language, and the gap between public virtue and private behavior.
book-7187: A comic travel narrative follows writer Douglas Adams and zoologist Mark Carwardine as they journey to remote habitats in search of some of the world’s most endangered animals. Their route reaches islands, forests, rivers, and reefs, where they encounter species such as the kakapo, Komodo dragon, mountain gorilla, northern white rhinoceros, and Yangtze river dolphin. The book combines field notes, conservation reporting, and deadpan observation about airports, boats, weather, bureaucracy, and the awkward realities of wildlife expeditions. Beneath the humor, it examines extinction, habitat loss, and the fragile relationship between human activity and biological survival. Specific landscapes, animal behavior, and conversations with scientists and local guides ground its argument that rarity is not an abstraction but an immediate ecological crisis.
book-7188: After finding a rare Babe Ruth baseball card in a boarded-up house, sixth-grader Griffin Bing sells it for a tiny sum to a local collectibles dealer, only to learn the card is worth a fortune. When the dealer refuses to return it, Griffin organizes a risky plan to steal it back. Set in a contemporary American suburb, the story follows Griffin and a small group of classmates, each with a useful skill, as they prepare for a break-in involving guard dogs, security systems, and shifting loyalties. The central conflict pits resourceful children against a dishonest adult and raises questions about fairness, trust, and what counts as justice. Themes of friendship, teamwork, ingenuity, and moral choice drive this fast-paced children's mystery-adventure.
book-7189: A graphic memoir traces a childhood and early adulthood shaped by food, family, and travel. Raised by a chef mother and a gourmet father, the narrator moves through kitchens, restaurants, and farmers markets, learning how meals carry memory, class, comfort, and celebration. Episodic comics recount holiday rituals, adolescent eating habits, restaurant work, and trips that introduce regional dishes and culinary traditions. Interspersed recipes and illustrated ingredients make cooking part of the storytelling rather than an appendix. The central thread is the effort to understand identity through appetite: what it means to grow up in a household where taste, labor, and love are expressed through cooking. Themes include family inheritance, sensory memory, creative work, and the ways everyday meals become a personal history.
book-719: Drawing on spiritual philosophy and practical self-examination, the book argues that much human suffering grows from identification with the ego: the mental voice that seeks status, possession, grievance, and control. It describes how compulsive thought shapes personal relationships, family roles, workplace behavior, and collective conflict, and it proposes a shift toward present-moment awareness as a way to interrupt those patterns. Across discussions of pain, attachment, resentment, and purpose, it presents awakening not as withdrawal from ordinary life but as a different way of inhabiting it. Everyday settings—marriage, parenting, ambition, success, and loss—become examples for examining consciousness, inner stillness, and responsibility. Themes include identity, spirituality outside formal doctrine, emotional reactivity, and the possibility of individual and social transformation through attention.
book-7190: During a summer on a wealthy East Coast island, teen Gwen Castle juggles restaurant shifts, family obligations, and the return of Cass Somers, the privileged boy whose departure left anger and confusion behind. Gwen comes from the year-round working community that serves the summer residents, and the novel traces the sharp social divide between locals and the affluent visitors who shape the island’s economy. As Gwen reconnects with old friends and confronts rumors, class tensions, and buried secrets within her family, she questions the stories she has accepted about love, loyalty, and her own future. The romance unfolds alongside conflicts about reputation, honesty, and identity, making the book a contemporary young adult story about first love, changing friendships, and learning to see people beyond inherited assumptions.
book-7191: A reference-style account examines the television series Pretty Little Liars, a young adult mystery drama set in the affluent Pennsylvania town of Rosewood. It outlines the premise of four teenage girls whose lives are disrupted after the disappearance of their friend Alison and by threatening messages from an unknown figure known as “A.” The description focuses on the show’s central structure of secrets, surveillance, blackmail, shifting loyalties, and the investigation of buried crimes. It situates the program within teen television and adaptation, noting its basis in Sara Shepard’s novels and its blend of high school relationships with suspense plotting. Themes include friendship under pressure, identity, gossip, family tension, deception, and the danger of hidden pasts returning to control the present.
book-7192: Four teenage girls in Rosewood, Pennsylvania—Aria, Emily, Hanna, and Spencer—remain trapped in a campaign of surveillance, blackmail, and staged accidents orchestrated by the elusive “A.” As old lies about friendship, family, romance, and status collide with new clues, each girl faces private pressures at home and at school while trying to identify the person manipulating every move. The novel combines high school drama with mystery: hidden messages, shifting alibis, buried secrets, and dangerous misdirection drive the plot. Relationships with boyfriends, parents, and rivals become evidence as much as comfort, and trust grows harder to sustain. Themes of guilt, performance, jealousy, and the cost of deception shape a story set amid suburban bedrooms, classrooms, parties, and police suspicion.
book-7193: Across 1960s New York and prewar Europe, a family mystery unfolds around Violet Grant, a gifted chemist who vanishes from her prominent American family and reappears in the shadows of the First World War. Decades later, Vivian Schuyler, a young columnist eager to escape society-page expectations, receives Violet’s suitcase and begins tracing the older woman’s hidden life through letters, laboratories, hotel rooms, and scandal. The novel follows Violet’s struggle to pursue scientific work in a world that limits women’s ambition, while Vivian confronts the silences and evasions of her own clan. Romance, betrayal, class privilege, exile, and female self-determination shape a narrative about reinvention, the costs of secrecy, and the fragile records women leave behind.
book-7194: Set in a world of private security firms, hidden identities, and obsessive desire, this romantic thriller follows a guarded woman pulled into the orbit of a dangerous investigation and the dominant bodyguard assigned to protect her. As threats tighten around her and clues point toward a violent predator, the pair move through nightclubs, surveillance operations, and high-risk encounters where trust is as precarious as safety. Their relationship develops through explicit erotic tension, power exchange, and the emotional strain of uncovering secrets neither fully controls. Mystery and suspense drive the plot, but the novel also centers on vulnerability, consent, loyalty, and the clash between self-protection and intimacy. Crime investigation, kidnapping danger, and sexual obsession shape the story’s central conflict.
book-7195: At Bloor’s Academy, Charlie Bone continues to navigate a school where children with magical endowments are drawn into the long, dangerous legacy of the Red King. When a mysterious beast becomes linked to the academy’s latest threats, Charlie and his friends must untangle old family secrets, hidden identities, and the schemes of the sinister Bloor family. Set between the gray, watchful corridors of the school and the tense world of Charlie’s unusual relatives and allies, the story centers on loyalty under pressure, the misuse of inherited power, and the risks of uncovering the past. Fantasy adventure, school rivalries, kidnappings, enchanted animals, and ancestral magic shape a conflict in which Charlie’s growing abilities matter as much as his courage and judgment.
book-7196: A contemporary sports romance set in New York follows a sharp, ambitious woman working in the media as she crosses paths with a famous professional football quarterback whose public image hides grief, pressure, and a complicated private life. Their attraction grows through flirtation, interviews, and chance encounters, but a relationship between a reporter and a star athlete brings obvious conflicts of interest and constant scrutiny. The story moves between locker rooms, bars, apartments, and city streets, grounding its humor and sexual tension in the routines of celebrity sports culture. Alongside the banter and explicit romance, the novel examines trust, career ambition, tabloid attention, past heartbreak, and the difficulty of separating genuine intimacy from the performance demanded by fame.
book-7197: Civil war and foreign invasion threaten the Annurian Empire after the murder of its emperor, while his surviving children struggle to hold a fractured realm together. Adare works within the capital’s court and religious hierarchy, trying to understand a fanatical movement and the political forces gathering around it. Valyn, trained among the brutal Kettral, faces mutiny, loyalty, and the cost of military command as war spreads across island fortresses and sea routes. Kaden, raised in a remote mountain monastery, pursues hidden knowledge about ancient powers and the beings moving behind human conflict. Set across imperial cities, monasteries, battlefields, and wilderness, the novel combines dynastic politics, martial discipline, religion, and questions of identity, power, and sacrifice in a secondary-world epic fantasy.
book-7198: Developed from a 1945 public lecture, this philosophical essay presents Jean-Paul Sartre’s defense of existentialism against charges of despair, amorality, and nihilism. Writing in the aftermath of war and occupation, he argues that human beings are not born with a fixed essence, divine plan, or moral blueprint; they become what they choose through action. The central claim is that radical freedom brings radical responsibility: each decision commits the individual and, by example, expresses an image of humanity as a whole. Sartre addresses anguish, abandonment, bad faith, and commitment, insisting that meaning arises from lived choices rather than abstract systems. The text situates existentialism within modern secular thought and explores freedom, ethics, accountability, and the burden of creating values in an indifferent world.
book-7199: Drawing on decades of travel across the United States and abroad, this memoir traces Gloria Steinem’s life as a journalist, feminist organizer, and public speaker shaped by movement from place to place. It begins with a childhood spent in cars and hotels with an itinerant father, then follows buses, airplanes, campaign trails, lecture halls, and meetings where she listens to women, workers, students, and political activists. The narrative connects personal history with major social movements, especially second-wave feminism, civil rights, and democratic organizing. Encounters on the road become the book’s central structure and argument: travel creates unexpected communities, challenges hierarchy, and turns private experience into collective action. Themes include freedom, identity, grassroots politics, friendship, and the relationship between storytelling and social change.
book-72: An isolated mountain hotel becomes the winter home and workplace of Jack Torrance, a struggling writer and recovering alcoholic, who arrives with his wife Wendy and their young son Danny after accepting a caretaker job during the off-season. Cut off by snow, the family settles into the vast Overlook Hotel, where empty corridors, a violent history, and lingering supernatural forces press on Jack’s instability and Danny’s psychic gift, known as the shining. As the hotel’s influence grows, domestic strain turns into terror inside a setting of locked rooms, topiary animals, ballrooms, and haunted memories. The novel combines supernatural horror with psychological suspense, focusing on addiction, family violence, isolation, childhood perception, and the way a place can feed on human weakness.
book-720: In contemporary Japan, high school student Ichigo Kurosaki can see ghosts and is drawn into the hidden work of Soul Reapers, warriors who guide the dead and fight monstrous spirits called Hollows. When a chance encounter with the Soul Reaper Rukia Kuchiki leaves her injured, Ichigo takes on her powers and responsibilities, defending his family and neighborhood from supernatural attacks while trying to understand the rules of the spirit world. The volume introduces a modern urban setting where school life, family routines, and street corners coexist with invisible threats and wandering souls. Its central conflict follows Ichigo’s uneasy acceptance of duty and violence, while themes of grief, protection, adolescence, and the boundary between the living and the dead shape the story.
book-7200: Creative work often falters not because of weak vision but because execution breaks down under competing priorities, distractions, and incomplete follow-through. Drawing on examples from entrepreneurs, designers, and other creative professionals, this guide examines how ideas move from inspiration to finished project. It argues for practical systems: organizing action steps, separating brainstorming from implementation, managing long-term projects, and building accountability within teams. The discussion addresses the tension between inventiveness and discipline, showing how meetings, workflows, and decision-making habits shape results. It also considers the role of community, leadership, and feedback in sustaining momentum. Set in the world of startups, studios, and knowledge work, the book focuses on productivity, collaboration, and the everyday obstacles that stand between ambition and concrete outcomes.
book-7201: Los Angeles nightlife, celebrity blogs, and reality television shape this young adult novel about sudden fame and private betrayal. Jane Roberts tries to manage the fallout from becoming the breakout star of a hit TV series while tabloids and gossip websites turn every friendship, date, and argument into public spectacle. As attention intensifies, she faces fractured trust with her best friends Scarlett and Madison, uncertainty about who is using her for exposure, and rumors that threaten both her relationships and her career. The story follows parties, studio meetings, and backstage conversations across an image-driven city where cameras never seem far away. Themes of friendship, ambition, romance, jealousy, and the cost of living as a manufactured celebrity drive the conflict, with mystery elements surrounding secrets, manipulation, and competing versions of the truth.
book-7202: Set in the world of underground boxing circuits, this contemporary romance follows Remington Tate, a volatile champion known as Riptide, as he fights for control inside and outside the ring. The novel centers on his relationship with Brooke Dumas, a former athlete whose presence offers intimacy, discipline, and risk. From Remington’s perspective, the story traces training camps, hotel rooms, arenas, and tour stops while he navigates fame, possessiveness, and the strain of bipolar disorder. The central conflict lies in whether love can survive jealousy, public pressure, and the instability that shadows his career. Themes of mental illness, desire, loyalty, vulnerability, and the cost of violence shape a romance grounded in physical competition and emotional exposure.
book-7203: Amid Denver’s tight-knit circle of private investigators, cops, and stubborn friends, a woman who has spent years surviving abuse and intimidation decides to fight back and claim a safer life. Her path keeps crossing with a hard-edged lawman whose protective instincts, criminal cases, and unresolved attraction pull her into escalating danger. As threats from violent men and past entanglements close in, the story mixes romantic pursuit, street-level suspense, comic banter, and found-family loyalty. The central conflict turns on whether she can trust help without surrendering independence, and whether their volatile chemistry can survive secrets, fear, and the risks of revenge. Themes include recovery from trauma, female friendship, possessive love, personal courage, and justice in a world where crime and intimacy constantly collide.
book-7204: On a bitter New Year's Eve, a poor child walks the streets barefoot, trying to sell matches while snow falls and windows glow with holiday warmth. Afraid to return home empty-handed, she shelters in a corner and begins striking the matches one by one. Each brief flame summons a vivid vision: a hot stove, a feast, a shining Christmas tree, and at last the loving presence of her dead grandmother. The story moves between urban poverty and dreamlike apparitions, using simple, stark scenes to show hunger, cold, loneliness, and the child's longing for safety and affection. Andersen's tale joins realism with fantasy and Christian imagery, presenting innocence, social neglect, compassion, and transcendence in a concise, haunting narrative.
book-7205: Shortly after the fall of the Taliban, a young British diplomat and former aid worker walks across central Afghanistan, traveling on foot from Herat to Kabul through winter snow, ruined villages, and mountain passes. The narrative combines travel memoir, political observation, and historical reflection as he depends on local guides, village elders, soldiers, and families for food, shelter, and protection. Encounters with war damage, hospitality, tribal custom, and suspicion reveal a country shaped by empire, civil conflict, and poverty rather than simple headlines about invasion and terrorism. The central tension lies in the difficulty of moving safely through a fractured landscape while trying to understand it honestly. Themes include endurance, cultural misunderstanding, survival, hospitality, and the limits of foreign knowledge about Afghanistan.
book-7206: A recurring dream draws six strangers toward a shared quest that blends paranormal romance with adventure. Sasha Riggs, a reclusive artist in North Carolina, begins seeing a mysterious island, a woman trapped in glass, and five unknown companions. Her search leads to Greece, where she joins travelers linked by magic, fate, and ancient bloodlines: a magician, a werewolf, a mermaid, a warrior, and a seer. Together they learn they are guardians chosen to recover three powerful stars before a dark goddess can claim them. Set between everyday modern life and myth-charged landscapes, the novel centers on awakening powers, forming uneasy alliances, and the growing love between Sasha and Bran as danger closes around the group.
book-7207: Across adolescence and early adulthood, a self-deprecating narrator recounts a string of awkward encounters with girls and women, from childhood crushes and disastrous dates to more serious relationships. Set in suburban California, college life, and the uncertain years of early adult independence, the memoir follows his repeated misunderstandings about romance, sex, and emotional maturity. Running through these episodes is the blunt, profane commentary of his father, whose skeptical advice collides with his son’s confusion and idealism. The central tension lies between longing for connection and sabotaging it through insecurity, immaturity, and comic misreading of social cues. Combining personal anecdote with family banter, the book explores masculinity, embarrassment, dating, heartbreak, and the slow, uneven process of learning how intimacy actually works.
book-7208: A cache of jewels vanishes during a violent political upheaval in the Middle East, and the trail leads quietly to Meadowbank, an elite girls’ school in the English countryside. What begins as ordinary school routine—lessons, games, rivalries, and anxious administrators—turns ominous when a sports mistress is found murdered in the pavilion. As fear spreads through dormitories and staff rooms, a second killing suggests that the school shelters someone connected to espionage, money, and a hidden inheritance. Hercule Poirot enters only after suspicion and gossip have tangled the case, and he must sort through princesses in exile, teachers with secrets, and students who see more than adults expect. The novel combines country-house detection with Cold War intrigue, examining class, loyalty, and deception behind respectable walls.
book-7209: Spanning centuries of French history, the novel follows several families whose fortunes rise and fall with the city of Paris, from medieval streets and religious conflict to revolution, empire, occupation, and modern reinvention. Aristocrats, craftsmen, students, artists, and political idealists move through landmarks such as Notre-Dame, the Louvre, Montmartre, and the boulevards reshaped by Haussmann, linking private ambitions to public upheaval. The central drama lies in how love, loyalty, class interest, and survival are tested as regimes collapse and new orders emerge. Battles over faith, monarchy, republicanism, and national identity unfold alongside domestic rivalries and social climbing. Themes include memory, inheritance, urban change, and the way a great city preserves traces of violence and aspiration across generations.
book-721: Through illustrated autobiographical essays, a young woman recounts childhood misadventures, household chaos, internet-era adulthood, and the strange logic of her own reactions to ordinary problems. Simple, expressive drawings and caption-driven scenes follow episodes involving overeating cake, failing at responsibility, living with disobedient dogs, and navigating family memories that turn embarrassment into comic narrative. Beneath the absurdity, the collection also addresses depression, motivation, and the difficulty of explaining mental illness when daily life seems outwardly trivial. The central tension lies between unruly emotion and the effort to impose order through storytelling, self-mockery, and observation. Themes include shame, resilience, procrastination, animal behavior, and the gap between how experience feels from the inside and how it appears to everyone else.
book-7210: Set largely in late nineteenth-century France, this collection gathers Guy de Maupassant’s concise stories of clerks, soldiers, shopkeepers, peasants, and provincial women whose ordinary desires collide with rigid social expectations. “The Necklace,” the best-known tale, follows a dissatisfied middle-class wife whose hunger for elegance and status leads to a disastrous deception. Around it, other stories examine vanity, poverty, marriage, class ambition, war, greed, and the small cruelties of daily life. Maupassant uses realistic settings, sharp dialogue, and ironic reversals to show how pride, chance, and reputation shape human lives. Written in clear, accessible prose, the volume introduces young adult and general readers to French realism through brief narratives that expose the tension between appearance and reality, social rank and personal longing, illusion and consequence.
book-7211: Set in the neon casinos, hotel towers, and service corridors of Las Vegas, this thriller follows Cassie Black, a former high-end thief who tries to leave crime behind. Drawn into one last operation involving a wealthy target and a carefully staged casino robbery, she finds the job collapsing into violence and deception. As police pressure grows and hidden players begin to surface, Cassie moves through counting rooms, surveillance systems, limousines, and desert roads to uncover who has betrayed her and why. The novel combines heist mechanics with murder investigation, tracing a woman skilled in disguise and escape as she confronts guilt, grief, and the dangerous pull of the life she thought she had escaped.
book-7212: A spoiled fifteen-year-old heir, Harvey Cheyne, is swept overboard from an Atlantic liner and rescued by fishermen aboard the Gloucester schooner We’re Here. Set on the Grand Banks during a North Atlantic cod-fishing season, the novel follows his forced separation from wealth, servants, and social privilege as he works among a practical, tight-knit crew. The central conflict lies in Harvey’s struggle to adapt to hard labor, danger, discipline, and the plain speech of men who judge worth by skill and conduct rather than family money. Episodes of hauling nets, cleaning fish, facing storms, and sharing cramped quarters create a detailed portrait of nineteenth-century maritime life. Themes include class, masculinity, apprenticeship, responsibility, and moral growth, as Harvey gradually learns competence, humility, and respect for work.
book-7213: Minneapolis police investigator Lucas Davenport hunts a calculating killer whose targets are linked to old political violence and bitter conflicts over Native American land, power, and money. The case begins with a brutal assassination and expands into a series of murders that suggest a disciplined campaign rather than random revenge. Moving through winter streets, government offices, wealthy suburbs, and reservation politics, Davenport follows clues tangled in corruption, historical grievance, and personal loyalty. The novel combines procedural detection with cat-and-mouse suspense as Lucas balances police work, informants, and his own volatile instincts against an adversary who plans carefully and strikes without hesitation. Themes of justice, vengeance, identity, and the long afterlife of public crimes shape the investigation.
book-7214: Set between contemporary New Orleans and the musical capitals of nineteenth-century Europe, this gothic novel follows Triana, a grieving widow and professional violinist whose life has narrowed into obsession, depression, and thoughts of death. Her isolation is interrupted by the appearance of a seductive, violent ghost who calls himself Stefan and claims a long history of genius, cruelty, and loss. As he draws her into his memories of aristocratic salons, concert halls, and ruined ambitions, the story links the discipline of classical music with possession, desire, and the burden of artistic ambition. The central conflict lies in Triana’s struggle to resist annihilation while confronting the ghost’s influence and her own despair. Themes include mourning, obsession, immortality, erotic power, and the destructive hunger for beauty and mastery.
book-7215: A young New York mother struggles to understand her small son’s violent nightmares, strange phobias, and detailed memories that do not seem to belong to him. As Noah speaks of another family, another home, and a death he could not have witnessed, Janie turns to Jerome Anderson, an aging psychiatrist known for investigating children who appear to remember previous lives. Their search leads from city apartments to coastal landscapes and into the unresolved history of a murdered man, where grief, obsession, and buried guilt shape every clue. Moving between psychological mystery and supernatural suspense, the novel examines maternal fear, memory, reincarnation, and the possibility that trauma can survive death and demand recognition from the living.
book-7216: A young child writes to the zoo asking for a pet, and a series of animals arrives in crates with flaps to lift. Each creature is rejected for a simple, child-centered reason: an elephant is too big, a lion is too fierce, a camel is too grumpy. The repeated pattern, sturdy pages, and hidden reveals shape an interactive read-aloud for babies and preschoolers, inviting prediction, naming, and participation. Set in the familiar imaginative space between home and zoo, the story turns animal characteristics into gentle humor while building vocabulary through adjectives and animal names. Its central movement comes from the search for the right pet, and its themes include curiosity, surprise, suitability, and the pleasures of repetition in early childhood reading.
book-7217: A gifted Tokyo high school student continues his secret campaign as Kira, using a supernatural notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it, while the enigmatic detective L tightens an increasingly personal investigation. As police scrutiny shifts from distant patterns of death to suspects inside the task force’s reach, the contest becomes a meticulous battle of surveillance, deduction, and deception. The volume moves between classrooms, family apartments, police headquarters, and hidden observation rooms, emphasizing how ordinary urban spaces become arenas for psychological warfare. Questions of justice, punishment, and moral authority remain central as Light tries to preserve his double life and outmaneuver investigators who are learning how disciplined and ruthless their opponent is. Obata’s sharp visual pacing underscores paranoia, strategy, and the cost of absolute certainty.
book-7218: Set in the Kingdom of Araluen and its neighboring lands, this young adult fantasy gathers linked tales from the Ranger’s Apprentice world, filling in events that occur between earlier adventures and after major battles. Will Treaty, the Ranger Halt, Horace, Cassandra, and other familiar figures face rescues, diplomatic missions, bandits, political unrest, and personal milestones as the stories move from forests and fiefs to castles and distant frontiers. The central interest lies less in one continuous quest than in how scattered episodes deepen friendships, loyalty, duty, and the craft of the Rangers. Archery, tracking, disguises, and battlefield strategy remain central, while several stories explore marriage, succession, mentorship, and the burdens of leadership. The collection expands the series’ history while preserving its episodic adventure structure.
book-7219: While visiting Washington, D.C., former military policeman Jack Reacher is drawn into a quiet Pentagon investigation involving a string of security breaches and four attractive female Army officers who all work in the same secret unit. Senior officials suspect that one of them is passing classified information, but no one can identify the leak or explain the motive.
