The novel follows military life in camp and on the march, from officers’ rivalries and class prejudice to close combat in India’s heat and dust. Its central conflict turns on Sharpe’s struggle to survive, recover his standing, and seize advancement in an army where birth matters as much as courage. Themes include imperial war, ambition, discipline, and the making of a hard, resourceful fighting man.
book-7308: After a family crisis in Iowa, sixteen-year-old Jean Honeychurch moves to her relatives’ apartment on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, where her glamorous cousin Tory rules the social scene and treats old superstitions as party tricks. Jean, nicknamed Jinx, has long believed she brings bad luck, especially after a childhood spell seemed to end in disaster. In New York, strange accidents, charms, and whispered folklore make that fear harder to dismiss. As she settles into a world of private schools, rooftop gatherings, and wealthy neighbors, she is drawn to a thoughtful boy next door and forced to confront Tory’s growing obsession with power. The novel combines contemporary teen life with witchcraft, family tension, guilt, and romance, exploring responsibility, jealousy, and the question of whether destiny can be changed.
book-7309: Set largely in late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century Europe, these tales follow artists, students, bourgeois families, and solitary observers as they confront desire, illness, social convention, and spiritual unrest. The title novella centers on an aging German writer who travels to Venice seeking rest and becomes fixated on a beautiful Polish boy while the city drifts toward a cholera outbreak. Around it, other stories examine frustrated love, artistic ambition, class tension, religious feeling, and the strain between disciplined public life and unruly inner impulse. Recurring settings such as boarding houses, city streets, theaters, and holiday resorts give the collection a historical texture, while the prose probes beauty, decay, repression, obsession, and the costs of self-control.
book-731: In Georgetown, Washington, D.C., a successful actress watches her twelve-year-old daughter change from an affectionate child into a violent, profane, and seemingly inhuman presence. Doctors offer diagnoses, tests, and institutional explanations, but the girl’s seizures, voices, hidden knowledge, and physical distortions defy medicine and psychiatry. As the crisis deepens, a Jesuit priest burdened by grief and doubt is drawn into the case, confronting the possibility of demonic possession and the demands of an exorcism ritual. The novel combines domestic realism, clinical detail, and Catholic theology with scenes of terror and investigation. Its central conflict pits skepticism against faith, and human frailty against an evil that invades the body and the home, exploring innocence, guilt, belief, and the limits of rational understanding.
book-7310: Eleven-year-old chemist and amateur sleuth Flavia de Luce leaves her family estate in 1950s England and is sent across the Atlantic to Miss Bodycote’s Female Academy in Toronto, a stern boarding school with a buried past. Soon after her arrival, a body drops from a chimney, and Flavia is drawn into an investigation involving missing students, old secrets, and the school’s murky connection to a wartime intelligence network. As she navigates dormitories, classrooms, and the unfamiliar streets of Canada, she relies on sharp observation, knowledge of poisons, and a taste for forensic detail. The novel combines a school story with a murder mystery, exploring exile, loyalty, identity, and the tension between childhood and adult danger.
book-7311: At a London comprehensive school, veteran history teacher Barbara Covett becomes fascinated by Sheba Hart, a charismatic art teacher whose unruly home life and classroom troubles leave her isolated. When Sheba begins a secret sexual relationship with one of her adolescent students, Barbara becomes confidante, observer, and increasingly controlling witness to the scandal that follows. The novel moves through staffroom gossip, suburban family strain, and the machinery of tabloids, police, and school discipline, while Barbara’s first-person account exposes her own loneliness, resentment, and hunger for intimacy. Set in contemporary England, it examines female friendship, predation, class tension, aging, self-deception, and the unreliable stories people tell about desire, morality, and power.
book-7312: In the hidden vampire society of Caldwell, New York, the Black Dagger Brotherhood faces new strain as war with the Lessening Society and the Band of Bastards continues. Rhage, the warrior known for the lethal dragonlike beast he carries inside him, is unsettled by change in his bond with his mate Mary and by a sense that his hard-won control may be slipping. At the same time, a young woman with ties to the Brotherhood is drawn into the vampires’ world, where bloodlines, loyalty, and old enemies shape every choice. The novel combines paranormal romance and dark fantasy with scenes of combat, court politics, family devotion, and possessive love, focusing on inner monstrosity, the cost of violence, and the struggle to protect intimacy during ongoing supernatural conflict.
book-7313: Set between Atlanta and the South Carolina shore, this novel follows Susan Hayes, a woman whose carefully managed life unravels when her marriage and career collapse. She returns to her family home on Sullivan’s Island, where the salt marshes, beach houses, and tightly knit Lowcountry community force her back into old roles and unresolved tensions. At the center is Susan’s difficult bond with her commanding mother, whose expectations shape every family gathering and private wound. As Susan reconnects with siblings, old friends, and the rhythms of coastal life, she faces questions of loyalty, identity, class, and belonging. Blending domestic comedy with family drama, the story explores Southern manners, generational conflict, romantic possibility, and the challenge of rebuilding a self after disappointment.
book-7314: After capturing the last Clow Card, elementary school student Sakura Kinomoto enters a new stage of her magical life in contemporary Tomoeda. Strange dreams, unusual disturbances, and a growing change in her own power suggest that the legacy of the sorcerer Clow Reed is not finished with her. Alongside guardian beast Kero, the reserved Yukito, and rival-turned-ally Syaoran Li, she faces mysteries surrounding the cards, her wand, and the meaning of becoming their true master. The volume combines school routines, costume-filled card battles, and quiet emotional shifts as Sakura’s feelings for the people around her deepen. Themes of responsibility, affection, courage, and maturation run through a fantasy story that blends everyday friendship and romance with secret magic.
book-7315: After moving with his family to a small Minnesota town, teenager Jacob Lau begins to see disturbing figures no one else notices and experiences vivid dreams tied to death, memory, and a hidden spiritual war. As his hearing loss and social isolation make ordinary high school life difficult, he learns that the world around him holds soul-eating beings, secret lineages, and guardians charged with protecting human souls. The central conflict follows Jacob as he tries to understand whether his visions signal illness or a dangerous inheritance, while sinister forces close in on his family and friends. Set between classrooms, snowy neighborhoods, and eerie unseen realms, the novel combines young adult fantasy and horror through themes of faith, identity, grief, temptation, and the burden of accepting an unwelcome calling.
book-7316: Thirty years after serving in Vietnam, Army investigator Paul Brenner returns to the country on an official tour with a State Department escort, ostensibly to discuss wartime cooperation and missing-in-action cases. Beneath the diplomatic itinerary, he carries a private mission: to learn what happened to a fellow soldier whose death in 1972 was officially blamed on the enemy but may have been murder. Moving through Hanoi, Hue, Saigon, and the Central Highlands, he confronts old battlefields, guarded memories, and a Vietnamese landscape transformed by peace and commerce. The novel combines military history, travel through postwar Vietnam, and a murder inquiry rooted in combat loyalties. Its central tensions involve truth versus official silence, the persistence of wartime guilt, and the uneasy meeting of former enemies in a place shaped by memory.
book-7317: On a single, sleepless night in the First World War, young soldier Tommo Peaceful remembers the rural English childhood that shaped him and his older brother Charlie. Their memories move through farm labor, school punishments, family loss, and Tommo’s deep attachment to Molly, the girl both brothers love. As the story shifts from village fields to the trenches of France, ordinary loyalties are tested by military discipline, class authority, fear, and the brutal routines of war. The novel centers on brotherhood, love, guilt, courage, and the cost of obedience, showing how private memories collide with public violence. Written for younger readers but grounded in historical detail, it presents wartime experience through an intimate, reflective first-person voice.
book-7318: Set in 1930s London and the Scottish countryside, this historical mystery follows Lady Georgiana Rannoch, a penniless young aristocrat who is thirty-fourth in line to the British throne. Cut off from money and expected to maintain royal dignity, she tries to live independently while navigating rigid class rules, unsuitable suitors, and family pressure. When Queen Mary quietly asks her to keep an eye on the Prince of Wales and his attachment to Wallis Simpson, Georgiana is pulled into dangerous royal intrigue. Her fragile freedom is further threatened when a man connected to her brother turns up dead, leaving her entangled in murder, police suspicion, and blackmail. The novel combines drawing rooms, servants’ staircases, and London boarding houses with themes of class, gender, duty, and self-determination.
book-7319: In magic-ravaged Atlanta, investigator Andrea Nash works dangerous jobs for Cutting Edge while hiding a secret that threatens her place among shapeshifters: she is a hyena beastkin raised to despise what she is. Her uneasy romance with Raphael Medrano, a bouda clan leader who wants marriage and children, collides with a new case when members of his family vanish. Following the trail through crime scenes, pack politics, and waves of lethal magic, Andrea uncovers a ritual tied to an ancient Egyptian power hungry for blood and devotion. The novel combines urban fantasy, horror, and romance through gunfights, shapechanging battles, and tense negotiations, while exploring trauma, identity, loyalty, and the strain between self-protection and intimacy.
book-732: In Seattle’s shadowy streets, a newborn vampire named Bree Tanner struggles to survive the violent, short-lived world of an army of newly turned vampires. Under the command of Riley, who serves a hidden creator, Bree learns the rules of hunting, secrecy, and constant territorial war while trying to understand why the group is being prepared for a coming confrontation. Her growing bond with another outsider in the coven gives her a fragile sense of trust, even as deception and fear shape every decision around her. Set alongside the events of Eclipse, the novella focuses on the brutal instincts of newborn vampires, the manipulation of the vulnerable, and the conflict between individual conscience and obedience within a predatory supernatural hierarchy.
book-7320: Across the fractured kingdoms of the Shattered Sea, Princess Skara sees her grandfather, mother, and brother murdered and loses a throne in a single night. Forced into exile, she must trade courtly polish for political cunning as she seeks allies against the ruthless warlord who has seized her kingdom. Beside her, Father Yarvi, the crippled minister and former king, works to bind old enemies into a fragile alliance, while veteran warriors such as Thorn Bathu and Raith carry the struggle onto sea and battlefield. The novel follows raids, embassies, and shifting loyalties through ports, halls, and island strongholds. Its central conflict turns on whether divided rulers can unite before conquest spreads, exploring power, vengeance, diplomacy, faith, and the hard education of leadership in a brutal world.
book-7321: Set in Denver, this romantic suspense novel follows Jules Lawler, a stylish, sharp-tongued woman who becomes entangled again with Vance Crowe, the hard-edged investigator and bounty hunter she has never forgiven for a painful incident in the past. When criminal danger begins circling her and the people around her, Vance pushes himself into her life as protector, turning old resentment into a volatile mix of anger, attraction, and reluctant dependence. The story moves through apartments, bars, surveillance jobs, and confrontations with violent men, combining comic dialogue with action and erotic tension. Central conflicts revolve around whether Jules can trust Vance, whether Vance can overcome his own controlling instincts, and how a romance can form under pressure. Themes include loyalty, female friendship, trauma, protection, and forgiveness.
book-7322: Set in the close-knit Conte family’s New York world of bakeries, business, and loud Sunday dinners, this contemporary romance follows Carina Conte, a practical youngest sister who has long carried an unspoken crush on Max Gray, the disciplined corporate vice president who works for her brother. Max values order, control, and emotional distance, while Carina hides vulnerability behind perfectionism and family loyalty. When family pressure and professional complications force them into close quarters, desire collides with old assumptions and carefully guarded fears. Their central conflict grows from mismatched expectations about love, marriage, and self-worth, as each must confront past wounds and the roles others have assigned them. Humor, sexual tension, Italian American family dynamics, and themes of trust, identity, and commitment shape the story.
book-7323: A small child and a friendly bear set out on a gleeful berry-picking adventure that quickly expands into a dreamlike landscape of raspberries, blueberries, blackberries, and strawberries. Told in bouncing rhyme, the story moves through meadows, streams, and fantastical berry places where canoes, hills, and fields are all shaped by fruit. The central action is simple—the pair gather, taste, and celebrate berries—but the book’s real focus is sound, repetition, and imaginative play. Bruce Degen’s text uses chantlike verse and playful word patterns that invite reading aloud, while the setting turns an ordinary summer outing into a nonsense-rich world of abundance. Themes of companionship, sensory delight, language, and childhood imagination shape this classic picture book.
book-7324: A teenage girl who has spent years seeing ghosts is sent to Lyle House, a group home for troubled youths, after a frightening public encounter with the dead. There she learns that the institution hides a secret experiment involving supernatural teens with dangerous abilities, including necromancy, sorcery, werewolf transformations, and clairvoyance. As Chloe Saunders and the other residents uncover surveillance, captivity, and manipulation by the Edison Group, they flee into forests, safe houses, and small-town streets while trying to understand their powers and decide whom to trust. The trilogy combines paranormal fantasy, horror, and suspense, focusing on identity, bodily change, friendship, betrayal, and the conflict between adult control and adolescent autonomy in a contemporary North American setting.
book-7325: On a world shaped by migration, war, and old magic, a gifted Singer named Rhapsody flees a brutal past and becomes entangled with two dangerous companions: a hardened assassin and a giant warrior marked by exile. Their escape carries them through hidden roots beneath the earth and into a transformed land where centuries have passed, nations have shifted, and ancient prophecies still exert force. As Rhapsody discovers that her voice can alter emotion, memory, and even the fabric of names, she is drawn into struggles involving sorcery, politics, and a rising threat tied to legendary evil. The novel combines quest fantasy, romantic tension, and court intrigue while exploring identity, trauma, friendship, and the burden of power in a realm where music and naming hold real consequence.
book-7326: Set in and around Harvard Medical School and Boston hospitals, this novel follows a cohort of gifted medical students as they move from anatomy labs and internships into demanding professional lives. The narrative centers on ambition, friendship, class difference, sexual rivalry, and the emotional cost of learning to heal. A brilliant woman fights for authority in a male-dominated profession, while her closest companion and eventual circle of colleagues confront competition, desire, marriage, illness, and ethical strain. Medical training provides the structure: dissections, examinations, wards, and emergency rooms shape the characters’ adult identities as strongly as family history does. The book treats medicine not only as science but as a social world where intellect, status, and private longing collide, and where success in the clinic does not simplify the heart.
book-7327: Set in eleventh-century Persia and extending into the early twentieth century, this historical novel follows the life and legend of Omar Khayyam, poet, astronomer, and skeptic, against the political upheavals of Seljuk Iran. Courts, observatories, gardens, and caravan cities frame encounters with Nizam al-Mulk and Hassan-i Sabbah, linking lyric verse to statecraft, religious zeal, and rebellion. A manuscript of the Rubaiyat becomes the thread connecting Khayyam’s world to a later narrator who traces its fate through Qajar Persia and the constitutional movement, toward exile and the Atlantic crossing of the Titanic. The narrative explores how poetry survives empires, how friendship turns into ideological conflict, and how memory, desire, and historical violence shape the stories civilizations preserve or lose.
book-7328: In a near-future New York City, homicide lieutenant Eve Dallas investigates a series of killings that appear random at first but reveal a chilling pattern. The victims are ordinary people selected by unseen predators who treat murder as a form of entertainment, turning the city into a playground for wealth, privilege, and cruelty. As Eve follows electronic traces, social connections, and carefully staged crime scenes, she confronts suspects whose money and influence shield them from ordinary scrutiny. Alongside the police investigation, her marriage to Roarke adds an intimate counterpoint of loyalty and trust under pressure. The novel combines procedural detection, romantic suspense, and thriller pacing while examining class power, boredom, sadism, and the dehumanizing effects of treating other lives as disposable.
book-7329: A girl named Darling grows up in a shantytown called Paradise in Zimbabwe, where hunger, demolished homes, political violence, and the stray promises of adults shape daily life. Alongside a sharp, unruly group of children, she scavenges guavas, witnesses street sermons and funerals, and tries to make sense of a country in crisis. The novel then follows her migration to the United States, where suburban Detroit offers safety and material abundance but also loneliness, undocumented precarity, and a painful distance from home. Moving between childhood immediacy and immigrant disillusion, it examines exile, language, class, race, and the gap between imagined America and lived reality. The narrative focuses on how migration alters family bonds, memory, and the possibility of belonging in either place.
book-733: On a small island in Puget Sound in 1954, a fisherman’s death leads to a murder trial that exposes the buried divisions of a close community. The accused, Kabuo Miyamoto, is a Japanese American veteran whose family history is entangled with local prejudice, wartime internment, and a disputed piece of farmland. As snow closes in on the island, the courtroom proceedings draw in a newspaper editor, former lovers, war memories, and long-simmering resentments between white and Japanese American residents. Moving between the trial and earlier decades, the novel examines racism, guilt, memory, justice, and the emotional aftermath of World War II. Its mystery structure is bound to a portrait of weather, landscape, and moral ambiguity in the Pacific Northwest.
book-7330: A bright red caboose rides at the end of a long freight train and feels overlooked beside the powerful black engine at the front. As the train crosses fields, towns, and mountain country, the caboose complains about being small, slow, and last, and wishes for the engine’s importance and praise. The story follows the train’s journey through a classic picture-book landscape while building a simple conflict about envy, purpose, and self-worth. When the train faces a steep mountain descent, the caboose’s brakes become essential to keeping the whole line of cars safe, revealing the specific job only it can do. Written for young children, the book uses repetition, rhythm, and talking train cars to explore usefulness, cooperation, and the dignity of every role in a community.
book-7331: Moving through the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s, this comic memoir follows Jen Lancaster from suburban childhood into early adulthood by way of the clothes she wears and the identities she tries on. Catholic school uniforms, plaid skirts, teen trends, office attire, and bridesmaid dresses become markers for family conflict, adolescent insecurity, ambition, friendship, and romance. Set largely in the American Midwest and in workplaces, schools, and social scenes that shape her, the narrative presents episodes about fitting in, rebelling, dating, and managing the gap between how she sees herself and how others see her. The central thread is self-invention: how fashion, class aspiration, and sharp self-scrutiny intersect as she remembers the embarrassing, funny, and revealing stages of growing up.
book-7332: Written for independent spiritual practice, this guide introduces modern Wicca as a nature-centered religion and magical tradition that can be followed outside a coven. It outlines core beliefs about divinity, ritual, ethics, the elements, lunar and seasonal cycles, and the use of tools such as candles, herbs, stones, and the athame. Practical chapters present methods for creating sacred space, casting circles, honoring sabbats and esbats, working simple spells, and keeping a personal Book of Shadows. The central argument holds that solitary worship can be disciplined, meaningful, and rooted in reverence for the natural world rather than secrecy or hierarchy. Themes include personal responsibility, ritual symbolism, intuition, ecological awareness, and the relationship between daily life and sacred practice.
book-7333: Set in the backyard of a prosperous family home in postwar America, this drama follows Joe Keller, a self-made manufacturer whose business success rests on a wartime scandal involving defective airplane parts. As his son Chris plans a future with Ann Deever, the former fiancée of Chris’s missing brother Larry, long-buried questions about guilt, responsibility, and family loyalty return with increasing force. The action unfolds over a single day, drawing together neighbors, parents, and children whose lives remain shaped by the Second World War. Through domestic conversation and mounting accusation, the play examines moral compromise, the human cost of profit, and the tension between private duty to one’s family and public duty to strangers. Themes include denial, accountability, grief, and the consequences of self-justification.
book-7334: Set over one night in suburban Melbourne, this young adult novel follows Lucy, an art-loving teenager who has built a private ideal around Shadow, the anonymous graffiti artist whose painted birds and blue landscapes haunt city walls. On the last night before school ends, she and her friends go looking for him through streets, train stations, parties, and alleyways marked by tags and murals. Instead, Lucy keeps crossing paths with Ed, a boy she dismisses as a hopeless slacker, while he hides a connection that could shatter her fantasy. Alternating perspectives trace misunderstandings, class tension, friendship, creative ambition, and the gap between the people imagined through art and the flawed people met in ordinary life. Humor and romance unfold against a vivid urban graffiti scene.
book-7335: Set in a village landscape inspired by southern Africa, this illustrated folktale follows Mufaro’s two daughters, who are famed for their beauty but differ sharply in character. Manyara is proud, cruel, and jealous, while Nyasha is gentle, hardworking, and kind to people, animals, and strangers. When the Great King announces that he will choose a wife, the sisters travel toward the city, each hoping to be selected. Along the road and at the king’s gate, they encounter unsettling tests that reveal their true natures. The story centers on rivalry within a family, the contrast between outward appearance and inward goodness, and the way humility, generosity, and respect shape destiny. Lush pictures and motifs from African oral tradition frame the narrative.
book-7336: Widowed royina Ista dy Chalion, long confined by court and family after a history of divine possession and supposed madness, leaves her household on a pilgrimage to escape surveillance and reclaim her own will. On the road and at a remote border castle, she encounters soldiers, nobles, and priests entangled in a violent legacy tied to the gods’ war against demons. As uncanny visitations return, Ista must decide whether she is cursed, chosen, or both, while navigating political loyalties, mourning, and an unexpected late-life attraction. Set in the World of the Five Gods, the novel combines court intrigue, theology, haunted landscapes, and military danger, with themes of spiritual vocation, female autonomy, trauma, age, and the difficult uses of mercy.
book-7337: Drawing on biographies of artists, scientists, inventors, and military leaders, this nonfiction work argues that mastery develops through a long apprenticeship rather than innate genius. It outlines a progression from disciplined observation and skill building to creative independence, using historical figures and contemporary examples to examine how people find their life’s task, learn from mentors, and absorb the hidden rules of a field. The central argument holds that focused practice, social intelligence, patience, and resilience turn expertise into original achievement. Set across workshops, laboratories, studios, and business careers, the book links personal vocation with professional development. Its themes include vocation, ambition, mentorship, deliberate practice, creativity, power, and the tension between conformity and individual vision.
book-7338: A deadpan comic premise sends a radio reporter on repeated trips to the afterlife, where Dr. Jack Kevorkian briefly stops and restarts his heart so he can interview the dead. In a series of short pieces, he meets figures from politics, literature, sports, music, and history, including Adolf Hitler, Isaac Asimov, William Shakespeare, and Princess Diana. The setting shifts between a clinical machine in the living world and a bureaucratic, oddly ordinary heaven populated by famous ghosts. Each encounter becomes a satirical exchange about war, fame, cruelty, art, poverty, and American public life at the end of the twentieth century. Blending speculative fiction, mock journalism, and black humor, the book uses the talk-show format to examine mortality, moral absurdity, and the thin border between celebrity culture and historical memory.
book-7339: Across essays anchored by recipes, a food memoir unfolds from a kitchen table outward to family history, travel, and adult self-discovery. Molly Wizenberg recounts childhood meals, her father’s unexpected death, time spent in Paris, and her move to Seattle, showing how dishes such as potato salad, stewed prunes, and chocolate cake become records of grief, love, friendship, and marriage. Domestic spaces, markets, restaurants, and small apartments form the setting for a narrative in which cooking is both daily practice and emotional language. The central movement follows a young woman learning how appetite, memory, and place shape a life. Themes include mourning, pleasure, independence, partnership, and the way recipes preserve intimate stories while inviting new forms of belonging.
book-734: Beginning in eighteenth-century Gambia, the narrative follows Kunta Kinte, a young Mandinka man captured by slave traders and transported across the Atlantic, then traces his descendants through plantations, the Civil War era, and Reconstruction into the twentieth century. Across generations, mothers, fathers, and children confront enslavement, forced separation, racial violence, and the pressure to surrender language, religion, and kinship ties. The story moves between West African village life and the American South, linking personal memory to larger histories of the slave trade and Black survival in the United States. Family names, oral tradition, resistance, labor, and the search for ancestry shape a multigenerational account of identity, inheritance, and the long struggle to preserve human dignity under slavery and its aftermath.
book-7340: A wolf blows down the first pig’s straw house, but the familiar nursery tale breaks apart when the pigs step out of their own story and wander through the white space between pages. They fold paper into airplanes, slip into other stories, and gather companions from different illustrated worlds, including a dragon and a cat with a fiddle. The setting shifts from the traditional fairy-tale countryside to comic panels, wordless page margins, and borrowed scenes from nursery rhymes, with artwork changing style as the pigs travel. The central conflict lies in escaping the fixed plot that expects them to be eaten and in choosing how their story will end. Themes include imagination, metafiction, freedom, and playful awareness of how books are made.
book-7341: Drawing on clinical psychology and behavioral research, this work argues that people can replace habitual pessimism with a more resilient explanatory style. Martin E.P. Seligman presents learned optimism as a practical response to depression, setbacks, workplace stress, illness, and everyday disappointment. The book explains how thoughts about permanence, pervasiveness, and personal responsibility shape emotion and action, then offers exercises for identifying self-defeating beliefs and disputing them with evidence. Case studies and questionnaires connect cognitive habits to achievement in school, business, sports, and health. Set within the framework of late twentieth-century psychology, its central concern is whether outlook is fixed or trainable. Themes include resilience, motivation, mental health, self-talk, and the relationship between interpretation and behavior.
book-7342: Teenager Violet Ambrose returns to small-town Washington carrying the trauma of a murder investigation and the dangerous secret of her unusual ability: she can sense dead bodies and the lingering echoes attached to killers. As she tries to settle back into school, family life, and her intense relationship with Jay Heaton, new disturbances pull her toward another case. Anonymous messages, missing girls, and violent psychic impressions suggest that a predator is still at work, while the authorities remain uncertain about what she knows. The novel combines paranormal mystery with young adult romance, placing questions of trust, fear, and responsibility at its center. Set between classrooms, wooded back roads, and crime scenes, it follows Violet as she balances first love, grief, and the burden of seeing what others cannot.
book-7343: A family of tiny people lives hidden within the walls and floorboards of an ordinary house, surviving by borrowing pins, spools, buttons, and other small objects from the human family above them. The Littles keep strict rules about secrecy, because discovery by “Bigg” people could destroy their carefully ordered world. Their quiet routine is threatened when signs suggest that the house may be sold and a new occupant might expose their home. As they search the attic, cupboards, and hidden passages for a safer future, the story turns everyday domestic spaces into a landscape of danger and invention. The novel centers on miniature adventure, family cooperation, resourcefulness, and the tension between curiosity about humans and the need to remain unseen.
book-7344: Literal-minded Amelia Bedelia sets out to help prepare a surprise shower, but her habit of taking every instruction at face value turns ordinary party tasks into comic confusion. In a domestic small-town setting of kitchens, shops, and party preparations, she follows directions exactly as she hears them, misunderstanding common idioms and social customs. As she shops, decorates, and gets ready for the event, language itself becomes the central source of conflict: everyday phrases mean one thing to the adults around her and something entirely different to Amelia Bedelia. The story uses repetition, wordplay, and household details to build humor while introducing young readers to double meanings in English. Themes include communication, interpretation, helpfulness, and the gap between what people say and what they mean.
book-7345: After their unstable mother abandons them in a shopping-center parking lot, thirteen-year-old Dicey Tillerman takes charge of her three younger siblings and starts south on foot in search of a great-aunt in rural Maryland. Their journey moves through highways, campgrounds, bus stations, and unfamiliar towns, where money runs short and every choice carries risk. Dicey must find food, shelter, and a way to keep the family together while protecting James, Maybeth, and Sammy from authorities and from people she cannot fully trust. The novel follows a child-led odyssey across the eastern United States and centers on survival, responsibility, family loyalty, and the hard balance between independence and the need for home.
book-7346: A dark druid curse, a shape-shifting mirror, and a clash between sixteenth-century Scotland and the modern world drive this paranormal romance. Jessi St. James, a scholar of Celtic artifacts, becomes entangled with Cian MacKeltar, a Highland laird trapped for centuries in enchanted isolation and bound to dangerous magic. As ancient enemies maneuver for control of druid power, the pair move between misted castles, hidden chambers, and contemporary city streets, trying to break a spell that distorts time, desire, and memory. The central conflict turns on whether love and trust can survive deception, sorcery, and the violent legacy of clan warfare. Themes include fate, captivity, erotic obsession, magical inheritance, and the pull of Scotland’s mythic past into the present.
book-7347: Across a universe shattered into separate elemental realms, the struggle between the Sartan and the Patryns grows more dangerous as Haplo, a Patryn voyager, moves deeper into the designs of his imprisoned people. The action centers on Arianus, the realm of air, where floating islands, elven cities, human kingdoms, and assassin politics create a brittle balance of power. As old rivalries sharpen into war, Alfred, the hesitant Sartan, and other returning figures are drawn into competing loyalties, secret histories, and the mystery of the Death Gate itself. The novel combines quest fantasy with science-fantasy worldbuilding, using magical labyrinths, dragon-snakes, rune magic, and imperial schemes to explore mistrust, manipulation, racial hatred, and the cost of obedience to ancient vengeance.
book-7348: Sports agent and sometime investigator Myron Bolitar is drawn into a kidnapping case when WNBA star Brenda Slaughter asks for help after her father vanishes and a ransom demand arrives. The search pulls Myron through the world of professional basketball, celebrity contracts, tabloid scrutiny, and old family secrets, while his sharp-tongued ally Win works his own ruthless angles. Set between arenas, suburban homes, and New York streets, the novel balances puzzle plotting with dry humor and sudden violence. As Myron follows conflicting clues, he confronts questions of loyalty, race, class, and the hidden costs of fame. The central conflict turns on whether Brenda’s family history, her rising career, or something far more dangerous lies behind the abduction and the threats closing in around her.
book-7349: Recovering from betrayal and imprisonment, Corwin of Amber returns to the one true royal city at the center of a multiverse of shadow worlds, where rival siblings scheme for the throne and a cosmic war looms. Determined to reclaim power from his brother Eric, he turns to Shadow in search of a way to bring firearms and modern weapons into Amber, where ordinary gunpowder fails. His quest carries him through shifting realities, from contemporary Earth to eerie courts and battlefields shaped by will, memory, and bloodline. The novel combines family intrigue, parallel-world travel, and military preparation with a first-person voice that is sharp, suspicious, and wounded. Themes include legitimacy, revenge, identity, and the unstable line between strategic ambition and obsession.
book-735: A violent confrontation in Gotham City centers on the escalating struggle between Batman and the Joker, framing their feud as a contest between order and chaos. The story follows the Joker after an escape from Arkham Asylum as he launches a calculated attack aimed at Commissioner James Gordon and those close to him, forcing Batman into a race across amusement parks, carnival rides, and rain-soaked city streets. Intercut scenes sketch a possible origin for the Joker, linking crime, humiliation, and one disastrous day. Brian Bolland’s detailed artwork and stark urban settings emphasize menace, theatricality, and psychological pressure. The graphic novel explores madness, trauma, moral limits, and the fear that catastrophe can erase the boundary between hero, villain, and victim.
book-7350: Strong-willed, sharp-tongued Gilly Hopkins arrives in yet another foster home expecting to outsmart the adults and leave as soon as she can reunite with the glamorous mother she idolizes. Placed with warm, unconventional Trotter, alongside a shy foster brother and an elderly blind neighbor, she brings defiance, class prejudice, and carefully guarded loneliness into a small-town household. At school and at home she tests every bond, using wit and cruelty to protect herself from disappointment. The novel follows her struggle between fantasy and reality as she confronts abandonment, disability, race, poverty, and the meaning of family. Themes of belonging, trust, resentment, and emotional resilience shape this realistic middle-grade story about foster care and chosen connections.
book-7351: Across the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, marine engineer and investigator Dirk Pitt follows a chain of incidents that links modern sabotage, vanished ships, and an ancient seafaring mystery reaching back to the aftermath of the Trojan War. The novel moves through shipwreck sites, corporate compounds, coastal cities, and underwater ruins as Pitt and the NUMA team confront a powerful industrial dynasty with plans hidden behind shipping wealth and scientific expertise. Their search joins archaeology, oceanography, and espionage, with clues drawn from Homeric legend, Phoenician trade routes, and relics long buried at sea. Central tension comes from the effort to decode the past before a contemporary conspiracy alters global power. Themes include maritime history, greed, environmental danger, technological control, and the persistence of myth in modern geopolitics.
book-7352: On the eighteenth-century American frontier, a young settler woman is captured in a Shawnee raid on the Virginia backcountry and forced westward through wilderness and village life far from her family. Drawing on the historical story of Mary Ingles, the novel follows her resolve to escape and travel home through forests, mountains, rivers, hunger, and winter weather. The central conflict lies in her struggle to survive the brutal journey while navigating fear, injury, and the uncertain boundaries between Native communities and colonial settlers during the French and Indian War era. Frontier cabins, trading paths, and the Ohio Valley landscape shape a narrative concerned with endurance, captivity, homecoming, and the physical demands of crossing an often hostile continent with little food, shelter, or guidance.
book-7353: Set in Vienna, this play follows a crisis of law, sexuality, and political authority after Duke Vincentio withdraws from public rule and leaves the severe Angelo in charge. Angelo revives long-neglected moral statutes, condemning the young Claudio to death for fornication, which drives Claudio’s sister Isabella, a novice preparing for convent life, to plead for mercy. Her appeal exposes a central conflict between rigid justice and human frailty when Angelo’s private desire collides with his public righteousness. Through disguises, secret tests, prison scenes, and comic subplots involving bawds, officers, and petty criminals, the drama examines corruption, hypocrisy, chastity, punishment, and mercy. Written as one of Shakespeare’s problem plays, it combines dark comedy with ethical debate about power, gender, and the uneasy administration of justice.
book-7354: A prosperous American couple offer shelter to a frightened young woman who appears on their doorstep with no clear past, no family, and a childlike vulnerability. As she settles into their orderly household, accidents and acts of violence begin to gather around her, and ordinary domestic space turns threatening. The story moves between suburban interiors, police inquiry, and the hidden history that seems to shadow the newcomer, building a mystery around identity, trauma, and whether evil can wear an innocent face. Part suspense novel and part horror tale, it centers on a family trying to protect itself while uncovering who the stranger really is and why terror follows her. Themes include memory, deception, obsession, and the thin boundary between safety and menace.
book-7355: In a near-future world shaped by secret laboratories and time travel, two teenage girls confront the same catastrophe from different points in its timeline. One lives as a captive in a bleak future, where a brilliant boy’s invention has fueled war and dictatorship; the other moves through an ordinary high school life, unaware that her choices are tied to that same device. As timelines loop and collide, each girl must decide whether to trust love, friendship, or her own memory. The novel centers on attempts to prevent the creation of a time machine and the moral cost of changing history. It explores identity, causality, manipulation, and the fear that saving the world may require destroying the person one loves.
book-7356: A memoir of adolescence shaped by parental hoarding, this narrative follows a girl who grows up in New York apartments crowded with trash bags, broken objects, and secrecy. She moves through school, friendships, and first love while trying to hide the condition of her home and the instability it creates. The central struggle lies between fierce loyalty to her parents and her need for order, honesty, and a life not defined by clutter. Family dysfunction, shame, anxiety, and resilience remain at the center, alongside practical insight into the emotional patterns of hoarding and the children who live with it. Written for teen and adult readers, it presents a personal account of mental illness, class appearance, and the difficult work of separating identity from a parent’s disorder.
book-7357: Set in Restoration England after the return of Charles II, this historical novel follows Amber St. Clare, an orphaned village girl who rises through the volatile world of London court society. She moves from country innocence to the capital’s theaters, plague streets, noble houses, and royal circles, using beauty, ambition, and wit to survive. Her pursuit of wealth, status, and lasting love drives a series of shifting alliances and romantic entanglements, while the era’s political instability, social display, and sexual double standards shape every choice. Against a background of the English court, the Great Plague, and the Great Fire of London, the narrative examines desire, class mobility, power, and the costs of chasing security in a society ruled by reputation and favor.
book-7358: Three orphaned siblings—Kate, Michael, and Emma—are sent to the isolated town of Cambridge Falls, where a crumbling mansion and a hidden volume called the Emerald Atlas pull them into an old struggle over magic and power. When the book reveals an ability to send them through time, they uncover the town’s buried history, the disappearance of children, and the rule of a sinister Countess who feeds on fear. As they search for clues about their parents and their own place in a larger prophecy, the children face wolves, dwarves, and dangerous enchantments. Set in a fairy-tale world with castles, underground passages, and temporal puzzles, the novel centers on sibling loyalty, courage, loss, and the burden of changing the past without destroying the future.
book-7359: Growing up in northwest London, two brown girls bond over dance lessons, old movie musicals, and an ambitious idea of escape, even as class, talent, and family history divide them. One becomes a gifted performer; the other, restless and observant, moves through schools, friendships, and later a job assisting a famous singer whose philanthropic project unfolds in West Africa. The novel shifts between council estates, celebrity circles, and a Gambian village to trace how race, money, motherhood, and cultural inheritance shape lives. Through fractured friendship, absent fathers, political idealism, and performance itself, it examines imitation and authenticity, the uses of art, and the uneasy power relations that connect London and Africa, private longing and public virtue.
book-736: A young Black narrator moves from the American South to Harlem, tracing a painful passage through college, factory labor, political organizing, and urban unrest. Anonymous and repeatedly misseen by those around him, he confronts white benefactors, Black leaders, union men, and a revolutionary Brotherhood that each claims to define his role. The novel follows his struggle to build an identity in a society structured by racism, spectacle, and power, while exposing the social masks imposed by ideology and stereotype. Set against the segregated South and the charged streets of mid-20th-century New York, it examines visibility, alienation, betrayal, and the costs of speaking in one’s own voice. Ellison combines realist scenes with surreal episodes to explore race, individuality, and American democracy.
book-7360: During the final days of the Second World War, the heavy cruiser USS Indianapolis completes a secret mission delivering components for the atomic bomb, then is torpedoed in the Philippine Sea and sinks within minutes. Hundreds of sailors are left in open water for days, facing dehydration, exposure, delirium, salt poisoning, and shark attacks while rescue is delayed by naval miscommunication and ignored distress signals. The narrative follows the ship’s voyage, the attack by a Japanese submarine, the ordeal of the scattered survivors, and the aftermath, including questions of command responsibility and the court-martial of Captain Charles McVay. Drawing on interviews, military records, and survivor testimony, it examines courage, endurance, trauma, and the failures of wartime bureaucracy that turned a naval disaster into one of the deadliest sea tragedies in U.S. history.
book-7361: At a modern Japanese high school, Karin Maaka tries to hide an embarrassing family secret: she comes from a household of vampires, yet instead of feeding on blood, she produces too much of it. Her condition causes sudden nosebleeds and forces her to seek out someone to give blood to, turning traditional vampire lore into a comic source of trouble. Daily life grows more complicated when a new transfer student, Kenta Usui, seems to trigger her attacks and may notice that something is wrong. The volume follows Karin as she balances school routines, her eccentric supernatural family, and the beginnings of a romance shaped by secrecy. Themes include identity, adolescent embarrassment, family expectations, and the playful collision of horror motifs with romantic comedy.
book-7362: Set in contemporary Los Angeles, this young adult novel follows Emi Price, a talented set designer who is more comfortable arranging fictional spaces than navigating her own feelings. While handling an estate sale for a legendary film figure, she and her best friend uncover a letter that points toward an unknown granddaughter, drawing Emi into a small mystery tied to old Hollywood history. The search leads her to Ava, an ambitious young woman whose presence unsettles Emi’s carefully ordered life. As attraction grows, Emi must confront grief, family expectations, artistic identity, and the difference between creating perfect scenes and living honestly inside them. Themes of first love, queer identity, friendship, and the glamour and artifice of the film industry shape the story.
book-7363: On the eve of his thirteenth birthday, Jeremy Fink receives a locked wooden box left by his father, who has died, with a note promising that it contains the meaning of life. The box has four keyholes, but the keys are missing, and Jeremy and his impulsive friend Lizzy set out across New York City to find them before his birthday ends. Their search leads through pawnshops, eccentric apartments, and subway rides, while Jeremy’s careful, anxious nature clashes with Lizzy’s appetite for risk. Beneath the mystery puzzle, the novel follows a grieving family and a boy trying to understand his father’s absence. Themes of friendship, loss, memory, growing up, and what gives ordinary days value shape this middle-grade adventure.
book-7364: A young girl named Trisha grows up in a family that treasures stories, drawing, and school, but she cannot make sense of the letters and words that seem to “dance” on the page. As she moves from class to class, her difficulty with reading brings confusion, shame, and bullying from other children, even while her talent for art remains clear. Set in elementary school and rooted in Patricia Polacco’s own childhood, the story follows Trisha’s growing frustration until a compassionate teacher, Mr. Falker, recognizes her dyslexia and gives her the patient, direct help she needs. The picture book centers on literacy, learning differences, perseverance, and the life-changing effect of a teacher who sees a child’s hidden struggle and dignity.
book-7365: In a near-future rural American South marked by debt, military veterans, and 3D fabrication, Flynne Fisher earns money by playing security in virtual environments for other people. While filling in for her brother on a high-paying job, she witnesses a violent event that seems too vivid to be a game. The incident links her world to a drastically different London decades ahead, where extreme wealth, social collapse, and advanced technology have remade daily life. As people in both timelines begin to pursue her, the novel follows brokers, fixers, hackers, and families navigating an asymmetric connection across time. The story examines surveillance, class power, corporate secrecy, and the human cost of treating bodies, labor, and whole communities as disposable peripherals.
book-7366: Across a group of stories set largely in small-town Ontario and other ordinary domestic landscapes, women and men confront decisive turns in marriage, family life, work, illness, and memory. A waitress, a child, an aging spouse, and other sharply observed figures move through kitchens, train stations, sickrooms, and rented houses where old choices return with new force. One story reaches to the nineteenth-century mathematician Sofia Kovalevsky, extending the collection beyond contemporary Canada while keeping its focus on desire, intellect, secrecy, and loss. The central drama in these narratives lies in how private lives are altered by accident, betrayal, social constraint, and sudden knowledge. Themes include female autonomy, class, aging, mortality, and the unstable meanings people give to happiness.
book-7367: At a wedding in Lake Tahoe, photographer Madison Daniels tries to keep her life orderly and avoid the kind of reckless mistake that could cost her career and reputation. The problem is Chase Gamble, the groom’s brother and best man, a wealthy contractor with a blunt mouth, a flirt’s confidence, and a reputation Madison has no interest in testing. After a single impulsive night leaves them tangled together, proximity and gossip make distance difficult, and Madison must decide whether Chase is only trouble or something more dependable than his bad-boy image suggests. The novel follows a contemporary romance built on sexual tension, banter, family weddings, and public scrutiny, while exploring trust, vulnerability, class assumptions, and the risk of wanting a real relationship when both people expect disappointment.
book-7368: Set in rival Mediterranean-style courts shaped by slavery, dynastic politics, and border war, this fantasy romance follows Damianos, the exiled heir of Akielos, as he remains hidden in the Veretian prince Laurent’s entourage after being sent there as a political captive. A fragile alliance forces the two men to travel through hostile territory, negotiate with nobles, and confront assassination plots, raids, and court intrigue while preparing for a larger military threat. The central conflict turns on whether Damen can protect his identity and claim, and whether Laurent can trust the man tied to his brother’s murder and his country’s enemy. Themes of power, loyalty, manipulation, consent, and desire run through a story focused on strategy, uneasy dependence, and a slow shift from enmity toward intimacy.
book-7369: In contemporary New York literary circles and hidden private rooms, notorious erotica writer Nora Sutherlin balances public success with a secret life shaped by BDSM, devotion, and old wounds. When her publisher assigns a young, inexperienced editor, Zachary Easton, to work on her new manuscript, professional collaboration turns into emotional tension as he is drawn toward a world that unsettles his faith and assumptions. At the same time, Nora remains bound to Søren, a powerful priest whose past and authority complicate every new attachment, while a younger lover offers a different kind of refuge. The novel centers on desire, consent, spiritual conflict, control, and the cost of intimacy, tracing how art, religion, and sexuality become entangled in relationships marked by longing, shame, and dependence.
book-737: Amid the civil war in Sierra Leone, a twelve-year-old boy is driven from his village and separated from his family as rebel attacks spread through the countryside. The memoir follows Ishmael Beah’s movement through forests, roads, and refugee centers as hunger, fear, and grief shape daily survival. It then traces his forced recruitment into the government army, where military training, drugs, and violence transform children into soldiers. Alongside scenes of combat and displacement, the narrative examines trauma, memory, revenge, and the erosion of childhood under war. Later chapters turn to rehabilitation and testimony, showing the difficult effort to reclaim identity and language after atrocity. The book combines personal witness with historical context about Sierra Leone’s conflict and the use of child soldiers.
book-7370: Set in Albany, New York, during the Depression, the novel follows Francis Phelan, a former baseball player, day laborer, and drifter who returns to the city after years of homelessness. He moves through graveyards, rail yards, cheap bars, and flophouses, accompanied by Helen, a singer and fellow itinerant, while confronting the family and neighborhood he abandoned. The central conflict lies in Francis’s struggle with guilt, memory, and the damage caused by poverty, drink, and violence, especially the death that drove him away. Ghosts, hallucinations, and street-corner encounters give the city a haunted texture as the narrative examines shame, survival, Irish American working-class life, and the fragile line between dignity and ruin in hard times.
book-7371: A brutal killing in Los Angeles draws psychologist Alex Delaware back into police work alongside LAPD lieutenant Milo Sturgis. The case begins with a seemingly straightforward homicide, but witness statements, social connections, and hidden histories quickly fracture into competing versions of the truth. Moving through mansions, offices, and guarded family circles, Alex uses clinical insight to read behavior while Milo follows physical evidence and motive. Their investigation turns on deception in many forms: false identities, buried relationships, self-protection, and the stories people tell to preserve status. Set in contemporary Southern California, the novel combines procedural detection with psychological suspense, focusing on how wealth, secrecy, and damaged loyalties shape violence and obstruct justice.
book-7372: A lightly satirical, observational diary of a damply confident British clerk navigating everyday life in late-Victorian London, the book follows a well-meaning but self-conscious narrator through household chores, social visits, small triumphs, and comic misfortunes. The diary format captures a gentle, incremental strategy of self-presentation as he records conversations with family, acquaintances, and neighbors, along with the minor embarrassments of work, leisure, and etiquette. The central tension arises from the narrator’s earnest wish to belong and be admired within a bustling commercial world that feels alien and fussy, prompting lingering self-doubt, modest aspirations, and a series of cameos by a cast of polite, eccentric, and sometimes intrusive characters. Themes include class manners, urban routine, aspirations, and the soft satire of ordinary domestic life in a social world of proprieties.
book-7373: As war gathers across the faerie lands of Prythian, Feyre returns to the Spring Court under false pretenses after the betrayal that shattered fragile alliances. She must gather intelligence, navigate courtly deception, and decide whom she can trust while Hybern’s invading forces threaten every court and the human realm beyond the wall. The novel moves through palaces, battle camps, and ancient territories, combining high fantasy warfare with an intense central romance between Feyre and Rhysand. Its conflict centers on political loyalty, revenge, survival, and the cost of power as rival High Lords, mortal queens, and old enemies pursue competing visions of freedom and dominion. Themes include trauma and recovery, found family, sacrifice, female agency, and the uneasy balance between love, duty, and leadership.
book-7374: Magic exists behind the ordinary streets of Ireland, where teenager Valkyrie Cain works with the living skeleton detective Skulduggery Pleasant to police sorcerers, monsters, and secret cults. As a new threat gathers, followers of the ancient Faceless Ones try to open a path for their gods to return, while political distrust and old rivalries weaken the magical community from within. Valkyrie balances school, family secrecy, and her growing skill in elemental magic as she is drawn into battles with assassins, grotesque creatures, and forbidden knowledge. The novel combines urban fantasy, horror, and detective adventure, centering on loyalty, courage, inherited darkness, and the cost of power when a hidden world edges toward invasion and collapse.
book-7375: A long rail journey carries the narrator from London through Europe, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent, and Southeast Asia, then onward to Japan and back across Siberia on the Trans-Siberian Railway. Part travel memoir and part social observation, the narrative records station platforms, sleeping cars, border crossings, dining compartments, and the shifting talk of fellow passengers met along the route. Cities, deserts, mountains, and ports appear through the confined, rhythmic perspective of train travel, with close attention to timetables, discomfort, delay, and the peculiar intimacy of shared compartments. The central movement is both geographic and inward, as the journey tests expectations about distance, foreignness, and motion itself. Themes include displacement, colonial afterlives, solitude, curiosity, and the romance and fatigue of overland travel in the modern world.
book-7376: After a series of violent incidents in Paris, Norway, and the Mediterranean, counterterrorism operative Scot Harvath traces the attacks to a clandestine network working across Europe and the United States. As intelligence fragments point toward a coordinated plot against American targets, he follows financiers, extremists, and political fixers through safe houses, embassies, and private compounds. The investigation turns on a hidden roster known as the “black list,” where names function as both warning and weapon. Operating outside normal channels, Harvath confronts kidnappings, assassinations, and competing agendas inside the national security establishment. Set in a post-9/11 landscape of covert operations and international surveillance, the novel centers on preemptive violence, state secrecy, loyalty, and the difficulty of identifying the enemy when terror networks and official power intersect.
book-7377: In a vast future City crowded with polluted streets, body modification clinics, media manipulation, and political spectacle, journalist Spider Jerusalem wages a personal campaign against corruption with obscene wit and relentless reporting. This volume follows his return to public life as he writes incendiary columns, clashes with police and editors, and digs into abuses hidden behind campaign slogans and official press releases. Episodic investigations move through slums, television studios, apartments, and government offices, building a portrait of urban life shaped by inequality, technology, and exhausted civic institutions. Darick Robertson’s dense, grimy artwork supports a satirical science-fiction narrative about power, propaganda, and the ethics of journalism, while the humor stays caustic, profane, and tied to anger at systems that turn citizens into spectators.
book-7378: Bob Howard works as a computational demonologist for a secret British agency known as the Laundry, a bureaucracy that treats occult threats as information-security problems. In a near-future London where advanced mathematics can open gateways to hostile dimensions, he is pulled from desk work into field operations after a stolen notebook and a compromised computer program point to an attempt to summon apocalyptic entities. The novel combines espionage procedure, office satire, and cosmic horror, following briefings, surveillance, and occult countermeasures through government corridors, research labs, and hidden ritual sites. Its central conflict pits civil servants and intelligence officers against cultists, rogue researchers, and the catastrophic consequences of forbidden knowledge. Themes include bureaucracy, technology as magic, institutional secrecy, and the fragility of reality in the face of incomprehensible forces.
book-7379: Daniel Pecan Cambridge narrates a comic, melancholy account of life organized by severe compulsions and private rules. Living largely inside his Los Angeles apartment, he counts steps, avoids cracks, worries over symmetry, and turns everyday errands into elaborate mental negotiations. The novel follows his attempts to manage obsessive routines while reaching toward connection through neighbors, therapists, and a woman who draws him beyond his carefully measured boundaries. Beneath the humor, the story examines loneliness, anxiety, self-invention, and the fragile distance between eccentricity and illness. Set in ordinary streets, shops, and domestic rooms, it presents an intimate portrait of a man whose intelligence and wit coexist with disabling fear, using his skewed perceptions to explore how people seek order, companionship, and dignity in a confusing world.
book-738: Widowed field mouse Mrs. Frisby faces a winter crisis when her youngest son lies dangerously ill and her family cannot move from their cinder-block home before the farmer’s plow destroys it. Seeking help, she enters a hidden society of extraordinarily intelligent rats living beneath the rosebush on the Fitzgibbon farm. Their secret traces back to NIMH, a laboratory where rats and mice were altered by scientific experiments and learned to read, plan, and question how they should live. As Mrs. Frisby navigates owls, cats, tractors, and farmyard dangers, the story joins animal adventure with ethical questions about technology, survival, community, and responsibility. The novel presents a rural setting of fields, barns, and hedgerows shaped by both natural threat and human intervention.
book-7380: London in 1540 forms the backdrop for a Tudor mystery in which lawyer Matthew Shardlake is drawn into the dangerous politics of Henry VIII’s court. Pressured by Thomas Cromwell, he investigates the supposed discovery of “dark fire,” a lost Greek incendiary weapon that could alter military power and royal favor. At the same time, he defends a teenage girl accused of murder, moving through prisons, guild halls, river wharves, and noble households to uncover what links the cases. The novel combines legal inquiry, religious upheaval, and court intrigue during the dissolution era, tracing how fear, corruption, and ambition shape justice. Themes include conscience under tyranny, the abuse of power, and the risks faced by those who seek truth in a violent, suspicious state.
book-7381: On the eve of their wedding, driven executives Chloe Mills and Bennett Ryan try to balance work, family expectations, and their relentless attraction as they prepare to marry in San Diego. The novella follows the couple through rehearsals, last-minute complications, and a honeymoon in which old habits of competition and provocation collide with the new realities of commitment. Set between boardrooms, hotel suites, and beachside luxury, the story centers on whether two intensely independent people can turn a volatile, erotic relationship into a stable marriage without losing the spark that defines them. Themes of trust, desire, partnership, and the comedy of planning a public ceremony shape this contemporary romance, with banter, sexual tension, and affectionate conflict driving the plot.
book-7382: In contemporary Brooklyn and Yonkers, two isolated lives move toward an uneasy connection. Arthur Opp, a reclusive former academic, has not left his house in years and lives with extreme obesity, surviving through routines, old books, and letters. Kel Keller, a large, gifted teenager from a struggling family, tries to balance school, baseball, and the demands of his distant mother, Charlene, a former student Arthur once knew. As Arthur and Kel begin corresponding, the novel traces loneliness, shame, class strain, hunger, and the ways bodies shape how people are seen and treated. Domestic spaces, city streets, school corridors, and the baseball field become settings for a quiet story about secrecy, care, and the possibility of human contact across age, circumstance, and long-buried regret.
book-7383: At Redwall Abbey, a newborn ferret is taken in and named Veil Sixclaw, but his presence unsettles the mice, otters, and other woodland creatures who remember the cruelty of vermin armies. As Veil grows, suspicion hardens into open conflict, raising questions about whether character is shaped by birth, choice, or the judgments of a community. Beyond the abbey walls, a young badger, Sunflash the Mace, travels through forests, marshes, and coasts while confronting slavers and war bands that threaten the peaceful lands around Mossflower. The novel moves between feast halls, river paths, and battles with searat and ferret foes, combining adventure with themes of belonging, prejudice, loyalty, and the difficult line between mercy and justice in a world of talking animals.
book-7384: On the island of Bougainville during the civil war in Papua New Guinea, teenage Matilda Laimo watches her village shrink under blockade, soldiers, and fear. The local school reopens under the guidance of Mr. Watts, the last white man left on the island, who reads Charles Dickens’s Great Expectations aloud to a room of children with few books and fewer certainties. As Pip becomes vivid in Matilda’s mind, the novel’s world collides with the realities of hunger, patrols, and suspicion. The story follows how reading shapes memory, desire, and selfhood in a place marked by colonial history and violence. Themes of storytelling, education, racial difference, maternal authority, and the costs of survival run through this coming-of-age historical novel.
book-7385: Italian-American home cooking shapes this cookbook’s approach to shared meals, presenting recipes and menus designed for weeknights, holidays, and casual gatherings. Giada De Laurentiis organizes dishes around the structure of family dinners, with antipasti, pasta, meat, fish, vegetable sides, and desserts that balance speed with freshness. The emphasis falls on accessible ingredients, clear preparation, and the role of the table as a daily family ritual rather than a formal performance. Headnotes and menu suggestions connect food to domestic routines, entertaining, and the traditions of Italian kitchens adapted to contemporary American life. Themes include hospitality, seasonality, kitchen efficiency, and the way cooking creates continuity across generations through familiar sauces, roasts, salads, and sweets.
book-7386: Set in a Bronx Catholic school in 1964, this play stages a moral and institutional crisis after Sister Aloysius, the severe principal, comes to suspect Father Flynn, a popular parish priest, of improper conduct with Donald Muller, the school’s first Black student. Sister James, a young teacher, wavers between trust and alarm as the accusation sharpens into a struggle over evidence, authority, and conscience. The action unfolds through tense conversations rather than overt revelation, keeping facts uncertain and motives contested. Questions of faith, guilt, gendered power, race, clerical hierarchy, and the costs of certainty drive the drama. By withholding definitive proof, the play examines how suspicion forms, how institutions protect themselves, and how doubt can unsettle both conviction and justice.
book-7387: In a contemporary American high school, sixteen-year-old Morgan Rowlands feels ordinary until a charismatic new student, Cal Blaire, introduces her to Wicca and a small circle that practices rituals, meditation, and spellwork. As Morgan studies covens, sacred tools, and the ethics of magic, she experiences unexpected power and a new sense of belonging, but the discovery unsettles her friendships, her family life, and her understanding of who she is. Suspicion, attraction, and secrecy shape the story as she tries to distinguish spiritual practice from manipulation and to decide whom she can trust. Set in a suburban world of classrooms, bedrooms, and nighttime gatherings, the novel explores adolescence, religion, female power, desire, and the risks of hidden knowledge.
book-7388: Set in contemporary Washington, D.C., this romantic comedy follows women linked by an obsession with shoes as careers, friendships, and love lives grow tangled. The story centers on a fast-moving social world of boutiques, offices, dates, and city apartments, where appearances can conceal debt, insecurity, and private schemes. As relationships shift and old secrets surface, the novel uses a light mystery thread to explore what people hide from friends, lovers, and even themselves. Harbison focuses on female friendship, consumer desire, class aspiration, and the gap between polished surfaces and messy reality. Humor drives scenes of shopping, gossip, and romantic misunderstanding, while the central conflict asks whether honesty and self-knowledge can matter more than status, style, and the fantasy of a perfect life.
book-7389: As Tessa Young and Hardin Scott try to build a future together, their relationship faces new strain from family secrets, career choices, and the damage left by repeated betrayal. The story moves between college life, apartments, and family homes as Tessa considers leaving for Seattle, while Hardin struggles with anger, jealousy, and revelations about his past. Their intense attraction remains strong, but trust proves fragile, and each argument forces them to confront questions about independence, forgiveness, and whether love can survive emotional volatility. Centered on an on-again, off-again romance, the novel explores toxic patterns, class differences, family dysfunction, and the uneasy transition from adolescence to adult commitment. It presents a contemporary young adult romance shaped by desire, conflict, and the consequences of intimate choices.
book-739: Four novellas trace private obsessions, buried crimes, and hard-won acts of endurance across ordinary American settings. In a Maine prison, a banker forms an unlikely friendship and clings to dignity under a brutal penal system. In suburbia, an intelligent teenager discovers that an elderly neighbor once served the Nazi death camps, and their secret binds predator and witness in escalating moral corruption. During a summer in small-town New England, four boys set out along railroad tracks to find a dead child, confronting class, fear, and the end of innocence. In a Manhattan doctors’ club, a physician recounts a winter tale of pregnancy, secrecy, and physical ordeal. Together the stories examine confinement, guilt, storytelling, memory, and the thin line between civility and violence.
book-7390: Set in New York’s Little Italy in the early twentieth century, this historical novel follows an Italian immigrant family struggling to build a life on Elizabeth Street after arriving from Sicily. As crowded tenements, street markets, church rituals, and factory labor shape daily existence, old-world customs collide with American pressures and neighborhood crime. At the center is a family crisis involving danger to a child and a woman’s search for help in a community divided between superstition, loyalty, and suspicion. The narrative traces immigration, poverty, marriage, motherhood, and the fragile networks that sustain newcomers in an unfamiliar city. Blending domestic drama with mystery elements, it depicts the textures of immigrant life and the fear, resilience, and cultural memory carried across the Atlantic.
book-7391: In the port city of Skull’s Bay, teenage assassin Celaena Sardothien arrives with fellow assassin Sam Cortland on an assignment from the King of the Assassins, Arobynn Hamel. Their mission appears to be a routine meeting with Pirate Lord Rolfe over a lucrative deal, but Celaena discovers that the transaction centers on human trafficking and enslaved people bound for forced labor. Caught between loyalty to her brutal guild and her own moral code, she must decide whether to obey orders or sabotage the bargain at great personal cost. Set in a dangerous coastal underworld of taverns, ships, warehouses, and hidden violence, the novella explores power, conscience, exploitation, and rebellion, while tracing an early turning point in Celaena’s life as a feared killer who refuses to accept every cruelty around her.
book-7392: Using the biblical story of Abraham and Isaac, this philosophical meditation examines faith as a demanding, paradoxical relation between the individual and God. A reflective narrator returns repeatedly to the moment on Mount Moriah, asking how Abraham can be understood as both obedient believer and potential murderer. The argument turns on the tension between universal ethics and religious commitment, introducing the idea of a “teleological suspension of the ethical” and exploring inwardness, silence, resignation, and the leap of faith. Set within Christian thought yet written as a work of probing literary philosophy, it studies anxiety, obedience, love, and the limits of rational explanation. The text addresses what it means to stand alone before the absolute, beyond public morality and ordinary understanding.
book-7393: In a world where rival shapeshifter peoples have fought for generations, the avian court and the serpent clan stand on the edge of ruin. Danica Shardae, heir to the birdlike Avian race, faces pressure from her family and the constant losses of war. Zane Cobriana, young ruler of the serpentine people, carries the same burden from the opposite side. To stop the bloodshed, they agree to a political marriage that forces both courts into uneasy contact. As Danica and Zane navigate ceremony, suspicion, and assassination threats, the novel centers on whether peace can survive inherited hatred. Set in royal eyries, hidden strongholds, and tense council chambers, it explores diplomacy, prejudice, leadership, and romance shaped by duty.
book-7394: Across a far-future human civilization linked by wormhole travel and ruled by rival governments, churches, and trading dynasties, a cosmic disaster opens the way for the dead to return and seize the living. As possession spreads from colony worlds to major habitats, political intrigue, military campaigns, black-market science, and religious prophecy converge into a system-wide crisis. Multiple factions pursue incompatible solutions: quarantine, extermination, negotiation, and a mysterious path toward transcendence. The novel moves between starships, orbital settlements, frontier planets, and occultized ruins, combining space opera with supernatural horror. Its central conflict pits individual survival and civic order against an invasion that blurs life, death, soul, and identity, while exploring themes of power, belief, corruption, sacrifice, and the social cost of technological empire.
book-7395: A runaway housekeeper with a talent for taking every instruction literally leaves her employers’ home after being scolded and sets off through a small town in search of new work. Along the way Amelia Bedelia misunderstands ordinary phrases, turning simple errands and household tasks into a chain of comic mishaps involving shops, neighbors, and would-be employers. The story unfolds in a domestic, everyday setting where language itself drives the conflict: adults mean one thing, and Amelia Bedelia hears another. Repetition, wordplay, and visual humor shape a gentle farce about idioms, communication, and patience. Written for young readers, the book pairs short episodes with illustrations to highlight the gap between spoken language and literal meaning while keeping the tone light, playful, and reassuring.
