book-7396: A firsthand travel narrative follows Norwegian explorer Thor Heyerdahl and a small crew as they sail a hand-built balsa-wood raft from Peru across the Pacific to Polynesia in 1947. Combining memoir, expedition report, and popular history, the account sets out Heyerdahl’s controversial argument that ancient South Americans could have reached Pacific islands on primitive vessels. The central conflict lies in testing that theory against ocean currents, storms, sharks, equipment failures, isolation, and the physical limits of a simple raft named Kon-Tiki. Detailed descriptions of navigation, weather, food, camp routine, and the open sea place the reader aboard the voyage itself. Themes include exploration, experimental archaeology, endurance, leadership, and the tension between scholarly skepticism and practical demonstration.
book-7397: Structured as a mock self-help manual, the novel follows an unnamed boy from a poor rural household into the expanding cities of an unnamed South Asian nation shaped by privatization, corruption, and rapid economic growth. He learns to navigate black markets, contaminated water, family obligation, and the unstable rules of entrepreneurship as he builds a bottled-water business. Running alongside his climb is a long, intermittent attachment to a woman identified only as the pretty girl, whose own path reflects class mobility and vulnerability. The book uses the language of advice and hustle to examine capitalism, urban migration, illness, desire, and aging. Its central tension lies between the promise of getting rich and the costs that development and ambition impose on bodies, relationships, and memory.
book-7398: Written for nonspecialists, this scientific exposition presents Einstein’s account of special and general relativity and the conceptual shift they require. It begins with the problem of measuring motion, time, and simultaneity in different frames of reference, then explains the constant speed of light, the relation between mass and energy, and the limits of Newtonian mechanics. The later chapters turn to gravity, describing it not as a force acting across empty space but as the curvature of space-time shaped by matter. Thought experiments, trains, clocks, rods, and astronomical observations provide the concrete examples. Alongside physics, the book engages philosophical questions about perception, geometry, causality, and how scientific theories revise ordinary ideas of reality.
book-7399: Set in contemporary London, this comic novel follows a young woman whose life has stalled after the loss of the man she expected to marry. As friends pair off, relatives offer advice, and work and social obligations continue, she moves through grief, denial, bad dates, and uneasy attempts to start again. The plot centers on her struggle to separate genuine mourning from habit, fantasy, and fear of being alone. Sharp scenes of dinner parties, phone calls, therapy, and late-night self-reckoning give the story a specific urban texture. Beneath the humor and romantic misadventures, the novel examines bereavement, female friendship, family pressure, body image, and the uneasy gap between public composure and private heartbreak.
book-74: Miles Halter leaves Florida for a boarding school in Alabama, drawn by the poet François Rabelais’s idea of seeking a “Great Perhaps.” At Culver Creek, he falls in with a tight circle of students whose late-night pranks, cigarettes, and hidden loyalties give shape to his new life. At the center is Alaska Young, brilliant, funny, moody, and unreachable, whose stories and contradictions fascinate him. When a shocking event divides the school year into a before and after, Miles and his friends try to understand what happened and what they missed. Set in dorm rooms, classrooms, and the wooded edges of campus, the novel examines first love, grief, guilt, friendship, and the search for meaning during adolescence.
book-740: Across the American Midwest of the late nineteenth century, a pioneer girl and her family move through forests, prairies, small towns, and new settlements as they build homes, harvest crops, endure blizzards, and search for stability. The collected Little House novels follow Laura Ingalls from early childhood in a log cabin in Wisconsin to adolescence and young adulthood on the Great Plains, tracing daily domestic work, frontier travel, school life, courtship, and the pressure of poverty. Wolves, hard winters, crop failure, illness, and isolation create recurring conflict, while family loyalty, self-reliance, faith, and adaptation shape the narrative. With Garth Williams’s illustrations, the volume presents historical fiction centered on settler life, household crafts, rural communities, and a child’s perspective on the changing American frontier.
book-7400: At Mount Washington High School, a cruel annual prank appears on homecoming week: a list naming the prettiest and the ugliest girl in each grade. The novel follows the eight students singled out by that sheet of paper as they move through one charged week of classes, parties, rumors, and shifting friendships. Some girls gain sudden status, while others face public humiliation, family pressure, and scrutiny from boys, teachers, and peers. As the list alters romances and social alliances, each girl must decide how much of her identity depends on beauty, popularity, and other people’s judgments. Set in a contemporary American high school, the story examines appearance, bullying, gender expectations, self-worth, and the power of gossip to shape everyday life.
book-7401: Set in Camas, Washington, from the 1950s through the Vietnam era, this literary family saga follows the Chance household, whose six children grow up under the shadow of their father’s unfinished baseball career and their mother’s fierce religious conviction. As the brothers and their sister move from sandlot games and schoolyard loyalties into draft resistance, political activism, spiritual searching, and adulthood, the novel tracks how a close family absorbs the pressures of war, social upheaval, and private grief. Baseball, scripture, sibling rivalry, and first love shape daily life, while arguments over faith, patriotism, nonviolence, and responsibility divide the family in intimate ways. The story examines American masculinity, conscience, marriage, and the stubborn bonds that hold people together across decades of change.
book-7402: Drawing on research in positive psychology and behavioral science, this nonfiction guide argues that happiness is not merely a reward for achievement but a practical starting point for better performance at work. Shawn Achor outlines seven principles intended to help readers build habits of optimism, resilience, social connection, and focused action in offices, classrooms, and other high-pressure environments. The book examines how mindset shapes productivity, creativity, motivation, leadership, and responses to stress, using studies, anecdotes, and workplace examples rather than abstract theory alone. Its central argument is that a more positive mental frame can improve decision-making and results for individuals and teams. Key themes include emotional well-being, success, habit formation, workplace culture, and the relationship between perception and professional effectiveness.
book-7403: A reincarnated dog continues his search for purpose by returning to the people he loves and watching over a new child, Clarity June, the granddaughter of his original owner. Moving through several canine lives and households, he observes a troubled family shaped by grief, addiction, divorce, and loneliness, and he tries to guide CJ toward safety, friendship, and love in the limited ways a dog can. The novel blends fantasy with domestic realism, using the dog’s candid, humorous narration to explore human relationships from ground level. Set in contemporary American homes, parks, and small communities, the story centers on loyalty, second chances, and the bond between humans and animals, while asking whether devotion can carry across death and rebirth.
book-7404: Drawing on Christian theology, pastoral counseling, and contemporary debates about romance, this guide examines marriage as a covenant rather than a private contract built on personal fulfillment alone. It addresses courtship, singleness, sexual intimacy, gender roles, forgiveness, and the daily disciplines that sustain long-term commitment. The argument places modern expectations of self-expression and compatibility alongside biblical teachings about sacrifice, service, and spiritual friendship, asking how couples can remain faithful amid disappointment, conflict, and cultural change. Examples from ministry and common marital struggles ground the discussion in ordinary domestic life, from communication failures to resentment and unmet desires. Central themes include covenant love, mutual responsibility, grace, and the tension between individual autonomy and a shared life shaped by religious belief.
book-7405: Gotham City adjusts to a new era after Bruce Wayne’s apparent death, with Dick Grayson taking on the Batman mantle and Damian Wayne serving as a volatile Robin. Their uneasy partnership drives a series of investigations that pit them against grotesque and theatrical threats, including Professor Pyg and the Circus of Strange, while a more brutal figure claiming Batman’s legacy stalks the city from the shadows. Set in rain-slick streets, hidden laboratories, and gaudy carnival spaces, the story combines superhero action with detective mystery and psychological horror. The central conflict turns on what Batman’s symbol means when worn by different men, and whether discipline, family loyalty, and moral restraint can survive grief, violence, and the temptation to fight monsters by becoming one.
book-7406: A schoolgirl named Airi Hoshina loves fairy tales and dreams of a perfect prince, but her ordinary life changes when a mysterious boy drops into her world from a magical kingdom. The child, Aram, is actually a prince under a curse: in sunlight he appears as a young boy, while in darkness he transforms into an older, handsome version of himself. As Airi hides him and tries to understand the rules of his enchantment, court politics, magical pursuers, and romantic confusion follow close behind. Set between modern Japan and a fantasy realm of castles, spells, and royal duty, the story blends comedy, shōjo romance, and adventure while exploring idealized love, identity, and the gap between fantasy and everyday life.
book-7407: While restoring a fifteenth-century Flemish painting of two noblemen playing chess, Madrid art expert Julia uncovers a hidden Latin inscription asking, “Who killed the knight?” The message appears to point to a murder concealed inside the painting’s original scene, but Julia’s research into the work’s provenance soon intersects with a series of present-day deaths. As she consults an art dealer, a chess master, and a curator, the novel moves between galleries, auction rooms, libraries, and the imagined courtly world inside the canvas. The investigation turns on iconography, chess strategy, forgery, and interpretation, asking how pictures encode violence and how intellect can both reveal and obscure motive. Themes include art history, obsession, deception, and the uneasy boundary between game and crime.
book-7408: A stormy night brings a soaked young woman to a castle gate, where a queen tests her claim to royal birth with an odd experiment involving a tiny pea hidden beneath a towering stack of mattresses. Drawing on Hans Christian Andersen’s fairy tale, this children’s fantasy unfolds in a kingdom of princes, queens, bedchambers, and courtly expectations. The central conflict turns on whether identity can be recognized through outward signs or must be proven through sensitivity, endurance, and custom. Janet Stevens’s retelling and illustrations emphasize exaggerated domestic detail, comic ceremony, and the absurd logic of palace life. Themes of class, appearance, legitimacy, and the rituals surrounding marriage shape a brief narrative that introduces young readers to a classic literary fairy tale.
book-7409: Set largely in the United States of the 1920s and 1930s, this collection gathers F. Scott Fitzgerald’s short fiction about debutantes, advertising men, soldiers, writers, clerks, and wealthy idlers moving through hotels, college campuses, suburban houses, and glittering city streets. The stories trace courtship, social ambition, financial risk, drinking, youth, and disillusion as characters chase beauty, status, love, or artistic success. Alongside realistic portraits of Jazz Age manners and business culture, several tales introduce dreamlike or fantastic premises that sharpen questions of identity, time, luck, and desire. Across comic episodes and quieter tragedies, the central tension lies between romance and money, self-invention and social class, and the fading promise of American prosperity. Edited and introduced by Matthew J. Bruccoli.
book-741: Linked stories follow Jane Rosenal from an observant adolescence in suburban New York into adulthood in Manhattan as she learns how romance, work, and family expectations shape a life. The narrative moves through bedrooms, offices, summer houses, and dinner tables, tracing awkward courtships, disappointing men, friendships, grief, and the small humiliations of class and ambition. Jane’s dry wit and sharp self-scrutiny frame encounters with older lovers, siblings, parents, and publishing-world colleagues, turning everyday scenes into studies of desire and miscommunication. Beneath the humor, the book examines coming of age, the performance of femininity, Jewish family dynamics, and the gap between the stories people tell about love and the compromises they actually make.
book-7410: After years of abuse in the West Virginia mountains, Heaven Leigh Casteel enters the opulent Tatterton mansion and is drawn into a secretive Virginia family ruled by money, illness, and old grudges. As she learns that her connection to the Tattertons reaches deeper than she imagined, she must navigate a household shaped by manipulation, forbidden desire, and competing claims of love and loyalty. The novel follows Heaven through ballrooms, sickrooms, and locked family spaces where every kindness seems to carry a price. Gothic romance and family melodrama drive the story’s central conflict: her search for safety, identity, and belonging in a world built on deception. Themes of class, incestuous obsession, trauma, and the lasting damage of parental cruelty run through the narrative.
book-7411: Set in the fragile years after the fall of the Empire, this Star Wars novel follows a New Republic strained by political rivalry, border crises, and rumors that Grand Admiral Thrawn may somehow have returned from the dead. Leia Organa Solo works to hold together uneasy alliances, while Han Solo travels into dangerous territory to investigate threats that could reignite galactic war. Luke Skywalker confronts both military deception and the unresolved legacy of the Jedi as evidence points toward a hidden Imperial strategy. Across smugglers’ routes, council chambers, and remote strongholds, competing factions exploit fear, misinformation, and old loyalties. The story centers on succession, statecraft, espionage, and the way the memory of past wars continues to shape decisions long after the battlefield has gone quiet.
book-7412: A collection of autobiographical essays traces a young internet celebrity’s life from suburban Michigan to online fame, using comedy to frame stories about family, school, travel, and public attention. The narrative moves through childhood awkwardness, first crushes, bullying, and the process of coming out as gay, then turns to conventions, red carpets, and the strange routines of a career built on YouTube and social media. Alongside jokes about pop culture, bad hair, and embarrassing encounters, the book addresses loneliness, anxiety, friendship, and the search for belonging in digital and physical communities. Its central thread is the tension between a carefully performed public persona and a private self still shaped by insecurity, ambition, and the desire to be seen clearly.
book-7413: A woman in New York appears to have a polished life: a wealthy, attentive husband, a privileged routine, and a marriage built on desire. That surface fractures when another man enters the story and turns domestic romance into a psychological mystery. The narrative moves through an intimate triangle in which passion, memory, and guilt are entangled with buried truths. As conflicting versions of love and loyalty emerge, the central tension shifts from adultery to questions of identity, trauma, and what each person is hiding from the others and from themselves. Combining contemporary romance with suspense, the novel uses wealth, urban isolation, and shifting perception to examine obsession, self-deception, and the dangerous stories people construct to survive unbearable loss.
book-7414: A routine traffic stop in suburban Baltimore turns into a decades-old missing-person case when an unidentified woman claims to be Heather Bethany, one of two sisters who vanished from a shopping mall in 1975. Questioned by detectives and shadowed by the press, she offers fragments instead of a full explanation, forcing police, family members, and the reader to revisit the original disappearance. The novel moves between the present investigation and the sisters’ childhood, tracing family tensions, ordinary suburban routines, and the hidden grievances that shape memory. Set in Maryland, the story combines procedural inquiry with psychological suspense, focusing on identity, trauma, sisterhood, and the unreliability of testimony as the central mystery becomes a study of what families conceal and what survivors choose to tell.
book-7415: A contemporary romance set around a tight-knit circle of tattoo artists and friends, the story follows Rome Archer, a former soldier trying to rebuild his life after military service and personal loss. Back in a familiar urban world of shops, bars, and complicated family expectations, he struggles with grief, survivor’s guilt, and a reputation he no longer wants. Cora Lewis, who has long hidden her feelings behind humor and loyalty, faces her own insecurity and fear of being overlooked. Their relationship develops as both confront old wounds, protective instincts, and the pressure of other people’s assumptions. The central conflict turns on whether intimacy can survive trauma, miscommunication, and self-doubt. Themes include healing, found family, physical and emotional scars, and the difficulty of coming home changed.
book-7416: An 18th-century comic novel follows Tristram Shandy as he tries to write the story of his life and repeatedly fails to get to the point. Instead of orderly autobiography, the narrative wanders through his conception, birth, family disputes, military memories, household accidents, and elaborate digressions on philosophy, language, and storytelling. In Shandy Hall and other English settings, Tristram’s eccentric father Walter, practical mother, devoted Uncle Toby, and argumentative servants turn ordinary events into debates about names, noses, education, fortification, and fate. The central tension lies between the desire to impose rational order on experience and the unruly sprawl of life itself. Themes include time, memory, bodily vulnerability, narrative form, and the comic gap between human intention and what actually happens.
book-7417: On the African savanna, a young giraffe named Gerald longs to join the Jungle Dance, but his long legs and awkward steps make him the target of teasing from other animals. Told in lively rhyming verse, the story follows his struggle with embarrassment, exclusion, and self-doubt as music fills the night and every creature seems to move with ease except him. A chance encounter with a small, encouraging friend helps Gerald listen differently and discover a rhythm that suits his own body. The book centers on dancing, confidence, and finding individual expression rather than copying others. Bright animal scenes and playful language support themes of kindness, resilience, and the idea that talent can appear when someone is given patience, support, and the freedom to be different.
book-7418: Seventeenth-century Italy forms the setting for a historical novel about Artemisia Gentileschi, a young Roman painter struggling to claim artistic authority in a world controlled by fathers, patrons, and courts. After learning her craft in her father Orazio’s studio, she endures sexual violence and a public trial that turns her private suffering into civic spectacle. The narrative follows her movement through Rome, Florence, and other Italian cities as she seeks commissions, financial independence, and recognition for paintings such as Judith Slaying Holofernes. Domestic obligations, marriage, motherhood, and rivalry with male artists complicate her work, while questions of faith, desire, honor, and reputation shape every decision. Art, female ambition, bodily experience, and the cost of turning pain into images drive the novel’s central conflict.
book-7419: Organized as a concise self-help reference, this work presents a metaphysical framework that connects physical illnesses and bodily symptoms with recurring mental and emotional patterns such as fear, resentment, guilt, and self-criticism. It argues that the body reflects inner beliefs and that healing begins by identifying thought habits associated with specific conditions, from headaches and back pain to digestive and respiratory problems. Entries pair ailments with proposed psychological causes and with affirmations intended to encourage self-acceptance, forgiveness, and emotional change. Blending popular spirituality, mind-body philosophy, and practical guidance, the book explores personal responsibility, the power of language, and the possibility of transformation through consciousness. Its central concern is how beliefs, stress, and emotion shape health and how altered thought may support recovery.
book-742: Humanity lives in a vast underground silo buried deep beneath a ruined landscape where going outside means death, and the few relics of the past are tightly controlled. Within this closed society, strict rules govern work, reproduction, and knowledge, while each level of the structure develops its own labor, status, and resentments. As a series of deaths and investigations disturb the silo’s fragile order, a mechanic is drawn into questions about who built this world, what lies beyond the airlock, and why dissent is punished so harshly. The novel combines post-apocalyptic survival with political mystery, focusing on censorship, social hierarchy, engineered belief, and the pressure placed on ordinary people who begin to doubt an inherited system.
book-7420: Middle school student Ichigo Momomiya goes on a museum date in Tokyo and is caught in a strange experiment that fuses her DNA with that of an endangered wildcat. Soon she discovers she can transform into Mew Ichigo, a cat-eared heroine with enhanced agility, and she is recruited to fight parasitic aliens that infect animals and people. As a café run by mysterious scientists becomes the team’s base, she searches for other girls who carry endangered-animal powers and struggles to balance secret battles with school, friendship, and an awkward crush. Set in contemporary urban Japan, the manga combines magical-girl action, romantic comedy, and environmental themes, using transformation scenes, monster attacks, and café life to introduce a story about identity, responsibility, and protecting the natural world.
book-7421: Set in rural Montana in the late 1980s and early 1990s, this young adult novel follows Cameron Post as she grows up after the sudden death of her parents and tries to understand her attraction to girls in a conservative small-town world. Living with her grandmother and strict Aunt Ruth, she moves through grief, friendship, secrecy, and first love while navigating church culture and local expectations about femininity, family, and desire. When her relationship with another girl is discovered, she is sent to a religious conversion camp that promises to cure homosexuality. The narrative centers on identity, shame, resistance, and the cost of forcing belief systems onto adolescents, while portraying the textures of teenage life through pickup trucks, prairie landscapes, Bible study, and hidden romance.
book-7422: A curious girl named Coraline Jones moves into a divided old house and discovers a locked door that opens onto a disturbing parallel home. In this graphic novel adaptation, the familiar rooms, eccentric neighbors, and rainy grounds of her new residence become the setting for a fantasy of doubles and deception. On the other side waits the Other Mother, a figure who offers attention, comfort, and a version of family life designed to trap Coraline. As Coraline explores the alternate world, she faces talking animals, eerie children, and small clues about vanished lives. The story centers on courage, loneliness, temptation, and the difference between genuine love and possession, using shadowy illustrations to sharpen its uncanny mood.
book-7423: In the kingdom of Ingary, cautious young Charmain Baker is sent to look after the house of her great-uncle William, the Royal Wizard, while he is ill. The task becomes complicated when she discovers that the house is governed by magical directions, hidden rooms, and doors that open into different places. As Charmain struggles with spells, household work, and a small magical dog, she is drawn into royal concerns over a missing cache of gold and the mysterious movements of lubbock creatures. She is joined by Peter, an apprentice with practical skills, and eventually crosses paths with the powerful wizard Howl and Sophie. The novel combines domestic comedy, wandering architecture, court intrigue, and questions about responsibility, competence, and growing independence.
book-7424: Set in Mexico and the United States during the 2000s drug war, this crime thriller follows DEA agent Art Keller as his long conflict with cartel leader Adán Barrera reignites after Barrera escapes prison. Their pursuit and counterattack unfold across border towns, deserts, prisons, newsrooms, and political back rooms, tracing how cocaine trafficking entangles police, soldiers, hit men, priests, journalists, migrants, and families. The novel frames the cartel war as both personal vendetta and system of corruption, where money, revenge, and power shape public violence and private grief. Assassinations, kidnappings, mass killings, and compromised institutions drive the plot, while the narrative examines loyalty, complicity, faith, and the human cost of prohibition and organized crime on both sides of the border.
book-7425: A memoir of grief, guilt, and public scrutiny examines life after the Columbine High School shooting through the perspective of Dylan Klebold’s mother. Sue Klebold recounts her family’s ordinary suburban life before the massacre, the shock of learning her son was one of the perpetrators, and the years of questioning that follow. The narrative focuses on parental love, warning signs, adolescent depression, suicide, and the limits of what families understand about a child’s inner life. Set against the history of one of the most widely discussed school shootings in the United States, the book combines personal testimony with reflection on mental health, blame, shame, and survival. It also addresses advocacy for suicide prevention and the difficult ethics of speaking from the aftermath of violence.
book-7426: In humid South Florida, ex-detective and solitary fishing guide Mick Stranahan is drawn into a violent tangle of fraud, vanity, and revenge after a patient dies on the operating table of a fashionable plastic surgeon. As investigators circle a web of malpractice claims, insurance scams, and political corruption, Mick becomes a target himself, pursued by a grotesquely memorable hit man and entangled with people who have their own reasons to silence the truth. The novel moves through marinas, canals, strip malls, and luxury clinics, using crime and dark comedy to expose the region’s mix of greed, spectacle, and environmental decay. Its central conflict turns on who is exploiting whom, and whether integrity can survive in a landscape ruled by money, image, and violence.
book-7427: At a London gentlemen’s club and on a missile base on England’s coast, British agent James Bond investigates industrialist Sir Hugo Drax, a national hero financing Moonraker, a rocket intended to defend Britain. What begins as a discreet assignment after a card-table cheating scandal widens into a security case involving sabotage, espionage, and the possibility that the weapon itself may be turned against the country it is meant to protect. Bond works with Special Branch officer Gala Brand to uncover hidden motives behind Drax’s public patriotism and the intense secrecy surrounding the launch. The novel combines gambling scenes, police procedure, and Cold War technology with themes of class performance, postwar nationalism, deception, and the vulnerability of modern states to enemies operating behind respectable identities.
book-7428: Written amid the political upheavals surrounding the Exclusion Crisis and the Glorious Revolution, this work sets out a foundational argument against absolute monarchy and for constitutional government. The first treatise attacks Sir Robert Filmer’s claim that kings inherit paternal authority from Adam, dismantling the religious and genealogical case for divine-right rule. The second treatise develops a positive political theory grounded in the state of nature, natural equality, individual rights, labor, property, consent, and the social contract. Government exists to preserve life, liberty, and estate, and political power remains legitimate only while it serves the public good. Central themes include sovereignty, revolution, religious and political authority, the limits of law, and the right to resist tyranny.
book-7429: A collection of nineteenth-century essays examines conscience, government, reform, and the moral claims of the individual in American public life. The central piece, “Civil Disobedience,” argues that citizens should refuse cooperation with unjust laws and institutions, grounding political resistance in personal ethics rather than party loyalty. Other essays turn to slavery, economic life, reading, solitude, and the natural world, linking spiritual independence with close attention to everyday experience. Set against debates over taxation, the state, and social responsibility in the United States, the volume presents a spare, declarative prose style and a persistent conflict between individual judgment and civic obedience. Recurring themes include nonviolent protest, self-reliance, moral accountability, simplicity, and the tension between public authority and private conscience.
book-743: Set in the ancient Near East under Roman rule, this comic historical novel follows Levi called Biff, the rough-edged boyhood friend of Jesus, as he is ordered by the angel Raziel to record the missing years of the Messiah’s life. The narrative moves from Nazareth through cities, deserts, and trading routes as Biff and Joshua search for wisdom among rabbis, magi, and ascetics. Its central tension lies between sacred destiny and ordinary human appetites: Biff craves food, sex, and mischief while Joshua struggles to understand compassion, justice, and the burden of becoming Christ. Blending biblical material with irreverent humor, the story explores friendship, faith, doubt, mercy, and the gap between official scripture and lived experience.
book-7430: Set in 19th-century New England, this children's and young adult novel follows Rose Campbell as she returns from a period of travel and enters late adolescence among her large circle of cousins. No longer the sickly child of the earlier story, she must decide what kind of woman she wants to become while relatives, suitors, and social expectations press different models of femininity on her. Household scenes, holidays, conversations, and small acts of loyalty shape a domestic plot centered on courtship, inheritance, family duty, and moral education. Rose’s affectionate but testing relationships with her cousins, especially the contrast between charm, ambition, and steadiness in the young men around her, bring the central conflict into focus. Themes include maturity, character, wealth, independence, and the meaning of love within a close-knit family world.
book-7431: Sixteen-year-old Mary Iris Malone, known as Mim, leaves her father and stepmother in Mississippi and boards a Greyhound bound for Cleveland after hearing that her estranged mother is ill. The novel follows her improvised cross-country trip through bus stations, highways, and temporary shelters as she meets drifters, runaways, and other travelers who unsettle her certainties. Written in a witty, intimate voice, the story combines road-novel adventure with letters, family secrets, and a coming-of-age search for truth. The central conflict lies in Mim’s attempt to reach her mother while confronting fractured family loyalties, buried grief, and her own unstable perceptions. Themes include mental health, trust, identity, and the gap between the stories people tell about themselves and the harder realities they avoid.
book-7432: In a North Carolina town, a family already marked by grief struggles to hold together when a teenage boy’s obsessive-compulsive disorder begins to dominate daily life. Felix Fitzpatrick, bright and deeply attached to his rituals, fears that any mistake will bring catastrophe, while his mother Ella tries to protect him and his younger brother from both the illness and the judgment of neighbors. As therapy, school pressures, and family tensions intensify, the household must confront guilt, denial, and the limits of love. Alongside the domestic strain, an unexpected romantic connection offers Ella a glimpse of renewal, complicating her loyalty and responsibilities. The novel explores mental illness, bereavement, marriage, adolescence, and the difficult balance between rescuing someone and allowing them to face the world.
book-7433: At a Catholic girls’ school in Sydney, seventeen-year-old Josephine Alibrandi faces her final year, the pressure of exams, and the social divisions of class and ethnicity. Raised by her single Italian-Australian mother and watched over by a formidable grandmother, she carries the stigma of being born outside marriage while trying to define herself beyond family gossip and community expectations. The unexpected return of her father unsettles old resentments and opens questions about loyalty, inheritance, and identity. Friendships, first love, and rivalry intensify as she moves between school privilege, working-class neighborhoods, and a close-knit migrant family. The novel examines adolescence, cultural heritage, intergenerational conflict, shame, belonging, and the struggle to claim an independent self within the demands of family and tradition.
book-7434: In a contemporary small-town and urban American setting, a guarded woman whose quiet life has long been shaped by fear becomes entangled with a hard, secretive man known as Raid, whose dangerous work pulls violence and suspicion to their door. As their relationship shifts from wary attraction to intimacy, criminal threats, buried trauma, and local power struggles force both characters to confront what they have survived and what they are willing to risk for trust. The novel combines romance with thriller elements, using investigations, intimidation, and hidden identities to drive the plot. Central themes include recovery from abuse, loyalty, protection, and the difficulty of building a stable future when the past remains active and dangerous. The story focuses on emotional healing alongside escalating external peril.
book-7435: In Albuquerque, private investigator and grim reaper Charley Davidson juggles ordinary missing-person work with a constant stream of dead clients who can speak only to her. As she follows clues through motel rooms, police files, and supernatural visitations, a new case involving a vanished woman and an escalating threat around her family pulls her deeper into danger. At the same time, her turbulent bond with Reyes Farrow, a beautiful and terrifying supernatural being tied to hell, grows more complicated as secrets, desire, and distrust collide. Mixing urban fantasy, horror, and romance, the novel centers on murder investigations, ghosts, demons, and the strain of loving someone connected to violence and prophecy, while Charley tries to protect the living without losing herself to the dead.
book-7436: A cache of papyrus scrolls draws an Egyptologist and her English husband into a dangerous search across Egypt and Ethiopia, linking the modern world to the court intrigues of the pharaohs. As they translate the writings of the ancient scribe Taita, the narrative opens onto a second story set in the Nile valley, where royal succession, war, and burial rites shape the fate of a hidden tomb. The present-day quest becomes a thriller of excavation camps, desert travel, coded clues, and violent rivals determined to seize the treasure first. Moving between archaeological investigation and ancient testimony, the novel centers on lost dynasties, tomb robbers, scholarly obsession, and the enduring power of texts to preserve both history and ambition.
book-7437: A hard-partying teenager is sent to spend the summer with her estranged father just as he prepares for a new marriage, forcing her into a suburban household that feels nothing like home. Whitley Johnson arrives expecting boredom and conflict, but instead finds future step-siblings, wedding plans, and a watchful next-door neighbor named Nathan, whose steady presence unsettles the image she has built of herself. Set during one hot summer of family dinners, late-night conversations, and mounting emotional pressure, the novel follows her efforts to navigate divided loyalties between parents, new relationships, and her own reckless habits. The story centers on trust, blended family tensions, loneliness, self-protection, and the possibility of changing a life shaped by disappointment.
book-7438: On an isolated island off Prince Edward Island, a Scoutmaster leads five teenage boys on a routine camping trip that turns into a quarantine nightmare. An emaciated stranger stumbles into their camp carrying a bioengineered parasite that causes ravenous hunger, rapid bodily decay, and grotesque physical transformation. Cut off from the mainland by weather and official containment, the troop faces infection, starvation, panic, and the collapse of trust within the group. The novel combines survival thriller and body horror, tracing how fear and adolescent cruelty intensify under pressure. Its central conflict pits the boys’ efforts to protect one another against the parasite’s relentless spread and the human impulse toward selfishness. Themes include contagion, isolation, bodily vulnerability, and the fragility of social order.
book-7439: London in 1543 forms the backdrop for a Tudor mystery in which lawyer Matthew Shardlake is drawn into a series of killings that echo the imagery and punishments of the Book of Revelation. Summoned into the dangerous orbit of Queen Catherine Parr and Archbishop Cranmer, he must investigate murders linked to radical religious circles while Henry VIII’s court seethes with factional rivalry, fear, and informers. As Shardlake follows clues through prisons, churches, lawyers’ chambers, and the king’s palaces, he confronts both a calculating murderer and the political volatility of the Reformation. The novel combines criminal investigation with a portrait of plague-shadowed, overcrowded London, exploring conscience, heresy, state power, and the personal cost of seeking truth under a tyrannical regime.
book-744: A practical spiritual guide argues that psychological suffering is sustained by identification with thought, memory, and anticipation, and that relief becomes possible through sustained attention to the present moment. Drawing on ideas from Buddhism, Christianity, meditation, and contemporary self-help, it presents the ego as a mental construct that keeps people trapped in anxiety, resentment, and dissatisfaction. Short sections and question-and-answer passages address everyday situations such as stress, relationships, work, and inner conflict, offering exercises in observation, stillness, and acceptance. The central argument holds that awareness of the “now” interrupts compulsive thinking and opens a different sense of self grounded in presence rather than narrative. Themes include consciousness, attachment, emotional pain, mindfulness, and the search for spiritual transformation in ordinary life.
book-7440: A sequence of one hundred sonnets addresses a beloved in poems set among ordinary domestic objects, the Chilean coast, gardens, streets, bread, wood, water, and the changing light of the day. Written as intimate lyric poetry rather than narrative fiction, the collection traces erotic desire, companionship, memory, gratitude, jealousy, and the pressure of time on a long partnership. The central movement lies between private devotion and the larger world: the speaker celebrates a specific marriage while linking personal love to the body, labor, nature, and the political landscape of twentieth-century Latin America. Stephen Tapscott’s English translation presents Neruda’s compact sonnet form, earthy imagery, and direct address, making the volume searchable for readers interested in love poetry, marriage poems, translated Spanish literature, and modern lyric verse.
book-7441: Shifting across 1940s America, this historical novel follows teenage half sisters Eva and Iris after their unreliable mother disappears and leaves them to make a life together. Their journey moves from small-town Ohio to Hollywood film sets, Long Island mansions, and wartime New York, gathering a changing household that includes drifters, servants, and soldiers. As the sisters improvise new identities, they confront abandonment, class privilege, anti-Semitism, race, and the unstable bargains women make to survive. The central tension lies in whether family is something inherited or something assembled from accident and loyalty. Through sharp scenes of domestic reinvention and wartime disruption, the narrative examines chosen kinship, performance, desire, and the fragile hope of building a home in a country shaped by glamour and loss.
book-7442: Set in Regency London, this historical romance follows sharp-tongued Hyacinth Bridgerton, the youngest of the Bridgerton siblings, as she becomes entangled with Gareth St. Clair, a witty but troubled gentleman burdened by a cruel father and questions about his inheritance. Their connection deepens when Hyacinth helps Gareth decipher an old Italian diary that may reveal family secrets and hidden wealth. As they move through drawing rooms, musicales, and private investigations, flirtation gives way to a more serious emotional struggle over trust, legitimacy, and reputation. The novel combines courtship comedy, family intrigue, and mystery, focusing on verbal sparring, social expectation, and the risks of intimacy in a world where marriage, lineage, and scandal shape every choice.
book-7443: Set in the wizarding world of Hogwarts, this short companion volume gathers background pieces on authority, school governance, and disruptive magical beings. It expands on the roles of headmasters, the Ministry of Magic, and influential figures connected to the castle, while also tracing the history of notorious poltergeists and other eccentric presences in its corridors. Drawn from Pottermore writings, the collection mixes fictional history, character sketches, and lore rather than a single continuous plot. Central concerns include how power is exercised in magical institutions, how rules collide with rebellion, and how personality shapes leadership. The text offers additional context for familiar names and places from the Harry Potter series, with decorative visual elements by MinaLima supporting the archival, reference-like format.
book-7444: A foundational work of German idealism traces the education of consciousness from immediate sense certainty through perception, understanding, self-consciousness, reason, spirit, religion, and finally absolute knowing. Moving through figures such as the master and slave, the unhappy consciousness, and ethical life in the polis and the modern state, it presents experience as a sequence of conflicts in which each claim to truth exposes its own limits and gives rise to a new form. The setting is intellectual and historical rather than narrative, linking individual awareness to social institutions, labor, language, law, and culture. Central arguments concern dialectical development, recognition, freedom, and the relation between subject and object. Themes include alienation, historical change, skepticism, desire, and the possibility of philosophical knowledge.
book-7445: Set in the world of a Colorado motorcycle club, this contemporary romance follows a woman rebuilding her life as she is drawn into an intense relationship with a protective, rough-edged biker tied to Chaos. Their attraction develops amid club loyalties, old wounds, family obligations, and the dangers that come with outlaw affiliations. Domestic scenes, sharp banter, and explicit sexual tension balance threats from past relationships and the pressure of trusting someone whose life runs on violence and brotherhood. The novel centers on whether love can survive fear, jealousy, and the pull between independence and belonging. Themes of chosen family, recovery from emotional damage, masculinity, female resilience, and the appeal of risk shape a story that combines humor, conflict, and possessive passion in a contemporary American setting.
book-7446: Across a far-future Confederation of habitats, colony worlds, and living starships, a crisis spreads when the dead begin returning to possess the living. The novel follows multiple factions as governments, mercenaries, religious leaders, and starship crews struggle to contain an expanding wave of possession that turns political rivalries and frontier settlements into battlefields. Joshua Calvert and other recurring figures move through space stations, jungle planets, and aristocratic estates while searching for information that might explain the breach between the living universe and the afterlife. Mixing space opera with gothic horror and supernatural fantasy, the story centers on social collapse, fanaticism, organized crime, military intervention, and the moral cost of survival in a civilization whose technology cannot easily defeat a metaphysical enemy.
book-7447: An immortal warrior haunted by the demon of Promiscuity moves through a brutal supernatural world where the Lords of the Underworld battle Hunters, rival immortals, and the consequences of Pandora’s box. Paris survives by seduction, yet every woman he takes to his bed dies, turning desire into punishment and grief. When he becomes entangled with Sienna Blackstone, a dangerous young woman linked to enemy forces and to a power he cannot easily control, attraction collides with prophecy, revenge, and war. Their relationship unfolds across fortresses, hidden realms, and violent confrontations, while gods and demons manipulate the stakes. The novel combines paranormal romance and dark fantasy through themes of cursed sexuality, guilt, loyalty, and the possibility of intimacy for characters shaped by violence and supernatural fate.
book-7448: In a divided kingdom where silver-blooded nobles wield elemental powers and red-blooded commoners live under their rule, Mare Barrow becomes both prisoner and political symbol. Confined in the royal palace by King Maven, stripped of freedom and separated from the Scarlet Guard, she endures court surveillance, manipulation, and the weaponization of her own image while rebellion spreads beyond her reach. Outside the capital, shifting alliances among exiles, soldiers, and rival houses turn the struggle for Norta into a wider campaign against hereditary power. The novel moves between palace captivity and military maneuvering, centering on civil war, propaganda, trauma, loyalty, and the unstable bond between resistance leaders who need one another but do not fully trust one another.
book-7449: Set in New York in 1967 and later moving through Paris and the Caribbean, the novel follows Adam Walker, a Columbia student whose brief friendship with a wealthy, enigmatic Frenchman named Rudolf Born draws him into sex, violence, and a crime that continues to shape his life. Years later, Adam tries to record what happened, and other voices enter the narrative, complicating the line between testimony and invention. The story unfolds through manuscripts, letters, and shifting narrators, turning a personal recollection into an inquiry about evidence, authorship, and deception. Central tensions arise from desire, moral responsibility, and the difficulty of telling the truth about traumatic events. Themes include memory, guilt, power, and the instability of identity in literary self-portraiture.
book-745: A comic memoir unfolds through episodes from an eccentric childhood in rural Texas and an adulthood shaped by anxiety, depression, and spectacular social embarrassment. Jenny Lawson presents a family landscape crowded with taxidermied animals, deadpan parents, bizarre pets, and a father whose practical jokes and hobbies make ordinary domestic life feel surreal. As she moves into dating, marriage, work, and internet notoriety, the central tension lies in trying to function as a responsible adult while her mind and circumstances veer toward chaos. The narrative treats panic, shame, and isolation alongside absurd set pieces, using confession and exaggeration to explore how humor operates as a survival strategy. Themes include mental illness, family mythology, self-deprecation, marriage, and the uneasy border between private breakdown and public storytelling.
book-7450: Set in contemporary Egypt and framed through an intimate marital crisis, this literary novel unfolds as an extended address from a wife to her husband over the course of a single charged night. As domestic tension exposes resentment, desire, and estrangement, the narrative turns outward to ancient mythology, religious symbolism, and the long cultural history of the feminine body. Pharaonic goddesses, serpent imagery, sacred ritual, and patriarchal interpretations of faith become part of a philosophical argument about women, power, and memory. Blending realistic scenes of urban middle-class life with essayistic reflection and a faint aura of the fantastic, the novel examines marriage, gender hierarchy, spirituality, and the conflict between inherited beliefs and lived experience. Its central concern is the place of womanhood within both private love and civilization’s oldest myths.
book-7451: Sixteen-year-old April moves from New York to a new home in Connecticut after her parents divorce, leaving behind her friends, her boyfriend, and the city life she knows. When her strict father plans to relocate her again, she and her friend Vi devise a reckless solution: pretend they are living under adult supervision while actually occupying a house on their own. What begins as a fantasy of freedom fills with missed curfews, secret parties, neighbor problems, shifting friendships, and complicated romance. As April tries to manage lies to parents, school pressures, and her feelings for both old and new crushes, the novel explores independence, trust, family change, and the gap between teenage ideas of adulthood and the responsibilities real freedom requires.
book-7452: Across a stark post-apocalyptic wasteland of sand seas, ruined towns, and scavenged camps, teenage fighter Saba tries to build a life after overthrowing a brutal ruler and rescuing her family. Peace does not last. Haunted by visions and drawn toward the growing power of a mysterious, persuasive leader named DeMalo, she becomes caught between loyalty to Jack, duty to her brother Lugh, and the demands of a changing world. As old enemies shift and new alliances form, the novel follows Saba through caravan roads, rebel hideouts, and contested settlements where trust is fragile and violence is never far away. The story centers on power, prophecy, romantic attachment, and the question of whether survival can coexist with compassion.
book-7453: A girl grows up in working-class Ohio under a mother who craves medical attention and repeatedly presents her daughter as gravely ill, a pattern associated with Munchausen syndrome by proxy. The memoir follows childhood doctor visits, invasive tests, emergency-room scenes, and the daily confusion of being trained to perform sickness while doubting her own body. Family instability, poverty, and a household ruled by manipulation shape the narrator’s sense of self as she tries to understand why pain, fear, and public sympathy are constantly staged around her. Alongside the personal story, the narrative examines child abuse hidden inside medical systems, the authority granted to parents and physicians, and the long psychological aftermath of surviving coercion, neglect, and fabricated illness.
book-7454: A middle-aged woman and a man with whom she has shared a long, complicated love affair meet again after years apart, and the novel traces their relationship backward through earlier encounters across decades. As the chronology reverses, scenes of hotel rooms, marriages, careers, letters, and partings reveal how desire, loyalty, ambition, and missed timing shape their bond. The central tension lies between the private intensity of their connection and the public lives they build with other people. Set in contemporary American and international locations associated with travel and professional life, the story examines memory, secrecy, adultery, and the way people revise the past. The reverse structure turns each meeting into an inquiry into what love preserves, what it damages, and what remains unresolved.
book-7455: In 1870 Texas, a widowed former soldier, Captain Jefferson Kyle Kidd, makes a living traveling from town to town to read newspapers aloud to paying audiences hungry for reports of war, politics, disasters, and inventions. His solitary routine changes when he agrees to escort Johanna, a ten-year-old girl taken years earlier by the Kiowa and now reclaimed by government agents, to distant relatives in San Antonio. As they cross rough frontier country marked by violence, lawlessness, and cultural division, Kidd confronts the practical dangers of the road and the deeper question of where the child belongs. The novel follows an uneasy bond between an aging news reader and a resistant girl, exploring captivity, language, memory, and the fragile work of building family after war.
book-7456: Counterterrorism operative Scot Harvath is drawn into a fast-moving hunt that stretches across Paris, Norway, and the mountains of Afghanistan as a new wave of attacks threatens American targets. Working through intelligence fragments, surveillance, and field operations, he pursues a network of jihadist militants, financiers, and political enablers connected to unfinished business from earlier conflicts. The novel moves through embassies, safe houses, prisons, and remote training camps, pairing action set pieces with espionage tradecraft and intelligence analysis. Its central conflict turns on whether Harvath can identify and stop the plot before another mass-casualty strike succeeds. Themes include national security, retaliation, the costs of covert war, and the tension between personal loyalty, revenge, and state power.
book-7457: Drawing on the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata and a wide range of regional and vernacular traditions, this illustrated retelling presents the struggle between the Kauravas and the Pandavas as both dynastic history and spiritual inquiry. The narrative moves through Hastinapura, forests, courts, battlefields, and exile, tracing dice games, vows, marriages, rivalries, and the Kurukshetra war. Alongside the story, brief interpretive notes connect episodes to Hindu ideas of dharma, karma, kingship, duty, caste, gender, and the tension between worldly power and inner detachment. Krishna, Draupadi, Bhishma, Karna, Arjuna, and other major figures appear not as simple heroes or villains but as participants in moral dilemmas shaped by desire, obligation, and fate. The book treats myth as a living tradition whose meanings shift across tellings.
book-7458: Set in rural China in the 1920s and 1930s, this historical novel follows a young girl from a farming family who is sent to work in a silk factory and dormitory house. Among the women who sort cocoons, reel thread, and labor through long shifts, she learns the strict routines of silk production and the bonds that form within an all-female community. The novel traces the tension between family duty, economic survival, and a growing desire for self-determination as the workers negotiate loyalty, friendship, and the limited choices available to them. As political upheaval and war begin to press in from outside the factory walls, the story examines women’s labor, collective resilience, class, and the fragile shelter created by companionship in a changing China.
book-7459: An English gentleman on holiday in the small Central European kingdom of Ruritania discovers that he is the double of the newly crowned king. When the king is drugged and abducted by his ambitious half brother on the eve of the coronation, he agrees to impersonate the monarch to prevent a coup and preserve the throne. Court ceremonies, hunting lodges, country roads, and a forbidding castle become the setting for a story of mistaken identity, political intrigue, swordplay, and divided loyalties. As he navigates plots among nobles and soldiers, his role draws him into danger and into a restrained attachment to Princess Flavia. The novel explores honor, duty, legitimacy, and the tension between personal desire and public responsibility in a romanticized nineteenth-century Europe.
book-746: In the canal city of Camorr, a gifted orphan grows into Locke Lamora, leader of the Gentleman Bastards, a small gang of confidence tricksters who pose as nobles, priests, and merchants to steal from the city’s rich. Beneath the city’s ornate palaces and criminal underworld stands a tense balance between noble houses, merchant wealth, and the secret rule of the Capa Barsavi. That order begins to fracture when a mysterious rival known as the Grey King launches a violent campaign against the underworld, drawing Locke and his fiercely loyal companion Jean into a struggle far larger than any swindle. The novel combines elaborate heists, gang politics, disguise, and swordplay while exploring friendship, vengeance, class, loyalty, and the costs of deception.
book-7460: A teenage girl remains caught between dangerous vampire brothers as loyalty, desire, and survival collide in a contemporary paranormal setting. After learning more about the hidden rules that govern their undead world, she faces increasing pressure from the possessive leader who claims a bond with her and from the gentler brother whose protection offers a different future. Rivalries inside the vampire family sharpen, human friendships grow harder to preserve, and ordinary school life gives way to secrecy, pursuit, and violence. The novel centers on romantic conflict, coercion, and the costs of belonging to a supernatural clan, while also tracing a young woman’s struggle to keep agency over her own body and choices as blood ties, obsession, and mortal danger close in around her.
book-7461: Set in a contemporary small-town and college-age world, this romance follows a young woman trying to stay invisible after hardship leaves her isolated and wary of dependence. Her life shifts when she crosses paths with a very tall, heavily tattooed man whose rough appearance hides patience, loyalty, and a close-knit family. As attraction grows between them, the story centers on practical obstacles as much as emotion: unstable housing, financial insecurity, damaged self-worth, and the fear of becoming a burden. Humor and flirtation balance scenes of vulnerability while the couple negotiate trust, intimacy, and the difference between pity and genuine care. Themes of chosen family, disability and body image, resilience, and accepting help shape a warm contemporary love story driven by tenderness and banter.
book-7462: After a man is blown apart by his own homemade bomb on a Wisconsin roadside, writer Peter Aaron sets out to reconstruct the life that led to the blast before the story is distorted by police and newspapers. His account follows novelist Benjamin Sachs from literary success and political idealism into a chain of accidents, failed relationships, assumed identities, and increasingly secret acts. Moving through New York apartments, New England retreats, and the wider American landscape of the late twentieth century, the novel combines confession, investigation, and political unease. It examines friendship, marriage, authorship, surveillance, and the unstable line between public protest and private obsession, while asking how chance events can redirect a life and how any story about another person is assembled from fragments.
book-7463: Washington, D.C., politics, televangelism, and federal investigation intersect in this thriller. Faith Lockhart, a sharp lobbyist, discovers that powerful men around her are hiding a criminal network tied to money, influence, and a nationally known religious empire. When evidence makes her a target, she is forced to run, drawing the attention of Lee Adams, a cynical investigator assigned to protect her while trying to determine whom he can trust. Their flight moves from government offices and luxury hotels to revival stages and back roads as assassins and officials close in. The novel centers on corruption in public life, manipulation of belief, media spectacle, and the difficulty of finding moral certainty inside institutions built on ambition, secrecy, and image.
book-7464: In the savage frontier called the Spine of the World, barbarian hero Wulfgar returns from captivity deeply scarred in body and mind, unable to resume the life and friendships that once defined him. He drifts through Icewind Dale and the northern wilderness, taking work as a caravan guard and selling his strength while anger, grief, and drink pull him toward self-destruction. Around him move merchants, innkeepers, rogues, and old enemies, turning the road into a place of fragile alliances and sudden violence. Set in the Forgotten Realms, the novel combines tundra travel, tavern intrigue, and brutal combat with a study of trauma, exile, masculinity, and the difficult search for purpose after war and torture have reshaped a man’s identity.
book-7465: On Halloween in a suburban town, shy schoolgirl Carly Beth Caldwell buys a grotesque green mask after repeated teasing from classmates and her younger brother leaves her angry and humiliated. The costume gives her a frightening new confidence, and she begins using its snarling face to scare the people who have mocked her. Soon the prank turns dangerous when the mask starts to feel alive and refuses to come off, trapping her between childish revenge and a loss of self-control. The story follows her race to undo the curse before the transformation becomes permanent. Mixing schoolyard bullying, trick-or-treat streets, costume shops, and body horror, the novel centers on fear, identity, cruelty, and the consequences of becoming what others dread.
book-7466: A murder in the badlands of New Mexico draws former CIA operative and onetime monk Wyman Ford into a search for a stolen notebook, a coded message, and a rare Tyrannosaurus rex fossil hidden in the canyons. The trail runs through paleontology labs, Santa Fe money circles, and desert archaeology as rival collectors, scientists, and hired killers pursue evidence that could upend careers and fortunes. The novel combines wilderness travel, forensic clues, and scientific rivalry, with scenes set among sandstone cliffs, dig sites, and remote ranch country. Its central conflict turns on who controls a spectacular prehistoric discovery and what people will do to possess it. Themes include greed, scientific ethics, secrecy, and the uneasy border between scholarship, commerce, and violence.
book-7467: A minimalist London townhouse at One Folgate Street links the lives of two women in this psychological thriller. Emma, fleeing a violent break-in, moves into the stark, technologically controlled house with her boyfriend and agrees to the owner’s rigid rules about possessions, routines, and behavior. Three years later, Jane, recovering from personal loss, rents the same property and becomes fascinated by its severe design and by the charismatic architect who created it. When Jane learns that the previous tenant died unexpectedly, she begins to trace Emma’s last months in the house. The novel alternates between the two timelines, using domestic space, surveillance, memory, desire, and self-reinvention to explore manipulation, grief, and the danger hidden inside an apparently perfect home.
book-7468: At the towering, accidentally sideways Wayside School, the students in Mrs. Jewls’s class return to a place where ordinary classroom routines keep collapsing into absurdity. Short linked episodes follow children such as Todd, Maurecia, Sharie, and Myron as they face baffling teachers, disappearing possessions, mixed-up rules, eerie misunderstandings, and the school’s trademark illogic. Set in a single-room classroom high above the playground, the stories turn spelling lessons, recess, and lunch into comic problems that rarely behave by real-world logic. Beneath the nonsense, the book observes school friendships, jealousy, fairness, embarrassment, and the small struggles of fitting in. The result is a collection of surreal school comedy in which language, authority, and everyday habits are twisted into strange but recognizable childhood conflicts.
book-7469: In the summer of 1960, a group of schoolboys in Elm Haven, Illinois, senses that something ancient and predatory has awakened beneath the routines of a small Midwestern town. Old buildings, abandoned places, and familiar adults begin to feel wrong as a series of disturbing incidents points toward a hidden evil centered on the boys’ school and the town’s past. As they investigate, bicycles, baseball diamonds, farm fields, and empty streets become the landscape of a supernatural siege. The novel combines childhood friendship, grief, courage, and the loss of innocence with scenes of stalking terror and escalating violence. Set against heat, cornfields, and small-town rituals, it explores how ordinary communities conceal buried histories and how children confront horrors that adults cannot or will not see.
book-747: Raised at a boarding school in Ancelstierre, where magic barely works beyond the border, Sabriel has grown up apart from the Old Kingdom and from her father’s dangerous office as Abhorsen, the necromancer who lays the dead to rest. When a desperate message reaches her, she crosses into a landscape of ruined reservoirs, frozen rivers, and ancient Charter stones to find him. Armed with bells, charter magic, and a reluctant companion, she confronts Free Magic creatures and spirits that refuse death’s order. The novel combines quest fantasy with horror as it explores inheritance, duty, courage, and the boundary between life and death. Its central conflict turns on whether Sabriel can claim her father’s role and stop a rising power from breaking the kingdom’s fragile protections.
book-7470: Chicago private investigator Harry Dresden works cases the police cannot explain because he is also a practicing wizard, listed in the phone book under “Wizard.” In this graphic novel adaptation, a double murder involving impossible forces pulls him into a criminal underworld of mob figures, occult practitioners, and dangerous creatures stalking the city at night. As Lieutenant Karrin Murphy seeks his help and mistrusts his secrets, Dresden juggles debt, suspicion, and the risks of using magic under the scrutiny of the White Council. The story moves through rain-soaked streets, crime scenes, and spellwork, combining noir investigation with urban fantasy and horror. Its central conflict turns on uncovering who is using lethal sorcery and stopping another supernatural killing before Dresden becomes the next target.
book-7471: In sunstruck Miami, a string of grotesque murders targeting tourists draws a newspaper reporter, police detectives, and ambitious officials into a chaotic investigation. The violence is tied to a bitter campaign against Florida’s tourist economy, real-estate greed, and the destruction of mangroves, beaches, and wildlife. As the case widens, a rogue band of conspirators exploits media spectacle, local corruption, and public fear, turning the city’s kitsch attractions and waterfront sprawl into scenes of menace. The novel combines mystery and thriller plotting with sharp satire of boosterism, tabloid journalism, political vanity, and environmental damage. Through kidnappings, bomb threats, and absurd civic pageantry, it presents South Florida as a place where paradise, commerce, and violence collide.
book-7472: Set in a decaying Egyptian coastal town, this literary thriller follows an investigation into the public death of a young woman whose body is found hanging in a square, an image that exposes the town’s buried violence. As witnesses, neighbors, and old acquaintances remember her life, the narrative pieces together a social map of alleys, apartment blocks, cafés, and strained families. The central conflict lies less in solving a simple mystery than in confronting the corruption, cruelty, sexual repression, and everyday humiliation that shape the community around her. Shifting between memory, rumor, and inquiry, the novel studies how a place manufactures its victims and its lies. Themes include social decay, gendered power, collective guilt, urban marginality, and the thin line between investigation and obsession.
book-7473: Life in the small Pacific Northwest town of Cedar Cove unfolds through intertwined domestic and romantic dilemmas centered on the house at 204 Rosewood Lane, where family strain, grief, and new attachment shape everyday decisions. Grace Sherman faces pressure from her daughters and questions about her late husband while trying to build a future with Cliff Harding. Judge Olivia Lockhart remains a steady presence as friends and neighbors bring their private troubles into public view. Across porches, kitchens, church gatherings, and local streets, characters confront trust, forgiveness, widowhood, and the challenge of beginning again after disappointment. The novel uses community gossip, family conversations, and courtship to explore how love, faith, and loyalty are tested in an intimate coastal setting.
book-7474: In Atlanta, Georgia Bureau of Investigation agents Faith Mitchell and Sara Linton are pulled into a murder case when a woman’s body is found in a filthy, abandoned apartment linked to drug traffic and police corruption. The evidence points toward Will Trent, who has vanished into a dangerous undercover operation and appears to be entangled with violent criminals and with his volatile wife, Angie Polaski. As Faith and Sara try to determine whether Will is hunting suspects or becoming one, the investigation moves through crack houses, squad rooms, and hidden networks of dirty cops. The novel combines procedural detection with psychological suspense, focusing on divided loyalties, addiction, intimate violence, and the strain that secrecy places on trust, friendship, and romance.
book-7475: At Bathory High, sixteen-year-old Vladimir Tod tries to survive eleventh grade while hiding a dangerous secret: he is a half-vampire with growing powers and enemies in both the human and vampire worlds. After the death of his guardian, he is pulled deeper into vampire politics, prophecy, and family history, even as school, friendships, and first love demand ordinary teenage choices. New attacks and unsettling messages suggest that someone is hunting him, and training meant to protect him only reveals how unprepared he is for what is coming. Set in a small-town high school shadowed by undead rivalries, the novel combines horror, dark fantasy, and coming-of-age tension, focusing on identity, grief, secrecy, loyalty, and the cost of accepting a monstrous inheritance.
book-7476: A down-at-heel actor in a future interplanetary society is hired for an unusual political role: he must impersonate a missing statesman whose speeches and presence shape relations between Earth, Mars, and the colonies. Set among campaign headquarters, passenger liners, and Martian diplomatic ceremonies, the novel turns theatrical craft into a tool of state. The central conflict lies in sustaining the deception while navigating hostile party rivals, public scrutiny, and the ethical weight of speaking for another man. As the performance deepens, questions of identity, responsibility, and political leadership come to the foreground. The story combines electoral intrigue, body doubles, and Solar System world-building, especially its attention to Martian customs and the fragile diplomacy between human and alien societies.
book-7477: An FBI profiler returns to a rural Nebraska community when a series of child abductions and ritualized murders suggests that a notorious serial killer may have resumed hunting. Maggie O'Dell works with local law enforcement, including a sheriff under pressure from frightened parents and a town shaken by rumor, grief, and suspicion. As the investigation moves through farmhouses, churches, schools, and isolated roads, the case links forensic evidence with the hidden histories of families and the emotional aftershocks of earlier crimes. The novel combines police procedure, psychological suspense, and a restrained romantic thread while focusing on predation, trauma, religious imagery, and the difficulty of separating evil acts from the ordinary surfaces of small-town life.
book-7478: Drawing on personal stories, Christian spirituality, and everyday setbacks, Anne Lamott reflects on three brief prayers she sees as basic forms of human speech to God: asking for help, expressing thanks, and responding with wonder. The book moves through ordinary settings—family life, friendship, addiction recovery, grief, and moments of beauty—to argue that prayer does not require polished language, certainty, or piety. Instead, it presents prayer as a practice of honesty, dependence, and attention in the middle of mess, fear, and joy. Memoir and spiritual guidance intertwine as Lamott considers vulnerability, gratitude, faith, and doubt, showing how simple words can frame a life shaped by need, connection, and awe.
book-7479: Across the coastlands of Mossflower, a restless young hare named Tammo leaves home to join the Long Patrol, the fighting force that serves the badger rulers of Salamandastron. His training in the mountain fortress unfolds as a ruthless vermin warlord gathers an army and begins a brutal march across fields, woodlands, and abbey lands. The story follows military patrols, forced marches, skirmishes, and journeys between Redwall Abbey and the western shore, bringing together hares, mice, otters, and other woodland creatures against a common enemy. Alongside battles and escapes, the novel explores courage, discipline, loyalty, grief, and the cost of leadership. It combines quest adventure, animal fantasy, and the recurring Redwall setting of abbeys, caves, shorelines, and forest strongholds.
book-748: Telepathic waitress Sookie Stackhouse navigates a volatile Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires have revealed themselves, shape-shifters face growing hostility, and the hidden world of the fae begins to break into everyday life. After a local shifter is murdered and Sookie’s own fairy blood draws dangerous attention, she is pulled into a tangle of missing persons, family secrets, and supernatural reprisals. While her relationship with vampire Eric Northman remains complicated, pressure from vampire politics, pack loyalties, and anti-supernatural violence leaves her with few safe allies. The novel combines small-town crime, paranormal horror, and romantic tension, focusing on identity, prejudice, kinship, and the cost of belonging to several worlds at once.
book-7480: Drawing on archaeology, criminology, military history, psychology, and statistics, this work argues that violence has declined over long stretches of human history, from tribal raiding and homicide to torture, slavery, and war between states. It surveys prehistoric remains, medieval crime records, early modern justice, the rise of commerce and centralized government, and the twentieth century’s paradox of catastrophic world wars alongside falling rates of interpersonal and political killing. The central argument weighs human impulses toward dominance, revenge, and cruelty against capacities for empathy, self-control, reason, and moral reflection. Across discussions of civilizing institutions, Enlightenment ideals, literacy, cosmopolitan exchange, and human rights movements, it examines how social norms change and asks why modern societies have become less tolerant of bloodshed.
book-7481: A sequence of children’s poems moves through nurseries, gardens, rainy streets, and imagined islands, pairing everyday English childhood with comic fantasy. Verses about a king’s breakfast, a bear named Edward, a swan called The Emperor of the River, and a boy who changes into a knight or explorer turn small domestic moments into adventures. Christopher Robin appears as a recurring child figure, while Ernest H. Shepard’s illustrations anchor the scenes in Edwardian drawing rooms, parks, and toy-filled bedrooms. The collection balances nonsense rhyme, gentle satire, and lyrical observation, with themes of play, make-believe, family routines, and the way children’s logic reshapes the adult world. Several poems introduce the tone and characters later associated with Winnie-the-Pooh.
book-7482: In a suburban Louisiana neighborhood during a long, hot summer, an adult narrator looks back on his early adolescence and the violent attack on the girl next door he has secretly adored. As police search for the assailant, the boy tries to make sense of suspicion, gossip, and the hidden lives of adults and children around him. The mystery of the crime drives the plot, but the novel also traces first desire, shame, family strain, and the loss of innocence. Streets, backyards, bicycles, and humid evenings create a vivid Baton Rouge setting where ordinary routines are unsettled by fear. Through memory and investigation, the story examines how communities construct explanations, how young people misunderstand what they witness, and how trauma alters a neighborhood’s shared past.
book-7483: A suspicious death draws forensic pathologist Lisa O'Malley into a homicide investigation that quickly widens beyond a single body.
