When Robin’s reckless raids draw new enemies and old loyalties begin to fray, Scarlet must navigate suspicion, violence, and the return of figures from her past. Blending historical adventure with romance and legend, the novel follows thefts, ambushes, and court intrigue while exploring identity, survival, trust, and the cost of belonging to a rebellion.
book-7658: Set in a Tennessee high school and its surrounding church community, this young adult romance follows Parker Shelton, a star softball player trying to hold together her reputation, friendships, and faith after her family is shaken by a public scandal involving her pastor father. At school she focuses on the softball field and the possibility of college recruitment, while at church she faces gossip, exclusion, and pressure to remain the dependable girl everyone expects. Her growing connection with Brian, an assistant baseball coach, complicates her sense of right and wrong and exposes the gap between private desire and public judgment. The novel centers on first love, athletic ambition, religious community, family shame, and the struggle to define identity when trust in parents, friends, and belief begins to fracture.
book-7659: At a summer community on the North Carolina coast, Riley Griggs plans to sell the family beach house after her marriage collapses, but the weekend unravels when her estranged husband disappears and his body is soon found in the water. As police question his business dealings and private life, Riley sorts through hidden debts, secret relationships, and grudges that ripple through Belle Isle’s tightly linked circle of neighbors, in-laws, and seasonal residents. The novel combines beach-town domestic life with a murder investigation, following Riley as she protects her home, reconsiders her future, and tests old loyalties. Themes of betrayal, friendship, financial ruin, second chances, and the uneasy gap between public respectability and private deception drive the story.
book-766: An imprisoned sovereign of dreams escapes after decades of captivity and returns to a damaged realm in this fantasy horror graphic novel set across twentieth-century England and the United States. Morpheus, also called Dream of the Endless, finds his kingdom in ruin, his subjects scattered, and the tools of his power stolen. His search leads through occult mansions, nightmare landscapes, Arkham Asylum, and ordinary diners where human cruelty and desire surface under supernatural pressure. The collection combines myth, dark fantasy, and urban horror, introducing figures such as Lucien, Cain and Abel, Death, and the madman John Dee. Central conflicts involve the restoration of Dream’s authority and the consequences of trying to control sleep, stories, and imagination.
book-7660: In the hidden New York community called Fabletown, exiled figures from folklore and nursery tales struggle to rebuild civic order after war with the Adversary. This volume follows the political and emotional fallout as King Cole resigns, a new mayoral election divides the community, and Snow White and Bigby Wolf confront the consequences of their relationship. Around them, familiar names such as Prince Charming, Bluebeard, and Flycatcher pursue power, revenge, or private redemption. The stories move between city streets and the upstate Farm where nonhuman fables live under guard, combining murder investigation, court intrigue, and dark fairy-tale history. Themes of leadership, exile, class tension, and the gap between legendary identities and ordinary governance shape a fantasy mystery rooted in bureaucracy as much as enchantment.
book-7661: In late nineteenth-century Rio de Janeiro, a withdrawn lawyer known as Dom Casmurro reconstructs his youth in an effort to “tie together the two ends of life.” He recalls his childhood bond with Capitu, the clever neighbor he loves, and the family vow that threatens to send him to the seminary instead of toward marriage. As his memoir moves from adolescence to domestic life, affection gives way to suspicion, and the narrative centers on jealousy, social ambition, and the instability of memory. Through Bentinho’s self-justifying voice, the novel examines whether love can survive doubt, how class and reputation shape private choices, and how narration itself can distort the truth. The setting of parlors, churches, and streets of imperial Brazil grounds an intimate psychological drama.
book-7662: A sprawling comic conspiracy novel moves through 1970s New York, Las Vegas, Europe, and hidden enclaves where every rumor about secret power appears partly true. Journalists, police officers, occultists, anarchists, billionaires, and assassins become entangled in plots involving the Bavarian Illuminati, Discordian pranksters, fascist cells, psychedelic experiments, ancient artifacts, and apocalyptic schemes. The narrative shifts rapidly among viewpoints, documents, and hallucinations, treating politics, religion, sex, and science as competing systems for organizing chaos. Its central conflict concerns who controls reality: governments, clandestine societies, or individuals trying to think beyond programmed belief. Themes include paranoia, information overload, manipulation, freedom, and the instability of truth, with absurdist humor and science-fictional speculation used to turn conspiracy culture into both adventure story and philosophical satire.
book-7663: Teenager Alex Sawyer is wrongly convicted of murder and sent to Furnace Penitentiary, a vast prison buried beneath the earth where violent juvenile offenders disappear behind steel doors and endless concrete corridors. Inside, survival depends on avoiding inmate gangs, brutal guards, and the nightly opening of cells when masked enforcers drag prisoners away. Rumors spread about the Wheezers and the creatures made in the prison’s hidden laboratories, turning confinement into a science-fiction nightmare as much as a criminal sentence. Alex searches for allies and for a way to escape, while the prison’s machinery grinds down identity, trust, and hope. Set in a claustrophobic underground institution, the novel centers on injustice, fear, bodily transformation, and resistance to a system built on punishment and secrecy.
book-7664: In wartime England, an elderly retired detective living quietly among his beehives is drawn back into inquiry when a Jewish refugee boy in his village loses the parrot that is his only companion and a local man is found murdered. The bird’s string of German words and numbers, the child’s silence, and the atmosphere of secrecy around displaced persons and intelligence work turn a small-country investigation into a puzzle shaped by Europe’s catastrophe. Set in 1944 on the Sussex coast, the novella follows a Holmes-like mind confronting clues that point beyond ordinary motive toward exile, coded language, and the trauma carried by children uprooted by war. Its themes include memory, grief, Jewish displacement, and the limits of deduction in the face of historical violence.
book-7665: On Nantucket, a family of women gathers around an aging beach house and the summer business that has shaped their lives. Abby Chadwick, practical and recently widowed, struggles to hold together her household while her three grown daughters face their own upheavals in love, work, and identity. Conflicts over marriage, money, responsibility, and old resentments surface as the sisters return to the island’s dunes, harbors, and crowded seasonal rituals. The novel follows romances, breakups, and family arguments against a coastal New England setting of cottages, ferries, and shifting tides. Its central concerns are mother-daughter bonds, sisterhood, second chances, and the tension between independence and belonging, with Nantucket itself acting as both refuge and pressure point for change.
book-7666: In a bizarre America where poultry is illegal after a devastating avian flu epidemic, FDA agent Tony Chu investigates food-related crimes with a disturbing gift: he can receive psychic impressions from whatever he eats. This volume follows Chu as his cases expand beyond routine inspections into murders, conspiracies, and the search for clues hidden in meals, corpses, and contraband chicken. Set in restaurants, crime scenes, and government offices, the story mixes detective work with grotesque comedy and sharp visual exaggeration. Central tensions grow between Chu’s duty as a federal investigator, the physical cost of using his cibopathic power, and the increasingly secretive forces surrounding the bird flu disaster. Themes include appetite, surveillance, corruption, disgust, and the absurd overlap of bureaucracy and violence.
book-7667: Set in the American South, this horror novel follows a drifting group of vampires and the young people drawn into their orbit. In the small town of Missing Mile, North Carolina, a teenage boy named Nothing learns disturbing truths about his origins, while in New Orleans a reckless vampire named Zillah moves through clubs, highways, and decaying houses with his companions. Their paths converge in a landscape of punk music, addiction, violence, and hunger. The central conflict turns on identity, belonging, and the seductive pull of predation as human and undead desires collide. Blending gothic fantasy with literary fiction, the novel explores family, alienation, queer desire, and the damage left by beauty, obsession, and the search for connection.
book-7668: In late Victorian London, a shopkeeper named Mr. Verloc moves between a shabby Soho household and a shadowy circle of anarchists, informers, and foreign diplomats. Pressured by an embassy contact to stage a sensational act of terrorism, he becomes entangled in a plot centered on the Greenwich Observatory, drawing his wife Winnie and her vulnerable brother Stevie into mounting danger. The novel treats espionage and political violence as ordinary urban business, showing police inspectors, radicals, and bureaucrats linked by secrecy, self-interest, and surveillance. Set in lodging houses, streets, and government offices, it examines terrorism, conspiracy, marriage, exploitation, and the gap between public ideology and private motive, while tracing how a single planned outrage disturbs both a family and the city around it.
book-7669: A concise introduction to Zen Buddhism traces its development from Indian Mahayana thought through Chinese Ch’an to Japanese Zen, placing meditation, discipline, and direct experience at the center of the tradition. Alan W. Watts explains key ideas such as emptiness, nonduality, the limits of conceptual thought, and the relation between self, nature, and everyday action. The book contrasts Zen with Western habits of analysis and with more doctrinal forms of religion, arguing that Zen points toward an immediate awareness that cannot be captured fully in language. Historical background, religious vocabulary, and examples from monastic practice, art, and poetry situate Zen in its cultural setting. Themes include consciousness, identity, liberation from ego, and the tension between intellectual understanding and lived insight.
book-767: Set in the racetracks, ranches, and newspapers of 1930s America, this narrative history follows the undersized thoroughbred Seabiscuit and the three damaged men whose fortunes become tied to him: owner Charles Howard, trainer Tom Smith, and jockey Red Pollard. It traces the horse’s rise from overlooked also-ran to national sensation during the Great Depression, when crowds invest his races with hope and defiance. The account details the mechanics of horse racing, cross-country travel, injuries, betting culture, and the rivalry that leads toward a celebrated match race with War Admiral. Alongside the sporting story, it examines class mobility, resilience, risk, and the bond between humans and animals, showing how a racehorse becomes a public symbol in a period of economic hardship and mass spectacle.
book-7670: In a near-future United States shaped by surveillance, bioengineering, and covert warfare, a new nanotech drug allows people to connect mind to mind, sharing thoughts, skills, and emotions through a programmable neural network. The invention promises radical empathy and collective intelligence, but it also threatens governments, intelligence agencies, and religious extremists who fear any technology that can rewrite human consciousness. At the center is Kaden Lane, a young scientist drawn into a struggle between research ethics, state control, and the temptation to push evolution forward by force. The novel combines laboratory science, black-ops missions, courtroom politics, and digital security with questions about privacy, free will, addiction, and whether human connection becomes liberation or a weapon when thought itself can be hacked.
book-7671: Set in England after the Norman Conquest, this historical romance follows Aislinn, a Saxon noblewoman whose home is seized in war, and Wulfgar, the Norman knight who claims her castle by force of King William’s victory. Their relationship begins in captivity and hostility, shaped by conquest, class, and the brutal politics of occupied land. As Aislinn struggles to protect her people and preserve her dignity, Wulfgar must balance military duty, ambition, and a growing attachment that complicates his power over her. The novel centers on castle life, feudal loyalties, and the uneasy merging of Saxon and Norman worlds. Themes of coercion, survival, desire, revenge, and the possibility of trust drive a story grounded in medieval conflict and unequal power.
book-7672: In a future Chicago divided into rigid factions, a young Dauntless leader named Tobias Eaton, known as Four, investigates growing unrest inside his faction. Set alongside the early events of the Divergent series, the story follows his discovery of secret alliances, manipulated loyalties, and plans that threaten both Dauntless and the city’s fragile social order. As he watches authority harden into coercion, he must weigh obedience against conscience and decide whom he can trust. The novella centers on surveillance, betrayal, faction politics, and the cost of resistance within a controlled society. Told as a young adult science-fiction episode, it expands Four’s perspective on power, identity, and moral choice while showing the pressures that turn discipline and bravery into instruments of violence.
book-7673: Set in a small town in County Wexford in the late 1960s, this novel follows Nora Webster, a recently widowed mother of four, as she tries to rebuild a life after her husband’s death. Daily routines of shopping, office work, childrearing, and visits from neighbors become charged with grief, scrutiny, and financial pressure. Nora resists the expectations of relatives, priests, and local gossip while negotiating loneliness, anger, and the demands of motherhood. As Ireland changes around her, she slowly tests new forms of independence through work, music, friendship, and the management of her household. The narrative examines mourning, female autonomy, family obligation, and the quiet tensions of provincial Irish society with close attention to domestic spaces and ordinary speech.
book-7674: A young woman drawn into a hidden world of angels, demons, and prophecy struggles to protect her relationship as supernatural violence closes in around her. Set in contemporary America but rooted in biblical mythology, the novel follows a romance strained by secrecy, destiny, and the threat of possession and death. Family loyalty, forbidden love, and faith shape the conflict as human lives become entangled with ancient powers and apocalyptic stakes. Scenes of horror and suspense accompany the central love story, with stalkers, visions, and deadly confrontations pushing the characters toward difficult choices about trust and sacrifice. The book blends paranormal romance with dark fantasy, focusing on how devotion survives fear, grief, and the knowledge that the person one loves may also be the gateway to catastrophe.
book-7675: Former U.S. operative Cotton Malone is drawn into a high-stakes chase that links modern Chinese power struggles to a secret buried with the first emperor of China. Moving through Beijing, remote tomb complexes, and diplomatic back channels, the novel follows competing factions seeking an ancient clue said to affect the future of Taiwan, the Chinese presidency, and a vast hidden legacy. Assassins, intelligence operatives, and political insiders pursue the same prize as Malone tries to untangle court intrigue, family ambition, and historical deception. The story blends archaeological mystery with geopolitical suspense, using imperial burial chambers, rare artifacts, and state secrets to explore legitimacy, succession, nationalism, and the ways ancient history continues to shape present-day conflict.
book-7676: A tense Boston police procedural follows Detective D.D. Warren as she investigates a series of murders that suggest a predator with a highly specific obsession. The case intersects with the work of a child psychiatrist who counsels children marked by violence, neglect, and trauma, raising questions about whether buried memories, family secrets, and childhood abuse connect the victims. As the inquiry moves through apartments, clinics, and crime scenes, the novel balances forensic detail with psychological suspense, focusing on how fear shapes witnesses, investigators, and survivors. Central conflicts emerge between official evidence and damaged recollection, and between the urge to protect vulnerable children and the risk of exploiting them. Themes include trauma, memory, maternal responsibility, and the lasting consequences of violence within families.
book-7677: A wide-ranging home baking cookbook gathers recipes for cakes, cookies, pies, tarts, muffins, scones, breads, and holiday desserts, with an emphasis on practical technique and dependable results in an ordinary kitchen. It presents sweet and savory preparations, from everyday treats to celebratory pastries, and explains the core methods behind mixing batters, working dough, lining tart pans, baking custards, and judging doneness. The organizing idea is the transmission of recipes from a personal kitchen to other home bakers, so the writing focuses on clarity, ingredients, equipment, timing, and small problem-solving details. Themes of domestic craft, hospitality, and culinary memory run through the collection, while step-by-step instructions and notes help readers understand both classic American baking staples and more elaborate desserts that require planning and precision.
book-7678: Set in an affluent New England suburb, this contemporary novel follows a marriage disrupted when a young wife and mother faces a life-threatening illness. Daily routines of school runs, dinner tables, and country-club friendships give way to hospital appointments, fear, and difficult conversations about parenting, loyalty, and the future. As her husband struggles between hope and the practical demands of caring for their family, the couple must confront old expectations about love, duty, and the promises marriage requires people to keep when circumstances change. The story treats romance through the lens of domestic life rather than courtship, focusing on family bonds, vulnerability, grief, and the uneasy balance between privilege and emotional insecurity. Themes include illness, devotion, motherhood, and what commitment means under pressure.
book-7679: In the small Indiana town of Brownsburg, florist Febra “Feb” Landry has spent years trying to live around the wreckage of her breakup with police lieutenant Alexander Colton, the man she once expected to marry. Their uneasy distance collapses when women connected to old secrets begin turning up dead and the pattern points back to a traumatic crime from their teenage years. As the investigation tightens, Feb and Colt are forced into close contact, reopening anger, grief, and unresolved desire while a killer moves through familiar streets. Blending contemporary romance with police procedural suspense, the novel centers on second chances, hometown history, loyalty, and the long reach of violence, asking whether love can survive betrayal, memory, and the danger stalking both past and present.
book-768: U.S. Marshal Teddy Daniels arrives at Ashecliffe Hospital, a fortresslike asylum for the criminally insane on a remote island off Massachusetts, to investigate the disappearance of a patient who seems to have vanished from a locked ward. Accompanied by his new partner, he confronts evasive doctors, rigid orderlies, and a gathering storm that cuts the island off from the mainland. As the search deepens, clues point toward hidden experiments, institutional violence, and secrets tied to Teddy’s wartime memories and the death of his wife. Set in the 1950s, the novel combines detective investigation with psychological horror, using claustrophobic corridors, crashing surf, and shifting testimony to explore paranoia, trauma, guilt, and the unstable boundary between sanity and delusion.
book-7680: At a Japanese high school, Risa Koizumi and Atsushi Ootani become an odd comic pair: she is unusually tall for a girl, and he is unusually short for a boy. Their constant bickering makes classmates treat them like a comedy act, yet both are preoccupied with the same problem—how to find romance while feeling out of step with conventional ideas about height, attractiveness, and femininity or masculinity. As they trade insults, compare crushes, and reluctantly help each other with dating schemes, friendship begins to complicate their self-image. The manga combines school comedy with a romance built on insecurity, public embarrassment, and emotional mixed signals. Themes include body image, adolescence, peer pressure, and the gap between how teenagers perform confidence and how vulnerable they feel.
book-7681: At a literary gathering, a careless question revives an old scandal: years earlier, General Alistair Ravenscroft and his wife, Margaret, were found dead beside a pistol, and no one ever knew whether the case was murder, suicide, or some darker arrangement. Asked to help untangle the mystery for the sake of the couple’s grown daughter, Hercule Poirot joins Ariadne Oliver in reconstructing the past from the memories of aging governesses, relatives, servants, and family friends—the “elephants” who still remember. Moving between drawing rooms, country houses, and the long shadows of an English family tragedy, the novel turns on unreliable recollection, hidden motives, class manners, and the way old crimes continue to shape the living.
book-7682: Set in a contemporary urban world of text messages, late-night calls, and tightly guarded routines, this romance follows a young woman who depends on a witty long-distance friendship with a man she has never met in person. Their banter creates intimacy and comic warmth, but the relationship becomes complicated when real life, attraction, and painful histories push against the safety of the “just friends” label. As the connection deepens, the story balances flirtation and humor with darker material involving trust, vulnerability, and the lingering effects of trauma. The central conflict turns on whether emotional closeness can survive secrets, fear, and changing expectations once friendship shades into desire. Themes include chosen family, healing, loyalty, and the risks involved in letting another person truly see one’s private self.
book-7683: Organized as a month-by-month guide to infancy, this parenting manual follows a baby’s first year from the early weeks after birth through feeding, sleep, growth, and developmental milestones. It addresses practical questions about breastfeeding and formula, introducing solid foods, crying, colic, diapering, bathing, teething, illness, safety, travel, and child care, while also covering maternal recovery, parental stress, and changing family routines. The central aim is to help caregivers interpret infant behavior and make informed decisions during a period marked by uncertainty, exhaustion, and rapid change. Its subject is not fiction but everyday newborn and baby care in the home, with attention to medical guidance, common concerns, and the emotional transition to life with an infant.
book-7684: Set in a conservative American town in the 1950s, this historical romance follows a sheltered teenage girl whose first serious love collides with rigid family expectations, religious authority, and the era’s harsh judgments about sex and reputation. When an unexpected pregnancy upends her future, adults around her make decisions that expose the limited choices available to young women and the power families wield over secrecy, shame, and motherhood. The novel traces the emotional consequences of separation, silence, and sacrifice as the characters move through adolescence into adulthood. Themes of first love, parental control, class respectability, and the long afterlife of a hidden child shape a story centered on loss, forgiveness, and the hope of reunion.
book-7685: Set in Little Rock, Arkansas, in 1958, this historical novel follows a shy twelve-year-old girl whose carefully quiet life changes when she forms an intense friendship with a new girl at school. Their bond develops against the aftermath of the Little Rock Nine and the closing of the city’s public high schools to resist desegregation. As racial segregation shapes classrooms, neighborhoods, and family expectations, the narrator confronts prejudice she has barely questioned and silence she has long used for protection. The story centers on loyalty, moral courage, and the risks of speaking when adults demand obedience. Through school routines, church life, and tense city politics, it explores how racism divides a community and how friendship can force a child toward difficult choices.
book-7686: A self-help guide argues that lasting change begins with an accurate understanding of personal identity rather than with surface goals or quick behavioral fixes. Drawing on concepts from psychology, values clarification, and personal responsibility, it asks readers to examine the beliefs, habits, and family narratives that shape everyday choices. The discussion focuses on how people construct a public image, hide unmet needs, and drift into roles that conflict with their core convictions. Through exercises and reflective prompts, it presents a process for identifying a “true self,” defining priorities, and aligning work, relationships, health, and decision-making with those priorities. Central themes include authenticity, self-knowledge, accountability, emotional honesty, and the tension between external approval and an internally directed life.
book-7687: A zombie outbreak has collapsed the United States into scattered camps, empty highways, and violent ruins, and a teenager named Remy travels south with her younger brother after losing their home. As they move through abandoned towns and military checkpoints, they join other survivors whose motives are not always clear. The central conflict follows their attempt to reach safety while facing infected attackers, armed strangers, and the strain of fear inside the group itself. Set in a near-future American wasteland, the novel combines survival horror with a young adult coming-of-age story. Themes include sibling loyalty, trust under pressure, grief, and the moral compromises people make when ordinary social order disappears.
book-7688: A comedic manga reimagines world history and international politics through personified nations, with Italy, Germany, Japan, and other countries appearing as bickering, anxious, proud, or clueless young men. Episodic scenes draw on World War I and World War II, diplomatic rivalries, military alliances, and national stereotypes, turning battles, treaties, and cultural misunderstandings into short gags. Much of the humor centers on Italy’s cowardice and love of pasta, Germany’s rigid discipline, and Japan’s reserve, while England, France, America, Russia, and others enter to complicate every encounter. Beneath the parody, the volume uses cartoon conflict to explore nationalism, historical memory, cultural identity, and the absurdity of war. The graphic format emphasizes quick visual jokes, exaggerated expressions, and compact historical references rather than a single continuous plot.
book-7689: A young clownfish named Nemo is taken from the Great Barrier Reef and carried to a dentist’s aquarium in Sydney, leaving his anxious father Marlin to cross the open ocean in search of him. Along the way, Marlin travels with Dory, a forgetful blue tang whose optimism and short memory create both trouble and unexpected help. Their route passes sharks, jellyfish, sea turtles, and deep-sea predators, while Nemo faces his own fears inside the fish tank and plans escape with its other inhabitants. Set in vivid underwater landscapes, the story combines adventure, separation, and reunion with themes of parental fear, courage, disability, friendship, and learning to trust others. Its fantasy elements come through talking sea creatures and a stylized marine world shaped for young readers.
book-769: A consulting detective in Victorian and Edwardian Britain applies acute observation, forensic logic, and knowledge of human behavior to murders, thefts, disappearances, blackmail schemes, and baffling domestic secrets. Across London fog, country estates, boarding houses, and foreign outposts, Sherlock Holmes and his companion Dr. John Watson investigate clients from every social rank, confronting criminals, impostors, conspiracies, and the limits of official policing. The collection brings together short stories and novels that establish the classic detective formula: clues hidden in ordinary objects, interviews that expose motive, and confrontations in drawing rooms, alleyways, and lonely moors. Beneath the puzzles, the fiction examines reason and intuition, friendship, professional ethics, class anxiety, urban modernity, and the thin boundary between respectable society and violence.
book-7690: A trip to the doctor becomes a chain of misunderstandings in this early reader about Amelia Bedelia, a housekeeper whose literal way of hearing words turns ordinary instructions into comic confusion. Set in familiar places such as a home, a doctor’s office, and the spaces of daily errands, the story follows her as she tries to be helpful while misreading common phrases and medical directions. The central action comes from the gap between what adults mean and what Amelia Bedelia thinks they mean, creating jokes built on wordplay, idioms, and practical mishaps. Clear sentences, repetition, and exaggerated situations support new readers, while the humor introduces themes of language, interpretation, patience, and the small chaos that can grow from everyday communication.
book-7691: In an alternate Victorian world where werewolves, vampires, and steam-powered contraptions shape public life, Alexia Maccon leaves London for Egypt with her unusual infant daughter and a small circle of allies. The journey follows political upheaval in the supernatural community and growing questions about Alexia’s soulless nature, her child’s dangerous abilities, and the ancient forces tied to both. Desert ruins, river travel, secret societies, and academic rivalries replace drawing rooms, but the novel keeps its mix of manners, occult intrigue, and mechanical invention. As Alexia balances marriage, motherhood, and diplomacy, she confronts competing loyalties among pack, hive, and family. Themes include identity, power, empire, and the friction between scientific curiosity and supernatural tradition within a comic steampunk fantasy setting.
book-7692: Life in the small mountain town of Mitford turns on parish routines, front-porch conversations, and the private burdens carried by neighbors. Episcopal priest Father Tim Kavanagh prepares for marriage while continuing to pastor an unruly congregation, visit the sick, counsel the lonely, and navigate the steady stream of local crises and comic interruptions that define village life. Around him, shopkeepers, children, widows, and drifters bring questions of grief, forgiveness, vocation, and belonging into ordinary scenes of suppers, church events, and quiet walks. Set in contemporary North Carolina, the novel treats faith less as doctrine than as daily practice, tracing how community, prayer, aging, and commitment shape a middle-aged clergyman’s inner life. Themes of spiritual growth, domestic change, and pastoral care guide the episodic narrative.
book-7693: Drawing on the growth of Google from start-up to global technology company, this management guide explains how internet-era businesses organize people, ideas, and decisions. It focuses on hiring “smart creatives,” employees who combine technical depth, business judgment, and initiative, and argues that speed, openness, and data-driven experimentation matter more than rigid hierarchy. The book moves through corporate culture, product development, communication, strategy, talent management, and meetings, using examples from search, advertising, Android, and online platforms. Set within Silicon Valley and the wider software industry, its central argument is that abundant information, rapid change, and networked consumers require leaders to share information widely, empower engineers and product teams, and build companies that keep learning. Themes include innovation, scale, meritocracy, and adaptation in digital markets.
book-7694: For nine years, Sarai lives as a captive in the Mexican compound of a powerful drug lord, trapped between enforced luxury and constant threat. Her chance to flee appears when Victor Faust, a professional assassin with his own hidden agenda, arrives on business. Leaving the estate with him begins a violent flight across borders, where cartel power, hired killings, and police attention make every stop dangerous. The novel combines romantic suspense with crime thriller elements, following an uneasy alliance between a traumatized young woman seeking autonomy and a disciplined killer who survives by detachment. Themes of captivity, coercion, survival, moral ambiguity, and trust shape the story as both characters confront the consequences of violence and the possibility of choosing a different life.
book-7695: In contemporary London, Lucy Silchester drifts through a stalled career, a damaged family relationship, and the wreckage of a broken romance while telling small lies that keep everyone at a distance. Her crisis takes a fantastical turn when she receives repeated notices summoning her to meet her own life, which appears in human form and demands attention. As Lucy is forced to confront missed opportunities, unpaid emotional debts, and the gap between the person she presents and the person she is becoming, the novel blends romantic comedy with magical realism. The story centers on honesty, self-deception, grief, and second chances, using humor and surreal encounters to explore how ordinary habits, neglected relationships, and fear of change can shape a life as powerfully as any single dramatic event.
book-7696: A sequence of children’s poems moves through nurseries, gardens, woods, and make-believe kingdoms, observing the small ceremonies of early childhood with wit and exactness. Speakers and child characters count birthdays, play at kings and explorers, worry over bedtime, and transform ordinary rooms into adventurous landscapes. Familiar figures from the Hundred Acre Wood, including Winnie-the-Pooh, appear alongside Christopher Robin and a cast of nurses, animals, and toy companions. Ernest H. Shepard’s illustrations complement verses built from rhythms of conversation, repetition, and song. Rather than following a single plot, the collection gathers moments of play, loneliness, mischief, and growing self-awareness, tracing how a child tests independence while still living inside the secure structures of home, routine, and affectionate attention.
book-7697: In the coastal town of New Salem, a teenage witch remains bound to a secret coven whose members command elemental magic but fear the darker power gathering inside their circle. As rivalries sharpen, the group faces coercion from within and menace from older supernatural forces tied to families, bloodlines, and forbidden rituals. The story follows shifting loyalties among the coven’s twelve members, especially the strain between friendship, desire, and leadership, while a hidden attraction threatens fragile alliances. Scenes of spell work, charms, grimoires, and nocturnal ceremonies give the fantasy a horror edge, with possession, psychic influence, and occult violence pressing the characters toward dangerous choices. Themes include power, secrecy, jealousy, inherited responsibility, and the cost of belonging.
book-7698: After discovering that her husband has emptied their bank accounts and moved in with a younger woman, Atlanta homemaker Grace Stanton sees her carefully arranged suburban life collapse into debt, legal trouble, and public humiliation. Forced to find work and rebuild her confidence, she joins a scrappy support group for recently divorced women who meet at a local bar for “ladies’ night.” As Grace forms uneasy friendships, navigates family strain, and confronts the practical fallout of betrayal, she also becomes entangled with a neighbor whose interest complicates her resolve. Set in contemporary Atlanta, the novel blends romantic comedy with divorce drama, focusing on financial survival, female solidarity, revenge fantasies, and the slow recovery of identity after marriage ends.
book-7699: On a small island off New England, a wealthy blended family appears settled until old loyalties, jealousy, and grief begin to fracture the household. Sylvie, a magazine editor, marries into a prominent clan headed by a successful lawyer and his polished, socially demanding first wife, whose presence still shapes the children’s lives. As holidays, dinners, and school events force everyone into close contact, the family must confront rivalry between siblings, uneasy stepfamily bonds, and the pressure of class and reputation. The arrival of a child with special needs deepens existing tensions and exposes different ideas about care, responsibility, and belonging. Set in coastal houses, Manhattan offices, and private-school circles, the novel examines marriage, motherhood, privilege, and the fragile stories families tell about themselves.
book-77: Wrongly accused of theft, Stanley Yelnats is sent to Camp Green Lake, a juvenile detention camp in a dry Texas lakebed where boys spend their days digging five-foot holes under the eye of harsh wardens and counselors. As Stanley endures the heat, blisters, and arbitrary rules, he begins to suspect that the digging serves a hidden purpose. The story links his troubles to family bad luck, local outlaw history, and an old feud involving race, injustice, and survival in the desert. Shifting between past and present, the novel combines mystery, realism, and dark humor while tracing friendships among the boys and Stanley’s growing determination to understand the camp’s secrets. Themes include fate, punishment, friendship, and the long reach of buried history.
book-770: Set in ancient Rome during the collapse of the Republic, the play follows the conspiracy against Julius Caesar and the violent aftermath of his assassination. Senators led by Brutus and Cassius fear that Caesar’s growing power will destroy civic liberty, and they choose murder in the name of the commonwealth. Their act does not restore order: public rhetoric, factional loyalty, and military revenge drive Rome into chaos and civil war. Scenes move from the Senate and the Capitol to the streets, battle camps, and funeral orations, showing how private friendship collides with political duty. Written in verse and dramatic dialogue, the work examines ambition, honor, republicanism, manipulation, and the instability of popular opinion, while questioning whether noble intentions can survive the struggle for power.
book-7700: In a contemporary world shadowed by a hidden vampire race, a Breed warrior is drawn into the aftermath of a woman’s escape from years of brutal imprisonment. As the Order fights a widening conflict against corrupt Breed power and an older supernatural threat, the survivor’s damaged memory and mysterious past make her both vulnerable and dangerously important. The novel moves through urban safe houses, night streets, and the secret politics of the Breed, combining horror elements of blood, predation, and captivity with a central romance shaped by mistrust, trauma, and protective loyalty. The story explores recovery after abuse, the cost of violence, and the tension between private desire and duty to a clan at war.
book-7701: Set in Lisbon during the late nineteenth century, this novel follows the decline of the Maia family across three generations, centering on the cultivated young doctor Carlos da Maia and his circle of aristocratic friends, journalists, and politicians. As Carlos pursues a passionate love affair, family history and hidden kinship gradually turn private desire into a social and moral crisis. The narrative moves through drawing rooms, theaters, racecourses, and country estates, using gossip, letters, and conversation to map a society shaped by idleness, vanity, and frustrated ambition. Alongside its romance plot, the book studies the Portuguese upper class after liberal reforms, examining inheritance, education, adultery, provincialism, and the gap between intellectual ideals and everyday conduct. Themes include decadence, fate, family memory, and the collision between modernity and tradition.
book-7702: In a small town marked by church life, football culture, and old grief, a troubled young artist returns after years in foster care and reconnects with the girl who loved him as a child. Moses carries a violent family history, a gift that lets him see what others cannot, and a compulsive need to paint the hidden wounds and secrets around him. As his bond with Georgia deepens into first love, his visions and the town’s buried tragedies pull them toward danger and suspicion. Blending contemporary romance with supernatural horror, the novel centers on trauma, faith, guilt, and redemption, tracing how two teenagers confront abuse, loss, and the fear that loving someone damaged may also mean entering the darkness that follows him.
book-7703: Eight years after thirteen-year-old Julie Whitaker vanishes from her family’s home in Houston, a young woman appears on the doorstep claiming to be the missing daughter. Her return should end a long nightmare, but her mother, Anna, notices small mismatches in memory, manner, and speech that turn relief into suspicion. As Anna searches for the truth, the novel moves between the present-day household under strain and the hidden years of captivity, exposing the damage done by abduction, secrecy, and grief. Set in suburban Texas and on the road through a shadowy network of exploitation, the story examines trauma, identity, and the uneasy gap between the child a family lost and the stranger who comes back.
book-7704: Amid the wealth and routines of the Templeton family’s Maryland world, practical accountant Kate Powell has built her life on discipline, loyalty, and work. Raised alongside the Templeton daughters but always conscious of class difference, she manages the family business with precision and keeps her emotions tightly guarded. Her control is tested when Byron DeWitt, the sophisticated heir she has known for years, begins to see her as more than a dependable friend. As attraction deepens, Kate must confront old insecurities about money, belonging, and self-worth. At the same time, unexplained thefts and suspicious incidents around the Templeton stores introduce a thread of danger and mystery. The novel combines contemporary romance with family bonds, social ambition, trust, and hidden motives.
book-7705: Set in the affluent, insular world around Fallen Crest Academy, this young adult romance follows Sam as she remains caught between her fractured family life and the powerful Kade brothers, Mason and Logan. Gossip, loyalty, and status shape every hallway and party, turning private choices into public battles. As Sam’s relationship with Mason deepens, pressure grows from her mother, her mother’s new household, predatory classmates, and the constant scrutiny surrounding the Kade family. The novel centers on shifting friendships, possessiveness, and the way wealth and influence distort teenage relationships. Its conflict comes from Sam’s effort to protect her own sense of self while navigating jealousy, social warfare, and a home life that offers little stability. Themes include family conflict, reputation, trust, and emotional survival.
book-7706: Presented as the private journal of Fitzwilliam Darcy, this historical romance retells the events of Regency England from his point of view. The narrative moves from drawing rooms at Netherfield and Rosings to the grounds of Pemberley, tracing his guarded attraction to Elizabeth Bennet as family expectations, class prejudice, social embarrassment, and his own reserve complicate every meeting. Diary entries record his observations of Charles Bingley, Jane Bennet, George Wickham, and Lady Catherine de Bourgh, showing how misunderstandings harden into conflict and how self-scrutiny slowly alters his judgments. The novel centers on courtship, reputation, and moral growth, using the intimate first-person format to explore pride, desire, restraint, and the gap between outward manners and inward feeling.
book-7707: A murder investigation in Los Angeles pulls private detective Elvis Cole back into the wealthy Brentwood circles and old emotional territory he would rather avoid. When a former lover’s abusive former husband is found killed and she becomes the prime suspect, Cole and his partner Joe Pike begin tracing the dead man’s violent past through police files, private grudges, and buried connections among prosecutors, detectives, and affluent families. The case moves from canyon homes and courtrooms to bars, gang neighborhoods, and crime scenes, exposing how class privilege and institutional loyalty shape justice. As evidence shifts and witnesses close ranks, the novel centers on Cole’s divided loyalties, Pike’s hard-edged methods, and themes of memory, corruption, guilt, and the personal cost of pursuing the truth.
book-7708: Set in small-town Alabama, this novel follows three generations of Slocumb women whose lives are shaped by early pregnancy, family secrecy, and the long reach of the past. Fifteen-year-old Mose, practical and bright, lives with her glamorous young mother Liza and her hard-drinking grandmother Big. Their precarious household is disrupted when a small child’s skeleton is found beneath their yard, forcing old lies into the open and drawing police attention toward the family. As Liza, Big, and Mose struggle to protect one another, the story traces hidden parentage, buried trauma, addiction, class prejudice, and the fierce, tangled loyalty between mothers and daughters. Mystery and domestic drama intertwine as the women confront what has been concealed in order to imagine a different future.
book-7709: British comedian Miranda Hart mixes memoir, comic essays, and imagined conversations with her younger self to examine everyday embarrassment, family life, and the pressure to behave like a polished adult. Drawing on childhood memories, school experiences, dating misadventures, body image, work, and social rituals, she presents a running argument against self-consciousness and impossible standards of femininity. The setting shifts between home, public outings, holidays, shops, parties, and television work, with humor rooted in physical awkwardness and anxious overthinking. Beneath the jokes, the book considers confidence, loneliness, friendship, and the relief of admitting failure. Its central tension lies between the desire to fit social expectations and the persistent reality of feeling ungainly, odd, and unmistakably human.
book-771: Set in Berlin during 1933 and 1934, this narrative history follows William E. Dodd, the newly appointed American ambassador to Germany, and his daughter Martha as they enter a capital still projecting elegance while Adolf Hitler consolidates power. Drawing on letters, diaries, and official records, it traces diplomatic complacency, social fascination, and mounting evidence of state violence as the Nazi regime intimidates opponents, targets Jews, and expands its surveillance. Dodd struggles to warn Washington while navigating embassy politics and American isolation, and Martha moves through Berlin’s salons and affairs as the city darkens around her. The account examines denial, seduction by power, the limits of diplomacy, and how ordinary routines persist amid authoritarian terror.
book-7710: On the high plains of Holt, Colorado, several lives intersect as families, old bachelors, and children struggle through private hardship in a small agricultural town. Elderly ranchers Harold and Raymond McPheron continue their plain routines while confronting age, memory, and responsibility. Nearby, a frightened girl and her younger brother endure a violent, unstable home, and a troubled couple faces poverty, shame, and the strain of failed hopes. Against a landscape of feedlots, streets, schools, and open fields, the novel follows ordinary work, neighborly attention, and moments of cruelty that test the town’s fragile bonds. Kent Haruf presents domestic conflict, rural isolation, and the need for shelter, kindness, and dignity in spare scenes that examine endurance, family, and the possibility of care between people who have little language for grief.
book-7711: In a future American city where firemen burn books instead of extinguishing fires, Guy Montag serves the state by destroying printed words and the private thought they represent. His routine begins to fracture after encounters with a curious young neighbor and the growing misery inside his own home, pushing him to question a culture built on wall-sized screens, constant entertainment, censorship, and fear of dissent. As suspicion tightens around him, he moves from obedient functionary to hunted reader, confronting the cost of memory and independent judgment. Tim Hamilton’s graphic adaptation renders Ray Bradbury’s dystopian novel in panels of flame, ash, and stark urban interiors, emphasizing surveillance, mass media, anti-intellectualism, and the struggle to preserve literature against political and social conformity.
book-7712: At Hakusenkan, an elite private school, the seven highest-ranking students are separated into the privileged Special A class, where competition and gossip shape daily life. Hikari Hanazono enters determined to defeat Kei Takishima, the calm prodigy who has beaten her in every contest since childhood. Her single-minded rivalry drives comic battles over grades, sports, and pride, while Kei’s quieter attachment complicates their constant one-upmanship. Around them, the other Special A members form a tight, eccentric group whose friendships and status create misunderstandings, school events, and romantic tension. The volume blends shōjo romance with school comedy, focusing on ambition, class privilege, adolescent pride, and the gap between how characters present themselves and what they actually feel.
book-7713: On a near-future Earth at war with alien invaders called Mimics, new recruit Keiji Kiriya dies in his first combat drop and wakes to the morning before the battle. Trapped in a repeating cycle of training, deployment, and violent death, he gradually turns from an inexperienced soldier into a hardened fighter, trying to understand why the loop centers on him and how it might be broken. His path intersects with Rita Vrataski, a famous Special Forces warrior whose own connection to the battlefield suggests that his condition is not unique. Set in military bases, ruined coastlines, and mechanized infantry combat zones, the novel combines powered armor, invasion warfare, and temporal anomaly with themes of fear, discipline, survival, and the psychological cost of endless repetition.
book-7714: In first-century Galilee under Roman occupation, a Jewish boy named Daniel bar Jamin returns from years of hardship with a single purpose: revenge against the soldiers who destroyed his family. He joins a band of rebels in the hills and tries to build a secret network of resistance in his village, while also caring for his frightened sister Leah and navigating friendships with Joel, Thacia, and Simon. As unrest grows, Daniel’s fierce loyalty to violence and nationalism collides with the teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, whose presence unsettles his ideas about strength, freedom, and justice. The novel traces daily life in villages, fields, and mountain camps, and explores oppression, trauma, political revolt, family duty, mercy, and the difficult choice between hatred and forgiveness.
book-7715: A chance meeting on a flight from Paris to London leads a young man into an intense affair with Chloe, and the novel follows the relationship from first attraction through intimacy, doubt, jealousy, and separation. Set in contemporary urban Europe, it treats courtship and heartbreak as subjects for close philosophical examination, pausing over gestures, conversations, memories, and expectations. The central conflict lies between romantic idealization and the ordinary pressures that expose incompatibility: habit, miscommunication, sexual insecurity, and the desire to be fully known by another person. Blending literary fiction with reflective essay, the narrative considers why people fall in love, how they interpret signs of devotion, and how longing, projection, and self-consciousness shape modern relationships. Themes include desire, attachment, illusion, and the analysis of feeling.
book-7716: A toxic tort lawsuit in Woburn, Massachusetts, drives this narrative of environmental contamination, courtroom strategy, and scientific uncertainty. It follows plaintiffs’ lawyer Jan Schlichtmann as families who believe polluted well water caused childhood leukemia sue two large companies, while corporate attorneys, expert witnesses, and judges contest liability. The account moves between suburban neighborhoods, law offices, laboratories, and federal court, showing how epidemiology, hydrogeology, and civil procedure shape the search for proof. Central conflicts include the gap between moral outrage and legal standards, the cost of litigation, and the difficulty of tracing illness to a specific source. Themes of class, industrial pollution, ambition, and the limits of the American civil justice system frame a detailed case study of how evidence is built, challenged, and sometimes lost.
book-7717: An elderly man and woman live alone on a hillside and decide they would like one cat for company. The old man travels over mountains and valleys and finds a place crowded with cats of every color, size, and pattern—so many that he cannot choose and tries to bring home them all. What begins as a comic journey turns into a simple folktale about wanting too much, vanity, and learning to value modesty over excess. Set in a rural countryside of cottages, fields, and roads, the story uses repetition and rhythmic language to introduce counting, abundance, and animal imagery. Pen-and-ink illustrations and a pared-down narrative place the emphasis on household life, choice, and the surprising consequences of greed.
book-7718: Across the United States, a nomadic band of musicians hides an ancient secret: they are Carpathians, a dwindling race of powerful immortals who survive by blood and battle vampires. Desari, a singer fiercely protective of her chosen family, senses the approach of Julian Savage, a hunter marked by violence and isolation. Julian recognizes her as his lifemate, the one woman who can restore his emotions before darkness consumes him, but Desari resists the bond and the loss of freedom it seems to demand. As vampire attacks close in on the troupe, the novel combines paranormal romance, horror, and fantasy with clashes over trust, consent, loyalty, and the burden of predestined desire. Themes of belonging, survival, and the struggle against inner monstrosity drive the conflict.
book-7719: A Manhattan writer and obsessive keeper of other people’s secrets becomes entangled in a murder after the death of Diana Hotchkiss, a glamorous woman whose late-night calls and mysterious connections have drawn him into her orbit. Convinced that the official story does not explain what happened, he follows a trail through luxury apartments, political circles, private security firms, and hidden financial dealings. The investigation collides with his own unstable reputation, because his compulsive notebooks and voyeuristic habits make him look like an unreliable witness and a suspect. Set in contemporary New York, the thriller centers on surveillance, deception, sexual secrecy, and the way power protects itself. The novel combines amateur sleuthing with conspiracy suspense as private obsession turns into a dangerous search for the truth.
book-772: Presented as a sustained dialogue in classical Athens, this philosophical work follows Socrates as he debates justice, political order, education, and the nature of the good with a circle of interlocutors. The argument moves from the question of whether justice benefits the individual to the construction of an ideal city governed by philosopher-rulers, with detailed discussions of civic classes, censorship, poetry, mathematics, and military training. It also examines the soul, linking reason, spirit, and appetite to both personal ethics and public life. Memorable images, including the divided line, the sun, and the cave, frame its inquiry into knowledge and appearance. Major themes include power, morality, tyranny, truth, and the tension between philosophy and the practical demands of the state.
book-7720: A young narrator recounts his grandfather’s travels between Japan and the United States in an illustrated family memoir set in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Leaving his home village in Japan, the grandfather crosses the Pacific, marvels at deserts, rivers, farms, and city streets, and gradually builds a life in California. Yet he remains torn between places, returning to Japan while carrying memories of North America with him. The narrative follows immigration, return migration, and the emotional strain of loving two countries at once. Spare text and watercolor scenes focus on ships, mountains, birds, gardens, and family photographs, grounding large historical movements in ordinary experience. Themes of displacement, nostalgia, cultural identity, and intergenerational memory shape the story.
book-7721: Recently divorced from a polished Savannah lawyer, antiques picker Weezie Foley tries to rebuild her life in a city of crumbling mansions, old money, and sharp social hierarchies. Her search for estate-sale treasures and salvageable furniture leads her into disputes over inheritance, hidden property, and the suspicious death of a wealthy relative. With help from her blunt, loyal friend BeBe Loudermilk, she navigates family secrets, ex-husband drama, and the eccentric world of collectors, decorators, and Southern grande dames. Set in Savannah’s historic districts, the novel combines romantic entanglements with an amateur investigation, using humor and local color to explore reinvention, friendship, class, and the value attached to beautiful old objects.
book-7722: An archaeological dig high in the Andes uncovers a mummified Inca and a golden artifact whose impossible properties draw scientists, soldiers, and treasure hunters into a race beneath the mountains. As evidence points to a hidden labyrinth and a lost civilization preserved in volcanic depths, the expedition faces collapsing tunnels, deadly traps, and a ruthless struggle over a power that could alter modern warfare and medicine. Set in Peru among glacier fields, jungle ruins, and subterranean chambers, the novel combines expedition adventure with techno-thriller speculation. Its central conflict turns on whether ancient knowledge should be exposed, exploited, or buried, and its themes include colonial plunder, scientific ambition, survival under extreme conditions, and the dangerous lure of forbidden discovery.
book-7723: Set in the intellectual upheaval of seventeenth-century Europe, this philosophical work presents René Descartes’s attempt to ground knowledge on certainty rather than inherited authority. Through autobiographical reflection and systematic argument, he explains a method of doubt that rejects opinions, custom, and unreliable sense experience in order to find a secure starting point for thought. From that search emerges the famous claim that the thinking self can be known with certainty, followed by arguments about mind, God, nature, and the proper use of reason. The text also outlines a program for scientific inquiry based on clear ideas, analysis, and orderly deduction. Central themes include skepticism, consciousness, truth, mathematical reasoning, and the relation between philosophy, morality, and the emerging natural sciences.
book-7724: A covert campaign targets the world’s most decorated soldiers when an anonymous mastermind releases a kill list and places a vast bounty on the head of U.S. Marine officer Shane “Scarecrow” Schofield. Marked for death alongside other special-forces operatives, Schofield moves through airbases, deserts, secure compounds, and international battle zones while trying to identify who is organizing the assassinations and why. The novel combines military thriller and adventure elements: gun battles, helicopters, snipers, secret files, and improvised escapes drive the plot. Beneath the relentless pursuit, the story examines elite warfare, private money shaping violence, loyalty among soldiers, and the vulnerability of even the most heavily trained fighters when technology and conspiracy turn them into prey.
book-7725: At the International Paranormal Containment Agency, sixteen-year-old Evie faces a new crisis after the faerie realms are thrown into turmoil. Trying to build an ordinary life with her shape-shifting boyfriend Lend and her unusual friends, she is drawn back into prophecy, political intrigue, and a war that could spread from the faerie courts into the human world. Old loyalties fray as alliances shift among faeries, vampires, and other paranormal creatures, and Evie must decide whom to trust and what kind of future she wants. Set between agency headquarters, high school routines, and unstable magical territories, the novel combines supernatural adventure, romance, and dark humor while exploring identity, free will, friendship, and the cost of choosing between personal happiness and responsibility.
book-7726: Set in contemporary Berlin and the shadow of Nazi Germany, the novel follows Anna, an Australian woman recovering from divorce, who buys a long-abandoned villa on the shore of a lake. As she begins restoring the house, she uncovers clues about the Jewish family who once lived there and the wartime forces that tore them from their home. Her search through photographs, letters, and property records links present-day renovation with the hidden history of confiscation, displacement, and survival. A developing romance complicates her effort to rebuild her own life while pursuing the truth about the house’s former owners. The story combines family secrets, wartime memory, lost property, and emotional recovery, using the lake house as a focal point for questions of belonging, grief, identity, and the lasting imprint of history.
book-7727: A Buddhist monk and peace activist examines the meeting points between Buddhism and Christianity, using teachings, rituals, and spiritual practice from both traditions to explore compassion, mindfulness, suffering, prayer, and community. Set in the context of late twentieth-century interfaith dialogue, the book argues that Jesus and the Buddha offer complementary paths toward inner transformation and ethical living rather than mutually exclusive doctrines. It discusses meditation, the Holy Spirit, the Kingdom of God, the nature of peace, and the role of attentive breathing and loving action in daily life. The central focus is how believers and seekers can remain rooted in their own tradition while learning deeply from another. Themes include reconciliation, nonviolence, religious understanding, and the relationship between personal awakening and social responsibility.
book-7728: Across the scattered islands of the Archipelago, magic depends on true names, balance, and the disciplined speech of wizards. The trilogy follows Ged, first as a gifted, proud boy training in sorcery, then as a man confronting the shadow he has loosed into the world, while a parallel journey centers on Tenar, a girl raised in the dark labyrinths of the Tombs of Atuan under an ancient cult. As sea voyages carry characters among ports, towers, deserts, and dragon-haunted reaches, the central conflicts turn on power, freedom, identity, and the cost of trying to master death. The narrative combines coming-of-age fantasy with philosophical questions about equilibrium, mortality, responsibility, and the relation between human ambition and the natural order.
book-7729: After a family tragedy leaves college student Blythe McGuire isolated and barely functioning, she tries to disappear into classes and routine while carrying panic, grief, and survivor’s guilt. An invitation from her outgoing roommate pulls her into a close-knit circle of friends, where she meets Sabin, a patient young man whose steady attention challenges her instinct to withdraw. Set in contemporary campuses, apartments, and coastal outings, the story follows Blythe as she navigates trauma, intimacy, and the fear of trusting anyone with the full truth of her past. The central conflict lies between her need for connection and the emotional defenses that keep her numb. Themes include mourning, healing, friendship, anxiety, and the difficult work of learning how to live after devastating loss.
book-773: Set in Padua and nearby Verona, this comic play follows a courtship market in which Bianca, the younger daughter of Baptista, cannot marry until her older sister Katherina does. Bianca attracts multiple suitors, while Katherina is feared for her sharp tongue and refusal to submit to conventional expectations. Petruchio arrives seeking a wealthy wife and undertakes to win and “tame” Katherina, turning marriage into a contest of wit, power, performance, and public reputation. Alongside disguises, mistaken identities, and scheming servants, the action examines gender roles, obedience, economic bargaining, and the theatrical nature of social behavior. Written in verse and prose, the play combines farce and verbal sparring with an uneasy argument about authority, desire, and the pressure to conform within family and marriage.
book-7730: At the City Zoo, gentle zookeeper Amos McGee follows a daily routine with his animal friends: he races a tortoise, keeps quiet company with a shy penguin, lends a handkerchief to a rhinoceros with a cold, sits with an owl afraid of the dark, and plays chess with an elephant. When Amos wakes one morning with a fever and cannot take the bus to work, the zoo feels the absence of his steady care. In a small comic reversal, the animals set out for the city and arrive at his house to return his kindness. Set between the ordered spaces of the zoo and Amos’s cozy home, the story centers on friendship, reciprocity, illness, and the comfort of showing up for others during an ordinary sick day.
book-7731: Set in rural Montana in 1980, this novel follows Pete Snow, a troubled social worker and single father who investigates a report about a thin, neglected boy living off the grid near Fourth of July Creek. The case draws him toward Jeremiah Pearl, a paranoid survivalist who rejects schools, government, and modern society, and toward Pearl’s daughter, Benjamin, who moves between wilderness camps, bars, and back roads. As Pete struggles with his own failing relationship with his teenage daughter and the aftermath of his divorce, the novel traces collisions between state authority and radical self-reliance. Snowbound mountains, trailer homes, forests, and small-town offices frame a story about parental responsibility, masculine violence, poverty, political extremism, and the fragile line between protecting children and controlling families.
book-7732: Amid the cemeteries, bayous, and storm-dark streets of New Orleans, a killer begins stalking women connected to a notorious psychiatric institution, reviving old scandals and buried family secrets. The novel follows a woman drawn back into the case as police detectives and a skeptical lover race to identify a murderer whose methods suggest obsession, ritual, and intimate knowledge of the city’s hidden past. As clues lead through ruined hospitals, decaying mansions, and the aftermath of violence that still grips the community, the central conflict turns on whether trauma and memory can be trusted before the next attack. Blending mystery, romantic suspense, and serial-killer thriller elements, the story explores fear, guilt, inheritance, and the lingering power of institutional abuse.
book-7733: A Mississippi journalist recovering from a devastating family tragedy is drawn into the death of a close friend, a case that appears at first to be a suicide but points toward murder. Her search leads to a wealthy fertility specialist whose clinic offers hope to desperate couples while concealing a ruthless criminal enterprise. As she joins forces with an attorney and former lover, the investigation moves from small-town grief and medical records to surveillance, blackmail, and carefully staged deaths. Set in the American South, the novel combines courtroom intrigue, medical ethics, and serial-killer suspense. Its central conflict turns on proving crimes designed to look natural or self-inflicted, while themes of grief, obsession, reproductive technology, and the abuse of professional power drive the story.
book-7734: Set in rural Georgia during the Depression, this novel follows the Lester family, poor white tenant farmers trapped on exhausted land after cotton prices collapse and farming work disappears. Jeeter Lester clings to the hope of planting one more crop, even as hunger, debt, eviction, and neglect shape daily life in a collapsing sharecropping economy. Around him, family members pursue food, sex, marriage, and small schemes with a mix of desperation and indifference, exposing the damage poverty inflicts on bodies, relationships, and judgment. The narrative combines stark social observation with grotesque comedy, portraying roadside shacks, barren fields, and broken automobiles as part of a landscape of rural decline. Themes include economic ruin, class, moral erosion, racism, and the illusion of self-reliance in the American South.
book-7735: Set in mid-Victorian England, this nonfiction account reconstructs the 1860 murder of three-year-old Saville Kent at Road Hill House and follows Inspector Jonathan Whicher of Scotland Yard as he investigates the country-house crime. It traces the emerging methods of detective work—interviews, timelines, observation, and inference—against a culture obsessed with respectability, domestic privacy, and sensational newspaper coverage. As suspicion falls within the Kent family and household, the narrative examines class hierarchy, family secrets, and the public appetite for scandal. Alongside the case itself, it charts Whicher’s rise and professional ruin, showing how one unresolved investigation exposes tensions between modern policing and Victorian ideas about innocence, authority, and the hidden violence of the home.
book-7736: Set in Regency England and Paris, this historical romance follows Sebastian Ballister, Marquess of Dain, a brilliant, scandalous nobleman marked by a reckless reputation and a long history of emotional neglect. His path collides with Jessica Trent, a sharp-minded, self-possessed woman determined to protect her impractical brother from Dain’s influence. Their battle of wits turns into a public and private struggle over desire, pride, and control as attraction disrupts Jessica’s careful plans and Dain’s cultivated cynicism. Amid drawing rooms, gambling circles, family expectations, and social gossip, the novel explores class privilege, reputation, vulnerability, and the ways childhood shame shapes adult behavior. Humor and verbal sparring drive a courtship in which intelligence matters as much as passion, and marriage becomes a contest over trust, autonomy, and emotional honesty.
book-7737: Dorothy Gale is swept from a voyage at sea into the strange land of Ev, where she finds a kingdom emptied of its royal family and threatened by the underground power of the Nome King. Guided by the talking hen Billina and joined by Tik-Tok, a copper mechanical man who runs by wound-up thought, speech, and action, she travels through deserts, palaces, and caverns toward a rescue. Princess Ozma of Oz arrives with a small company to challenge the king’s enchantments and restore order. Set between the familiar plains of Kansas and a series of vividly imagined fairy realms, the novel mixes quest adventure with comic invention, emphasizing courage, loyalty, cleverness, and the unsettling instability of magic and authority.
book-7738: Reconstructing the 1889 disaster in western Pennsylvania, the narrative traces how days of rain, neglected engineering, and class privilege converge when the South Fork Dam collapses above Johnstown. It follows the flood’s path down the Conemaugh Valley into streets, mills, railroad yards, and crowded homes, showing how an industrial town is destroyed within minutes. Alongside the catastrophe itself, the account examines the dam’s ownership by the exclusive South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club, failures of maintenance, and the limits of warning and rescue. Drawing on eyewitness testimony, newspapers, and public records, it presents both a dramatic chronicle of survival and death and an argument about human error, civic responsibility, and the unequal consequences of wealth, ambition, and environmental force in the Gilded Age.
book-7739: Set in a small American town during the Christmas season, this inspirational, semi-autobiographical story follows a teenage boy who longs for a particular gift and resents the handmade sweater his mother gives him instead. As family strain, poverty, anger, and grief shape his home life, the sweater becomes a symbol of love he is not yet ready to understand. The narrative traces his movement from self-pity and rebellion toward empathy, responsibility, and spiritual awakening. Framed as a reflective tale about memory and loss, it addresses parent-child conflict, material desire, forgiveness, and the lasting meaning of sacrifice. Religious themes of grace, redemption, and gratitude place the book between memoir, moral fable, and self-help meditation.
book-774: A gifted teenage hacker has spent years imprisoned in a satellite by the Lunar regime, forced to monitor Earth’s communications for Queen Levana. When fugitive mechanic Cinder and her allies trace the source of the surveillance, they draw Cress into their widening rebellion against Luna. The story moves between Earth, orbit, and desert landscapes as the group dodges soldiers, bounty hunters, and political traps while trying to expose Levana before her royal wedding. Alongside spacecraft chases and covert rescues, the novel develops a fairy-tale framework based on Rapunzel, reworked through cybernetics, plague, and interplanetary politics. Central conflicts involve captivity, identity, manipulation, and the risks of trust, as isolated characters learn to act together against an authoritarian ruler.
book-7740: Middle school diary entries, doodles, and comic-style illustrations follow Nikki Maxwell as she navigates friendship drama, school gossip, and the chaos of crushes. Set in her familiar school world of lunch tables, hallways, and after-school events, the story centers on Nikki’s efforts to understand romance while dealing with misunderstandings that threaten her relationships with friends and the boy she likes. Her self-conscious narration turns ordinary embarrassments into slapstick scenes, from social disasters to rivalries with the popular crowd. The book blends handwritten notes, cartoons, and jokes to explore jealousy, loyalty, reputation, and the pressure to act mature before feeling ready. Themes of self-expression, kindness, and surviving adolescent heartbreak shape this humorous installment in the Dork Diaries series.
book-7741: A chain of violent earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and impossible tidal disturbances spreads across the Pacific, threatening coastal cities and global collapse. In the middle of the crisis, marine veterinarian and former deep-sea pilot Karen Grace is drawn into an international investigation that leads from secret naval facilities to drowned ruins beneath the ocean. Scientists, soldiers, and intelligence operatives race to understand a pattern linking seismic upheaval, advanced technology, and legends of a lost civilization. Set on research vessels, remote islands, and the lightless seafloor, the novel combines technothriller suspense with speculative science and undersea adventure. Its central conflict turns on whether a small team can decode the evidence before political rivalry, sabotage, and the unstable earth itself trigger planetary disaster.
book-7742: On Long Island’s North Shore, attorney John Sutter returns to the Gold Coast after years in self-imposed exile and finds the old landscape of estates, private beaches, and social codes altered by violence and money. His reappearance draws him back into the orbit of Susan Stanhope, now the widow of Mafia boss Frank Bellarosa, whose death has left behind wealth, suspicion, and unfinished business. As John renews a dangerous relationship and moves among aristocratic families, federal investigators, and organized-crime figures, he confronts the collision between inherited privilege and criminal power. The novel combines mystery and thriller elements with a close portrait of class, loyalty, betrayal, and desire, using the guarded world of gated mansions and country clubs as the setting for secrets that refuse to stay buried.
book-7743: Set on a contemporary college campus and in the small-town orbit around it, this new adult romance follows a young woman trying to rebuild her life after violence and family instability leave her wary of trust and attachment. When she forms a connection with a protective, guarded man whose own past carries grief and responsibility, attraction grows alongside fear, secrecy, and the pressure of unfinished trauma. The story centers on emotional recovery, consent, intimacy, and the difficulty of choosing vulnerability when survival has required distance. Friends, apartments, classrooms, and late-night conversations create the everyday setting, while the central conflict turns on whether two damaged people can confront what they have endured without letting shame, anger, and silence dictate their future.
book-7744: In Regency England, a proper young widow and a notoriously sensual nobleman confront a desire that has smoldered for seven years.
