Jessica Sheffield has long tried to forget Alistair Caulfield, the Earl of Pennington, whose reputation for scandal and whose magnetic presence once threatened her family’s strict expectations. When they are forced into close proximity during a journey and within London society, old attraction turns immediate and dangerous. Their relationship unfolds amid ballrooms, country estates, gossip, and rigid class etiquette, where every glance carries social risk. The novel centers on the conflict between public decorum and private longing, as grief, duty, jealousy, and sexual awakening complicate trust. Themes include female respectability, aristocratic privilege, emotional vulnerability, and the cost of choosing passion over security.
book-7745: Teen thief Katarina Bishop returns to a world of cons, forged identities, and security systems when W. W. Hale the fifth becomes entangled in a crisis involving his powerful family. The action moves through glamorous hotels, private vaults, and elite European settings, especially Monaco, where wealth and criminal strategy overlap. As Kat and her crew investigate sudden changes in Hale’s behavior, they confront guarded relatives, layered deceptions, and a scheme tied to inheritance, loyalty, and revenge. Alongside the mechanics of a high-stakes heist, the novel follows tensions within the team and the strain between Kat’s professional instincts and her feelings for Hale. Themes of trust, family obligation, secrecy, and the cost of living by the rules of thieves shape this young adult mystery.
book-7746: A dual memoir and sports history traces the intertwined careers of Larry Bird and Earvin “Magic” Johnson from their emergence as college stars to their defining rivalry in the NBA. Set in the arenas, locker rooms, and media spotlight of 1980s professional basketball, it examines how the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers become symbols of a league’s resurgence. Bird and Johnson recount fierce Finals matchups, contrasting styles of play, pressure from fans and owners, and the gradual shift from competition to friendship. Jackie MacMullan adds reporting and context on coaches, teammates, race, celebrity, and the business of the modern game. The central thread is the tension between personal ambition and mutual respect, showing how two opposing stars help shape basketball history and each other’s public identities.
book-7747: War spreads across the Silver Marches of Faerûn as dark elf ranger Drizzt Do’Urden and his companions confront the aftermath of an orc invasion and the fragile politics of the North. Set among mountain strongholds, frontier towns, and the wild spaces between Mithral Hall and the Spine of the World, the novel follows clashes between dwarves, humans, elves, and the kingdom forged by orc leader Obould Many-Arrows. Battle, pursuit, and uneasy diplomacy drive the plot while personal loyalties strain under loss, vengeance, and divided duty. Alongside sword fights and wilderness travel, the story examines prejudice between races, the cost of leadership, and the possibility of peace in a world shaped by old hatreds and constant war.
book-7748: An elderly woman receives an unusual posthumous commission when the late millionaire Jason Rafiel asks her to investigate an unnamed crime he believed only she could solve. Following his instructions, Miss Marple joins a coach tour through English country houses and picturesque villages, where the itinerary itself conceals a trail of clues. As she studies the strangers on the trip, old scandals, a vanished young woman, and the shadow of violence begin to connect across past and present. Set in drawing rooms, gardens, hotels, and quiet rural communities, the novel builds its mystery through observation, memory, and conversation rather than spectacle. Themes include justice after death, the hidden damage of family secrets, the vulnerability of women, and the contrast between genteel appearances and brutal acts.
book-7749: A badly fractured family converges in Florida for a space-shuttle launch and turns a reunion into a chain of mishaps, crimes, and uneasy confessions. The Drummonds arrive carrying divorces, addictions, financial trouble, illness, and old resentments, while a biotechnology subplot involving HIV treatment, money, and stolen materials pulls them into danger. Set among motels, hospitals, highways, and the Kennedy Space Center, the novel mixes deadpan comedy with mystery and social satire. Its central tension comes from whether relatives who barely function on their own can protect one another when scandal and violence close in. Themes include kinship, damage, media spectacle, medical ethics, and the strange ways contemporary families improvise loyalty amid chaos.
book-775: Set in late 1960s and 1970s New York, this memoir traces Patti Smith’s early life as she arrives in the city with little money and forms a lasting bond with photographer Robert Mapplethorpe. It follows their years in cheap apartments, the Chelsea Hotel, bookstores, clubs, and art studios as they try to make lives in poetry, visual art, and music. The narrative presents downtown Manhattan as a landscape of hunger, improvisation, friendship, and artistic ambition, populated by musicians, artists, and bohemians. At its center is a relationship shaped by devotion, changing desire, and mutual influence as both figures search for identity and vocation. Themes include youth, creativity, poverty, queer life, grief, and the making of an artist within a specific cultural moment.
book-7750: On the Navajo reservation in the Four Corners region, a series of violent and baffling incidents draws Lieutenant Joe Leaphorn of the Navajo Tribal Police into an investigation shaped by landscape, custom, and fear. Tracks vanish in open country, a respected healer’s ceremonial “blessing way” is invoked, and rumors of witchcraft unsettle both Navajo families and outside researchers working among them. As Leaphorn follows clues across mesas, canyons, trading posts, and isolated hogans, he weighs practical police work against beliefs that many people around him take seriously. The mystery turns on murder, hidden motives, and the hazards of cultural misunderstanding, while the novel explores Navajo religion, tribal identity, and the tension between traditional knowledge and modern institutions in the American Southwest.
book-7751: A London-born magazine editor builds a settled life with a widowed investment banker and imagines that marriage will finally give her the family she has long wanted. That hope falters when his teenage daughters arrive for the summer, bringing resentment, grief, and divided loyalties into a carefully ordered house in Connecticut. The older girl’s hostility toward her new stepmother escalates into acts that unsettle the marriage and expose the influence of the girls’ volatile mother, whose custody battle continues to shape the family. Set in affluent suburbs and vacation homes, the novel follows domestic conflict rather than courtship, focusing on stepfamily strain, adolescent anger, maternal longing, and the fragile boundaries between love, responsibility, and self-preservation.
book-7752: On the rocky Swedish coast in Fjällbacka, a young girl is found drowned, and what first appears to be a tragic accident becomes a murder investigation led by detective Patrik Hedström. As police interviews move through summer cottages, family kitchens, and old fishing streets, the case exposes tensions between parents, neighbors, and longtime residents. The inquiry gradually reaches back into earlier events in the community, connecting the child’s death to buried resentments and carefully guarded histories. Alongside the procedural work, domestic scenes from Patrik and Erica’s new family life ground the story in everyday routines disrupted by violence. The novel combines small-town crime investigation with themes of parenthood, class, cruelty, memory, and the lasting damage of secrets kept for years.
book-7753: A demanding city pigeon fixates on one impossible wish: getting a puppy. Through a comic monologue directed at the reader, the bird argues, pleads, and imagines the perfect pet, picturing a small, cuddly companion that will fit neatly into its life. The setting remains simple and uncluttered, keeping attention on the pigeon’s expressive body language, exaggerated emotions, and rapidly shifting logic. When the idea of a real puppy becomes more concrete, enthusiasm collides with the realities of size, energy, noise, and responsibility. The story turns a familiar childhood desire into a humorous lesson about impulse, expectation, and the difference between wanting something and understanding what it actually involves. Themes include pet ownership, self-awareness, disappointment, and comic exaggeration.
book-7754: Drawing on biography, moral philosophy, and social criticism, this work argues that modern culture rewards achievement, image, and personal success while neglecting humility, self-discipline, and moral depth. David Brooks contrasts the “résumé virtues” valued in careers with the “eulogy virtues” associated with kindness, courage, honesty, and service, then traces how character forms through struggle, commitment, and acknowledgment of one’s flaws. Using figures such as Augustine, Dorothy Day, and George Marshall, he examines lives shaped by failure, duty, and inner conflict rather than self-optimization alone. The book is set in the landscape of contemporary American individualism but ranges across history and religion, asking how people cultivate integrity, resist vanity, and build meaningful relationships, communities, and ethical purpose.
book-7755: Along the Magdalena River in 1830, an aging Simón Bolívar begins his last journey after resigning the presidency of Gran Colombia. Weak from illness yet still surrounded by officers, servants, and political intrigue, he moves through river towns and plantations while memories of battlefields, lovers, betrayals, and republican dreams crowd the present. The novel treats the Liberator not as a monument but as a fatigued man confronting the collapse of his unionist project and the erosion of his authority. Its central tension lies between Bolívar’s legendary public role and his private decline as enemies gather, allies waver, and exile approaches. Themes of mortality, disillusionment, memory, and the unstable legacy of revolution shape this historical portrait.
book-7756: At a military academy in Lima, adolescent cadets live under a rigid code of discipline, hazing, and masculine honor. The novel follows several boys from different social backgrounds as they navigate barracks life, classroom drills, theft, punishments, and clandestine acts of rebellion. When a violent incident and its aftermath expose corruption inside the institution, loyalty to the group collides with private conscience and fear of reprisal. Shifting among multiple perspectives, the narrative links the closed world of the academy to the wider city beyond its walls, where family expectations, class divisions, and sexual anxiety shape each student’s choices. Themes of authority, violence, humiliation, and the formation of identity drive this portrait of youth under militarized power in mid-20th-century Peru.
book-7757: At a Washington, D.C., area high school, Amy, a brilliant teenager with cerebral palsy who communicates through a computerized voice device, enters senior year determined to expand her life beyond classrooms, aides, and family routines. She persuades Matthew, a classmate living with severe obsessive-compulsive disorder, to act as her peer helper, and their arrangement grows into a complicated friendship and romance. As Amy pushes for independence and social risk, Matthew struggles with intrusive thoughts, rituals, and the fear of losing control. Their relationship brings both of them closer to ordinary teenage experiences—parties, intimacy, college plans—while exposing the limits of good intentions and the weight of other people’s expectations. The novel explores disability, mental illness, consent, autonomy, and the desire to be seen as more than a diagnosis.
book-7758: A murder in Boston draws homicide detective Jane Rizzoli and medical examiner Maura Isles into a case that reaches back to an African safari gone catastrophically wrong. Years earlier, a group of tourists on the Botswana veldt becomes stranded after a violent attack, and the survivor’s account of lions, fear, and human betrayal shadows the present investigation. As another body appears, the detectives confront a killer who studies prey, stages scenes with chilling precision, and turns hunting into ritual. Moving between urban crime scenes and the unforgiving landscape of southern Africa, the novel combines police procedural detail with survival narrative. Its central tensions involve predator and prey, trauma carried across continents, and the thin line between civilized order and primal violence.
book-7759: Set in Manhattan and written as Mia Thermopolis’s diary, this young adult novel follows a teenager who is both an awkward high school student and the heir to the throne of Genovia. As Mia navigates algebra, student politics, family drama, and the constant interference of her glamorous grandmother, she also tries to make sense of her changing relationship with Michael and the social pressures of school dances and parties. The story centers on competing loyalties between royal duty, friendship, and ordinary adolescent desires, using emails, lists, and comic observations to track each crisis. Humor drives the narrative, but beneath the jokes it examines identity, public image, first love, and the difficulty of growing up when private mistakes can feel as consequential as matters of state.
book-776: Arranged as an alphabetical museum without walls, this illustrated reference surveys hundreds of artists from the Middle Ages to the late twentieth century, placing painting, sculpture, photography, performance, video, and installation side by side. Each entry centers on a single representative work and pairs a full-page color image with a concise account of the artist’s life, materials, historical moment, and visual concerns. The volume moves across regions, schools, and movements, linking Renaissance altarpieces, Baroque portraits, modern abstraction, conceptual art, and contemporary practice in one sequence. Its central argument is that art history can be approached through images as well as chronology, and that unexpected juxtapositions reveal shared themes of religion, power, identity, the body, landscape, and experimentation with form.
book-7760: Set in a contemporary college and small-town world shaped by money, gossip, and family pressure, this romance follows a young woman trying to rebuild her sense of safety after a violent assault. Her growing relationship with a guarded, wealthy young man offers comfort and desire, but it also exposes secrets, class differences, and the scrutiny of people who think they know what happened. As rumors spread and loyalty is tested, both characters must decide whether honesty and trust can survive shame, anger, and fear. The novel blends intense emotional scenes with banter and moments of humor, focusing on trauma, recovery, consent, intimacy, and the difficulty of choosing love while still learning how to live with damage that other people cannot see.
book-7761: Set in the contemporary American South, this romantic thriller follows a woman whose ordinary life is shattered when she becomes the key witness in a violent crime. Her testimony places her at the center of a murder investigation and in the sights of a ruthless killer determined to erase the only person who can identify him. As police pressure, courtroom strategy, and public scrutiny close in, she is forced into uneasy dependence on a hard-edged lawman whose protective role becomes emotionally complicated. The plot moves through hospitals, police stations, and small-town streets, balancing procedural suspense with a developing love story. Central tensions arise from fear, trust, and the risks of telling the truth, while the novel explores trauma, vulnerability, justice, and the conflict between self-protection and moral responsibility.
book-7762: Spanning the mid-20th century to the late 20th century, this historical novel follows a Palestinian family uprooted from the village of Ein Hod during the 1948 Arab-Israeli war and scattered across refugee camps, Jerusalem, Europe, and the United States. At its center is Amal, whose childhood in Jenin refugee camp is shaped by loss, exile, and the disappearance of her brother, taken into an Israeli family. The narrative traces several generations as war, occupation, migration, and memory shape intimate lives. Through scenes of camp life, family rituals, education, love, and political violence, the book examines dispossession, identity, grief, and the lasting effects of national conflict on ordinary people. It presents the Israeli-Palestinian conflict through domestic experience, emphasizing inheritance, belonging, and the struggle to hold onto home.
book-7763: Contemporary London provides the backdrop for a romantic comedy about Jo Green, a warm but drifting young woman who takes a nanny job with a wealthy, emotionally turbulent family. Inside an elegant house ruled by social pressure, money, and old resentments, she must manage difficult children, a glamorous but self-absorbed mother, and the strained atmosphere surrounding a charismatic husband. As Jo becomes entangled in the household’s secrets and shifting loyalties, the novel follows her growing attachment to the family and the complications of love across class and emotional boundaries. Domestic labor, privilege, loneliness, and the search for adult identity shape the story, while sharp dialogue and comic scenes of childcare, parties, and misunderstanding keep the tone light even as the household’s fractures become harder to ignore.
book-7764: Set in contemporary Chicago, this romance follows Rachel Livingston, an ambitious journalist assigned to profile Malcolm Saint, a magnetic young entrepreneur whose nightlife reputation makes him a public obsession. Rachel plans to use access to Saint to secure a career-making article, but the assignment becomes complicated as professional scrutiny turns into intense mutual attraction. Their relationship develops under the pressure of secrecy, class privilege, media attention, and Rachel’s concealed purpose. The novel centers on flirtation, sexual tension, and the ethical conflict between emotional intimacy and journalistic ambition. Humor and sharp banter shape scenes in restaurants, offices, parties, and penthouse apartments, while the story examines trust, power, desire, and the cost of pursuing success when love and deception become entangled.
book-7765: Los Angeles lies in ruins after a plague turns the dead into ravenous ex-humans, and a small band of costumed heroes helps defend one of the last secure refuges. Behind the walls of a fortified movie studio called the Mount, soldiers, mechanics, and civilians struggle to keep generators running, ration supplies, and repel constant attacks from the undead. The narrative follows masked figures with super strength, flight, stealth, and other powers as they balance rescue missions, patrols, and the ugly compromises of survival. Flashbacks to the first days of the outbreak reveal how quickly ordinary city life collapses and how secret identities become liabilities. Combining superhero adventure with zombie horror, the novel explores leadership, sacrifice, fear, and the fragility of social order under siege.
book-7766: Centuries after a failed attempt to halt the Inhibitors, a small band of humans crosses interstellar space toward Ararat, a planet hidden behind a lethal radiation veil and ruled by a quasi-religious regime. Among them are veterans of earlier wars, a wounded woman linked to strange technology, and the child they believe may matter to humanity’s survival. Their journey unfolds aboard damaged starships and through ruined colonies where advanced machines, political schisms, and old betrayals shape every choice. The novel combines space opera, hard-science speculation, and gothic atmosphere, exploring relativistic travel, artificial intelligence, memory, faith, and the burden of past violence. Central tensions arise from the search for refuge and meaning in a universe where extinct civilizations and predatory machines leave little room for human certainty.
book-7767: A group of children discover an enormous tree in an enchanted wood, where each branch hides unusual rooms and peculiar inhabitants, including Moon-Face, Silky the fairy, and Saucepan Man. At the top of the Faraway Tree, a ladder leads to a different land whenever the clouds part: places such as the Land of Birthdays, the Land of Take-What-You-Want, or more dangerous realms where rules shift without warning. The stories follow the children as they climb, explore, get trapped, and race home before a land moves on. Set between an ordinary English household and a changing magical world, the collection centres on curiosity, friendship, mischief, and the tension between adventure and safety in classic children's fantasy episodes.
book-7768: A mother’s memoir recounts the life and death of Cassie Bernall, a teenager killed in the 1999 Columbine High School shooting in Littleton, Colorado. Misty Bernall traces Cassie’s childhood, her rebellion and depression, her involvement with drugs and occult interests, and her later commitment to evangelical Christianity. The narrative follows family conflict, youth-group culture, and the search for moral direction in suburban America, then turns to the aftermath of the massacre and the public attention surrounding Cassie’s final moments. Blending personal testimony with Christian reflection, the book examines conversion, parental fear, adolescent identity, grief, martyrdom, and the effort to find religious meaning after sudden violence.
book-7769: A shy nature columnist at a London newspaper is mistaken for a celebrated foreign correspondent and dispatched to the East African state of Ishmaelia, where a civil war is expected to produce headlines. In hotel bars, government offices, and telegraph rooms, he meets rival reporters, opportunistic officials, and editors who value sensation over fact. The novel follows the machinery of the press as rumor hardens into news and private incompetence becomes public authority. Set between Fleet Street and a fictional colony on the brink of upheaval, it treats journalism, empire, and class as systems built on vanity, error, and performance. Its comedy comes from miscommunication, bureaucratic absurdity, and the gap between lived events and the stories newspapers decide to print.
book-777: An overweight, underpaid journalist at a North London newspaper moves through office gossip, bad dates, and persistent self-consciousness while dreaming of romance and reinvention. Jemima Jones writes a lonely-hearts column, secretly longs for a handsome colleague, and begins an intense email relationship with a man in California who seems to offer the glamour and devotion missing from her daily life. As she undertakes a dramatic transformation before flying to Los Angeles, the novel follows the gap between fantasy and reality in both love and body image. Set between London workplaces, cramped flats, and sunny American promise, the story treats weight, desire, friendship, humiliation, and self-worth with comic scenes and a sharp focus on how women are judged by appearance.
book-7770: After a divorce in midlife, a longtime writer leaves her familiar routines and begins an open-ended journey through Mexico, Central America, Asia, and the South Pacific, often living with local families rather than passing through as a tourist. The narrative follows practical encounters with buses, markets, village kitchens, language barriers, and improvised homes, while tracing a deeper experiment in freedom, solitude, and belonging. Instead of a fixed itinerary, the book presents travel as a way of rethinking identity, work, family, and home. Cultural exchange, hospitality, fear, curiosity, and the discipline of adapting to unfamiliar customs shape the memoir’s central argument: that a life organized around movement can become a serious form of self-discovery and connection to people across borders.
book-7771: A short-story collection set in suburbs, college towns, hospitals, and strained family homes follows women and men through divorce, illness, parenthood, grief, and uneasy romance. Across these pieces, Lorrie Moore focuses on ordinary American lives destabilized by betrayal, cancer, war, aging, and the failures of language itself. Teachers, sisters, spouses, and children move through kitchens, motel rooms, city streets, and sickrooms where jokes coexist with panic and tenderness. The central tensions are less plot-driven than emotional: how to care for other people without false sentiment, how to keep speaking when words feel inadequate, and how to endure loneliness inside marriage, family, and friendship. Themes of mortality, desire, domestic life, and dark comedy shape a portrait of late twentieth-century American intimacy.
book-7772: A wealthy New York businessman who built his reputation on casual sex and confidence agrees to fake an engagement for the sake of a major business deal, only to find himself entangled with a woman who already knows his worst habits. Set in boardrooms, penthouses, bars, and family gatherings, the story follows a playboy narrator as a publicity-driven arrangement begins to unsettle the rules he lives by. The central conflict grows from the gap between performance and sincerity: he can sell an image of commitment, but real intimacy threatens his carefully managed independence. Blending explicit romantic tension with comic banter, the novel centers on fake dating, friendship, desire, and the possibility that vulnerability may matter more than charm, money, or sexual bravado.
book-7773: On the island of Fennbirn, every generation produces royal triplets, but only one sister can claim the crown. Mirabella, Arsinoe, and Katharine are raised apart by rival factions that cultivate their gifts: elemental control, naturalist magic, and poison immunity. When they come of age, they are brought together for a succession ritual that requires the queens to hunt one another until a single survivor remains. Court alliances, foster families, and religious politics shape the contest, while affection and attraction complicate loyalties that should be simple. Set in a closed island kingdom governed by ritual and fear, the novel centers on dynastic violence, sisterhood, prophecy, and the pressure to perform power in public while facing private doubt.
book-7774: A chance romance in Paris becomes the framework for a memoir about marriage, migration, and learning a new culture through food. An American woman leaves New York for France after falling in love with a Frenchman, then navigates the daily negotiations of language, family expectations, work, and identity that accompany building a life abroad. Parisian apartments, neighborhood markets, country kitchens, and shared meals ground the narrative in specific places and rituals. Alongside the love story, recipes for tarts, stews, cakes, and other French dishes trace her growing confidence in the kitchen and her changing understanding of home. Themes of appetite, belonging, cross-cultural misunderstanding, and the intimate politics of domestic life run through this culinary travel memoir.
book-7775: As the American Civil War erupts, the Hazard family of Pennsylvania and the Main family of South Carolina find friendship strained by secession, military service, and divided loyalties. Set in plantations, foundries, battlefields, hospitals, and political salons, the novel follows spouses, siblings, and children as they confront enlistment, espionage, profiteering, slavery, and the collapse of the old social order. Personal attachments and marriages cross sectional lines, turning national conflict into domestic crisis. Against campaigns from Fort Sumter through the major theaters of war, the narrative examines how industrial wealth, plantation power, honor, ambition, and reform shape individual choices. Themes include family endurance, class privilege, race, patriotism, and the cost of violence when private love and public ideology can no longer be kept apart.
book-7776: Amid the hidden realms of Avalon and the human world, a teenage girl who has learned she is a fall fairy faces the approaching war that has shadowed the series. Laurel must balance ordinary life, dangerous magic, and divided loyalties as trolls threaten the gates to Avalon and force long-standing tensions into open conflict. Her bond with the dependable human boy who knows her secret and her powerful connection to a fairy guardian continue to shape her choices, turning romance into a question of duty, trust, and identity. Set in forests, schools, and enchanted strongholds, the novel centers on strategy, sacrifice, and belonging as Laurel and her allies prepare for a final confrontation over home, love, and the future of both worlds.
book-7777: Set largely inside an Internal Revenue Service Regional Examination Center in Peoria, Illinois, during the mid-1980s, this posthumously assembled novel follows accountants, trainees, and supervisors whose working lives revolve around tax returns, audits, forms, and fluorescent office routine. Its loose, fragmented structure presents multiple voices, including a version of David Foster Wallace, as it studies how bureaucratic labor shapes consciousness. The central tension lies less in plot than in the effort to endure monotony, data, and administrative pressure while remaining morally alert and psychologically intact. Scenes of classrooms, desks, government corridors, and Midwestern weather frame questions about boredom, attention, civic duty, loneliness, and the hidden drama of white-collar work. Humor and documentary detail coexist with meditations on paperwork, authority, and the possibility of meaning inside institutions.
book-7778: Set in the courts, villages, and family networks of ancient China, this classical collection gathers sayings, brief dialogues, and remembered encounters associated with Confucius and his followers. It presents a practical moral philosophy centered on self-cultivation, ritual conduct, humane government, filial duty, friendship, and the disciplined use of language. Rather than building a single systematic argument, the text moves through compact episodes on learning, music, ceremony, leadership, and the character of the exemplary person. Its central concern is how order can be restored in a time of political fragmentation: through virtue rather than coercion, and through habits of respect rather than force. Themes include ethics, education, authority, social harmony, memory, and the relationship between personal integrity and public responsibility.
book-7779: A memoir of the 1960s and 1970s Los Angeles rock scene follows Pamela Des Barres from suburban adolescence into the clubs, houses, and backstage rooms surrounding famous bands. She recounts encounters and relationships with musicians linked to the Byrds, Led Zeppelin, the Rolling Stones, Frank Zappa, and others, tracing how fandom, desire, style, and self-invention shape her identity. The narrative places groupie culture within Sunset Strip nightlife, touring circuits, and the wider sexual revolution, showing both glamour and vulnerability. Alongside portraits of performers and hangers-on, it examines women’s agency, obsession, performance, and the blurred line between participant and observer in celebrity culture. The result is a firsthand chronicle of rock history told through intimacy, memory, and scene-making.
book-778: Set in late medieval Paris beneath the towers of Notre-Dame Cathedral, this historical novel follows several lives drawn together by desire, pity, power, and public spectacle. Quasimodo, the deaf and physically deformed bell ringer, serves the archdeacon Claude Frollo, whose learning and religious authority give way to obsession with the Romani dancer Esmeralda. Around them move the vain captain Phoebus, the poet Gringoire, and the crowded streets, courts, and churches of fifteenth-century France. The central conflict turns on unequal power, misdirected love, and the violence of a city that turns punishment into entertainment. Hugo combines melodrama, gothic horror, and social observation to examine beauty and ugliness, fate and injustice, the treatment of outsiders, and the looming decline of medieval Paris before modern change.
book-7780: Set in contemporary Seattle, this urban fantasy follows Georgina Kincaid, a succubus who works in a bookstore while navigating the demands of immortals, vampires, and demons. Her uneasy balance between supernatural duty and ordinary city life grows more complicated after her relationship with novelist Seth Mortensen fractures, leaving her caught between desire, guilt, and loneliness. As infernal politics intrude and a dangerous mystery draws her deeper into the hidden world around her, Georgina must weigh loyalty to friends against the rules imposed by heaven and hell. The novel combines paranormal romance and horror elements with nightclub scenes, demon bargains, and occult intrigue, focusing on identity, temptation, forbidden love, and the cost of intimacy for a creature whose touch can consume human souls.
book-7781: After the fall of the prison, a scattered band of survivors moves through a ruined American landscape where every road, farmhouse, and abandoned town carries the threat of the walking dead. Rick Grimes struggles to keep leadership and purpose while grief, exhaustion, and fear reshape the group’s fragile loyalties. As they search for shelter and a reason to keep going, old certainties break down and questions of trust become as dangerous as the dead themselves. Charlie Adlard and Cliff Rathburn’s black-and-white artwork emphasizes empty highways, cramped rooms, and sudden violence, turning survival into a study of trauma and endurance. This volume centers on displacement, parental responsibility, group cohesion, and the uneasy possibility that human relationships, not fortifications, determine who remains alive.
book-7782: After a painful breakup, Iris Taylor leaves her old life behind and takes a job at a tattoo shop run by the intimidating Dex Locke. The shop’s daily rhythm—appointments, artists, regular clients, and the rough edges of a biker-adjacent crowd—forces her into close contact with a boss who is controlling, private, and unexpectedly protective. As attraction grows between them, Iris tries to hold on to her independence while Dex’s secrets and temper keep him at a distance. A threatening figure from Iris’s past and the danger surrounding Dex’s world add a thread of suspense to the romance. Set in a contemporary urban scene of tattoo parlors, motorcycles, and found-family friendships, the novel centers on trust, jealousy, personal boundaries, and emotional recovery.
book-7783: Set in Sicily during the Risorgimento of the 1860s, the novel follows Prince Fabrizio Salina, an aging aristocrat watching Garibaldi’s campaign and Italian unification overturn the Bourbon world that has sustained his family. From Palermo salons to a country estate and the town of Donnafugata, it traces shifting alliances between old nobility and the rising bourgeoisie, especially through the ambitions of Fabrizio’s nephew Tancredi and the marriage politics that bind wealth to title. The central conflict lies between historical change and private resignation: whether dignity, power, and tradition can survive when social forms remain but authority drains away. Through astronomy, religion, courtship, and ritual, the narrative examines decay, class transformation, mortality, and the seductive illusion that everything can stay the same by changing.
book-7784: Set in late nineteenth-century Canada, this graphic novel traces the secret beginnings of the mutant later known as Wolverine. A sickly boy named James Howlett grows up on a wealthy estate under rigid class boundaries, family tensions, and buried resentments. After a violent upheaval shatters his sheltered life, he is driven into the wilderness and toward a brutal mining camp, where survival, rage, and instinct begin to define him. As his strange abilities emerge, including healing and bone claws, the story explores how trauma, repression, and social cruelty shape identity. The narrative combines frontier landscapes, aristocratic households, and industrial labor with themes of memory, animal ferocity, inheritance, and the painful making of a solitary antihero in the Marvel universe.
book-7785: On the Atlantic coast of Virginia, a teenage girl grows up in a hardworking but troubled family, sustained by loyalty to her brother and by dreams that reach beyond the confines of Cutler’s Cove. Her world changes when long-buried secrets about her birth and parentage begin to surface, exposing lies, resentments, and a family history marked by obsession and control. As she is drawn into the orbit of wealthy relatives and a grand hotel dynasty, she faces class divisions, possessive adults, and romantic attachments shadowed by taboo and manipulation. The novel blends domestic melodrama, gothic horror, and young adult romance, focusing on identity, legitimacy, abuse within families, and the struggle to preserve innocence and self-respect in a setting where kinship is inseparable from power.
book-7786: Four urban fantasy novellas move through contemporary streets, bars, and hidden supernatural territories where desire collides with danger. Patricia Briggs introduces Anna Latham, an abused Chicago werewolf whose meeting with enforcer Charles Cornick exposes the brutal hierarchy of a pack and the possibility of protection, loyalty, and mate-bonding. Eileen Wilks, Karen Chance, and Sunny add stories of shapeshifters, witches, vampires, and other predators navigating uneasy truces, erotic attraction, and violent threats. Across the collection, women confront dominant packs, ancient power struggles, and bodies altered by magic or curse. The central tensions come from trust, consent, and survival within secret societies that exist beside ordinary modern life, combining paranormal romance with horror-inflected conflict and pack politics.
book-7787: Minneapolis detective Lucas Davenport pursues a brutal serial killer whose crimes seem to follow no stable pattern except escalating violence and a talent for disappearing. The investigation moves through winter streets, suburban houses, police interview rooms, and media glare as Davenport studies crime scenes, survivor accounts, and fragmentary psychological clues. The central conflict lies in a hunt for an offender who understands police procedure, manipulates identity, and turns each murder into a challenge to the investigators trying to stop her. As leads collapse and pressure mounts, the novel examines obsession, trauma, and the uneasy overlap between intuition and method in homicide work. Combining procedural detail with suspense, it centers on the mental duel between a seasoned cop and a predator who remains terrifyingly hard to read.
book-7788: In the land of Achar, rival noble houses, church politics, and an old war shape a fantasy epic with traces of prophecy and lost history. Axis, an outcast raised as a battle commander, learns that his birth ties him to the winged Icarii and to a struggle far larger than border skirmishes. As the ice-bound enemy Gorgrael stirs in the north, kingdoms and forests face invasion by supernatural armies, while loyalties split between brothers, lovers, and competing visions of power. The narrative moves between fortresses, sacred sites, and wilderness roads, combining military conflict, romance, and mythic revelation. Central concerns include legitimacy, heritage, religious authority, and the possibility of redemption in a world divided between human ambition and ancient, nonhuman forces.
book-7789: Set in Martinique and revolutionary France, this historical novel follows Rose Tascher, later known as Josephine Bonaparte, as she recounts her rise from a Creole plantation childhood to the dangerous salons and prisons of Paris. Married young to Alexandre de Beauharnais, she faces a brittle union, financial strain, class upheaval, and the violence of the French Revolution, including the ever-present threat of denunciation and execution. As political factions shift and family loyalties fracture, her private ambitions and emotional losses unfold alongside national collapse. The narrative centers on survival, reinvention, motherhood, social power, and the compromises required of a woman navigating marriage, desire, and status in a world remade by terror and opportunity.
book-779: Set in India during the mid-1970s Emergency, this historical novel follows four people drawn together in a crowded Mumbai apartment: a widowed seamstress seeking independence, two village tailors escaping caste violence, and a student from the mountains trying to make a life in the city. As political repression, forced sterilization, slum demolitions, and corruption spread through daily life, their fragile household becomes a refuge shaped by work, hunger, friendship, and mutual obligation. The narrative moves between village and city, tracing how poverty, social hierarchy, and state power press on ordinary bodies and choices. Themes of resilience, dignity, cruelty, and interdependence run through a portrait of urban survival in a society marked by inequality and abrupt historical change.
book-7790: A string of brutal killings drives this Arabic horror mystery through a contemporary Egyptian city marked by crowded streets, police files, and private fear. The narrative follows an investigation into a figure known as “the butcher,” while witnesses, suspects, and pursuers confront scenes of bloodshed that suggest both criminal violence and something harder to explain. As clues accumulate, the novel moves between interrogation, rumor, and psychological unease, building a portrait of a community unsettled by panic and secrecy. Mystery mechanics and literary-fiction attention to mood work together to explore terror, guilt, and the way violence alters memory and trust. The central conflict turns on identifying the killer and determining whether the threat comes from a human predator, a disturbed mind, or a darker force haunting the city.
book-7791: A suburban Philadelphia pediatrician is pulled back into the life she thought she had left behind when her former stepdaughter appears at her door after a violent death in Jill’s ex-husband’s household. As police focus on the teenage girl, Jill begins asking questions about the family she once knew: an ex-husband who betrayed her, a glamorous second wife, and a home filled with money, resentment, and concealed loyalties. The investigation moves through Main Line neighborhoods, courtrooms, and private memories as Jill weighs her stable new relationship against her need to protect a child she still loves. The novel combines domestic suspense, murder investigation, and family drama, focusing on maternal attachment, divorce, class privilege, deception, and the danger of returning to an unresolved past.
book-7792: Hansel and Gretel leave the safety of their father’s kingdom and wander through a series of connected Grimm fairy tales filled with severed heads, witches, dragons, demons, and dangerous bargains. Set in a bleak medieval landscape of forests, villages, and castles, the story follows the siblings as they try to survive one brutal trial after another while searching for a place where they belong. An intrusive narrator warns readers about the gore even as the plot moves deeper into old folklore. Beneath the violence, the novel examines family loyalty, abandonment, sin, forgiveness, and the cost of growing up in a world where adults fail children. The book reworks traditional tales into a dark fantasy for middle-grade and young adult readers, mixing horror, humor, and moral fable.
book-7793: In the city of Imardin, years after peace with Sachaka, Sonea’s son Lorkin studies black magic under the Magicians’ Guild and becomes an envoy to the Allied Lands embassy. When he is abducted by mysterious women from Sachaka, he is drawn into a hidden society whose strict laws, unusual magic, and political secrets challenge everything the Guild teaches. Back in Kyralia, his disappearance alarms the Guild and forces Sonea to confront old fears about Sachakan power. As diplomats, magicians, and rulers maneuver across borders, the novel follows tensions between duty and independence, the ethics of forbidden knowledge, and the uneasy aftermath of war. Court intrigue, magical training, and cross-cultural suspicion drive this opening volume of an epic fantasy trilogy.
book-7794: An unnamed Jewish-American man looks back over his life as illness and repeated surgeries narrow his world to hospitals, cemeteries, and solitary apartments on the New Jersey shore. From his boyhood in his father’s jewelry store in Elizabeth to marriages, divorces, children, work in advertising, and retirement, the novel traces a body’s steady decline alongside memories of desire, betrayal, and family attachment. The central conflict lies between his vivid appetite for sex, work, and self-invention and the inescapable fact of aging and death. Encounters with his brother, his lovers, his estranged sons, and the graves of his parents sharpen questions of guilt, loneliness, inheritance, and the ordinary failures that shape a life.
book-7795: Set in Jakarta’s streets, clubs, and tattoo parlors, this literary speculative novel follows Bodhi, a drifter with dreadlocks whose life unfolds through broken family ties, urban subcultures, and restless travel. As he moves among punks, artists, drug scenes, and spiritual seekers, he searches for the source of his own identity and the hidden pattern linking people, memory, and consciousness. The narrative blends concrete city detail with metaphysical questions, using Bodhi’s encounters and inner turbulence to explore alienation, freedom, fate, and transformation. Rather than centering on a conventional quest or romance, it traces a psychological and philosophical journey through modern Indonesia, where bodily experience, friendship, and mysticism gradually suggest that the self is rooted in something larger and more elusive than personal history.
book-7796: Six Latina professionals and longtime friends navigate work, love, family, and identity as they move through contemporary urban life in Boston and New York. The novel follows a tight social circle that includes a television reporter, a lawyer, a social worker, a magazine editor, and other women whose polished public lives hide infidelity, ambition, loneliness, class tension, and old resentments. Their weekly gatherings offer gossip, loyalty, and a place to measure the distance between cultural expectations and personal desire. As careers shift and relationships strain, the group confronts questions of race, sexuality, marriage, motherhood, and friendship within Latino communities and the broader American professional world. Blending romantic comedy with ensemble drama, the story examines intimacy, self-invention, and the fragile bonds that hold friends together.
book-7797: In the small town of Fell’s Church, a new wave of violence follows the apparent defeat of earlier supernatural threats, drawing Elena Gilbert, Stefan Salvatore, Damon Salvatore, and their friends back into conflict with a powerful hidden enemy. The novel combines high school routines, cemetery rituals, haunted woods, and secret gatherings as ordinary teenage life collides with vampire lore and psychic terror. Elena stands at the center of competing loyalties between the two vampire brothers while the group tries to identify the force manipulating attacks, fear, and suspicion across town. The story focuses on possession, resurrection, jealousy, sacrifice, and the pull between human affection and predatory hunger. Gothic horror, romance, and adolescent rivalry shape a plot about love tested by death and by evil that refuses to stay buried.
book-7798: A disillusioned Manhattan psychiatrist begins using dice to make everyday choices, then larger moral and sexual decisions, turning chance into a private philosophy and a social experiment. Set in New York in the early 1970s, the novel follows his attempt to escape routine, professional hypocrisy, and the fixed roles of husband, doctor, and citizen by surrendering control to random outcomes. As the method spreads from bedroom games and therapy sessions into friendships, work, and public behavior, the story treats liberation and self-destruction as inseparable possibilities. Satirical, provocative, and darkly comic, it examines identity as performance, the appeal of chaos, the limits of free will, and the uneasy border between psychological insight, manipulation, and madness.
book-7799: In Victorian England, young aristocrat Ciel Phantomhive serves Queen Victoria as a covert investigator, relying on Sebastian Michaelis, the flawless butler bound to him by a dark contract. This volume continues their blend of manor-house comedy and gothic mystery as the pair leave the safety of the Phantomhive estate to pursue a series of brutal murders in London. The investigation draws them into fogbound streets, upper-class secrets, and the hidden violence beneath polite society. Alongside elegant household routines and sharp servant banter, the story develops its central tension: a child master bent on revenge and the inhuman servant who protects him while waiting for payment. Themes of power, class, corruption, and the performance of civility shape this supernatural historical fantasy.
book-78: A recent Brown graduate lands a coveted assistant job at Runway, a powerful New York fashion magazine, expecting a stepping-stone into publishing. Instead, Andrea Sachs enters the orbit of Miranda Priestly, the magazine’s exacting editor, whose impossible demands govern every hour of the day. Amid designer clothes, photo shoots, sample closets, and Manhattan status rituals, Andrea struggles to meet relentless expectations while her friendships, romance, and sense of self begin to fray. The novel follows office politics and entry-level labor inside the glamour industry, using sharp humor to contrast luxury branding with exhaustion and humiliation. Themes of ambition, class performance, consumer culture, and the cost of professional success drive a story about how far a young woman will bend to survive a prestigious job.
book-780: A six-year-old boy with a spike of blond hair and a ferocious imagination moves through suburban days with his stuffed tiger, who appears as a living companion whenever adults are not looking. Short comic strips follow Calvin at home, in school, on sledding hills, and outdoors as he argues with parents, resists homework, torments babysitters, and invents alter egos, cardboard-box machines, and cosmic adventures. Hobbes answers with dry wit and pounces, but also serves as confidant, co-conspirator, and philosophical foil. Beneath the jokes about childhood mischief, the collection explores boredom, friendship, fantasy, consumer culture, education, family rules, and the unruly logic of a child testing the world’s limits. Watterson’s expressive drawings balance slapstick action with quiet moments of wonder in woods, snow, and backyards.
book-7800: Set in contemporary Los Angeles, this literary thriller follows Clay, now a successful screenwriter, as he moves through parties, film sets, hotels, and expensive houses haunted by his old circle from youth. A reunion with former friends and lovers draws him back into a world of cocaine, sexual bargaining, jealousy, and private violence. As a young actress becomes entangled with him, rumors, surveillance, and anonymous threats turn casual cruelty into sustained menace. The novel presents Hollywood as a landscape of wealth, performance, and emotional vacancy, where memories are unreliable and intimacy is inseparable from exploitation. Themes of moral numbness, power, voyeurism, and self-invention shape a narrative that blends social satire with psychological horror and noir suspense.
book-7801: Set in contemporary Philadelphia among wealthy, image-conscious families, this romance follows Lily Calloway and Loren Hale, childhood friends who maintain a fake relationship to conceal private compulsions. Lily struggles with sex addiction, while Lo battles alcoholism, and their arrangement gives each of them cover from relatives, gossip, and scrutiny. As their carefully managed facade begins to crack, friendship shifts into desire, and both must decide whether intimacy can survive dishonesty, relapse, and fear of exposure. The novel centers on addiction, dependency, secrecy, recovery, and the pressure of public appearances, while also tracing a turbulent love story between two people who understand each other’s damage better than anyone else. It combines family conflict, emotional vulnerability, and explicit romantic tension with themes of shame and self-acceptance.
book-7802: Set in Paris after a year of separation, this young adult romance returns to Allyson and Willem as they meet again following the whirlwind connection that first linked them on a European trip. The story centers on a single night in which both characters must decide whether the brief encounter that changed their lives can survive real conversation, past hurt, and the uncertainties of the future. Drawing on the emotional aftermath of travel, missed connections, and personal reinvention, the novella focuses on intimacy rather than spectacle, using city streets, hotel rooms, and late-night dialogue to explore memory, identity, forgiveness, and the difference between fantasy and commitment. It serves as a coda to their transatlantic love story while remaining grounded in the choices facing two young adults.
book-7803: A practical manual introduces the Kindle e-reader and explains how users navigate its hardware, software, and wireless bookstore features. Set in the everyday environment of personal reading and digital media management, it covers device setup, home screen menus, page turning, bookmarks, highlights, notes, dictionary lookup, and downloading books, newspapers, and periodicals. It also addresses battery charging, wireless connectivity, account registration, content organization, and common troubleshooting tasks. The central purpose is functional rather than narrative: helping readers move from printed habits to electronic reading with clear instructions for purchasing, storing, and accessing text on a portable screen. Themes include usability, digital ownership, annotation, accessibility, and the shift from physical bookshelves to cloud-based libraries and handheld reading devices.
book-7804: A near-future dictatorship hunts teenagers accused of witchcraft while siblings Whit and Wisty Allgood become symbols of rebellion. In this third young adult fantasy novel, the pair move through a shattered cityscape of prisons, secret safe houses, and battle zones as the New Order tightens its control and the resistance fractures under pressure. Wisty’s unstable magical fire grows more dangerous, Whit faces the burdens of leadership and prophecy, and both are pulled between family loyalty, romance, and the demands of a widening war. Mixing supernatural powers with dystopian politics, the story centers on persecution, state violence, teenage resistance, and the cost of using extraordinary power in a world determined to erase freedom, imagination, and dissent.
book-7805: After a foreign army invades Australia, a small group of rural teenagers remain hidden in the bush and continue a guerrilla campaign against the occupiers. Recovering from earlier losses, Ellie and her friends return to the devastated town of Wirrawee to gather supplies, contact scattered allies, and strike at military targets while their families are held in an internment camp. The immediate conflict pits their local knowledge and improvisation against patrols, checkpoints, and the strain of constant danger. Set in farmland, mountain hideouts, and a damaged country town, the novel focuses on sabotage, survival, and the moral cost of violence. Themes include loyalty, fear, grief, responsibility, and the abrupt end of ordinary adolescence under wartime occupation.
book-7806: Set in Hiroshima in the years after the atomic bombing of Japan, this children’s historical novel follows Sadako Sasaki, an energetic girl whose life changes when she becomes ill from radiation sickness. As she is taken from school and friends into the hospital, she learns the Japanese legend that folding one thousand paper cranes can bring healing or a wish granted. The story centers on her determined effort to keep folding cranes while her family and classmates struggle with fear, hope, and grief. Through spare scenes of hospital rooms, schoolyards, and postwar city life, the narrative explores the human cost of nuclear war, the endurance of children, and the power of peace, memory, and small handmade acts of courage in the face of suffering.
book-7807: In contemporary Japan, the cat-and-mouse struggle between student genius Light Yagami and detective L intensifies as a second Death Note user appears. Misa Amane, a famous model and devoted admirer of Kira, enters the investigation carrying her own notebook and the Shinigami Eyes, which reveal a person’s true name and lifespan. Her reckless killings and open loyalty complicate Light’s careful strategy, while L narrows his suspicions and pushes surveillance, confinement, and psychological pressure to force a confession. The volume centers on manipulation, obsession, and the exchange of power for human life, using supernatural rules, police procedure, and media spectacle to explore justice, identity, and the cost of devotion. Obata’s artwork emphasizes tense interrogations, urban interiors, and the eerie presence of the death gods.
book-7808: Confined to a hospital bed with a broken leg, Scotland Yard inspector Alan Grant turns from current cases to a centuries-old mystery after seeing a portrait of Richard III. Using documents, chronicles, genealogies, and the help of a young researcher, he reopens the question of whether Richard murdered the Princes in the Tower. The novel moves between modern detective method and fifteenth-century English politics, treating archives, rumor, and official histories as evidence to be tested. Set largely in a London hospital room but reaching into the Wars of the Roses, it examines how national myths are built, how propaganda shapes reputation, and how a criminal investigator’s habits can unsettle accepted versions of the past.
book-7809: Israeli intelligence operative and art restorer Gabriel Allon is drawn into a hunt for a Palestinian master terrorist after a bombing in Rome kills the son of the Israeli ambassador. Moving from Italy and Vienna to the Middle East and the corridors of European espionage, he follows a trail shaped by old covert operations, family losses, and the unresolved violence of the Arab-Israeli conflict. The novel combines spy tradecraft, surveillance, interrogations, and political maneuvering with Allon’s private grief and divided loyalties. Central tensions arise from retaliation, moral compromise, and the way past acts of war echo into the present. Themes include terrorism, memory, revenge, national identity, and the personal cost of intelligence work.
book-781: In a future society that surgically enforces beauty and social conformity, Tally Youngblood has been transformed again, this time into a “Special,” an elite enforcer engineered for speed, strength, and ruthless clarity. Sent to hunt rebels and preserve the city’s fragile order, she joins a violent team that sees ordinary people as weak and the resistance as a threat to civilization. As missions pull her between the wild landscape outside the cities and the controlled world she once tried to escape, buried loyalties and altered memories begin to clash with her chemically sharpened mind. The novel centers on identity under biological manipulation, the politics of perfection, and the struggle to recognize freedom, friendship, and conscience when the body and brain have been redesigned to serve power.
book-7810: Set in contemporary France and shadowed by an eighteenth-century libertine episode, the novel follows a writer-narrator during a night at a château hotel where scholars, television personalities, and lovers move through a series of comic and unsettling encounters. A parallel seduction from an earlier era runs beside the modern plot, linking courtship, memory, and bodily pleasure across centuries. The central argument contrasts slowness with speed: leisurely desire, reflection, and recollection give way to publicity, performance, and the frantic pursuit of visibility. Kundera uses short scenes, essayistic digressions, and self-conscious narration to examine eroticism, vanity, media culture, and the instability of identity. Themes include time, forgetting, authenticity, and the relation between desire and spectacle.
book-7811: War and political upheaval engulf the nation of Adro as field marshal Tamas fights to hold the capital against invading armies, royalist plots, and the fallout of revolution. Across battlefields, city streets, and occupied territory, powder mages, soldiers, spies, and sorcerers confront a widening crisis in which gunpowder, muskets, and industrial warfare collide with ancient gods and destructive magic. The novel follows divided loyalties, military strategy, and contested legitimacy as old aristocratic power gives way to uncertain republican rule. Its setting blends flintlock-era armies, bureaucratic intrigue, and supernatural forces, with conflicts shaped by coups, sieges, and secret alliances. Major themes include the costs of revolution, the burden of command, national identity, and the struggle to build a government while enemies press from within and without.
book-7812: A sequence of erotic short stories moves through apartments, cafés, brothels, beaches, and hotel rooms in Paris and other cosmopolitan settings, tracing sexual encounters rather than a single plot. Written in lush, literary prose, the collection follows women and men as they pursue desire, performance, voyeurism, infidelity, same-sex attraction, fetish, and fantasy. The central tension lies between private longing and the roles imposed by marriage, money, class, and gender, as characters test how far intimacy can become power, escape, or self-invention. Alongside explicit scenes, the stories examine the psychology of seduction, the staging of erotic identity, and the overlap between tenderness and manipulation. Posthumously published, the volume presents Anaïs Nin’s long-suppressed fiction of sensuality, secrecy, and imagination.
book-7813: Amid a zombie-ravaged American landscape, Rick Grimes leads a shrinking band of survivors along empty roads in search of shelter, food, and some workable code for living. This volume follows the group after devastating losses, when exhaustion, grief, and constant exposure leave them vulnerable not only to roaming walkers but also to other people with predatory intentions. As they take refuge in a rural church and weigh whom they can trust, the central conflict turns on how far they are willing to go to defend themselves and one another. The graphic narrative explores survival ethics, leadership under pressure, trauma, revenge, and the erosion of ordinary morality when hunger, fear, and desperation govern every decision.
book-7814: Near-future San Diego becomes a test bed for ubiquitous computing, augmented reality, and networked surveillance as recovered poet Robert Gu returns from Alzheimer’s-like decline to a world he no longer understands. Forced back into school alongside teenagers, he struggles with family tensions, professional pride, and the loss of status that comes with relearning ordinary life. Around him, libraries, classrooms, and city streets are overlaid with digital identities and invisible systems of control. A quieter mystery grows into a political and technological threat involving information warfare, mass persuasion, and the vulnerability of connected societies. The novel examines aging, memory, education, intelligence, and the social consequences of wearable computers, while grounding its speculation in domestic conflict and the changing institutions of reading and knowledge.
book-7815: A contemporary romance set around a major college football program, the story follows a guarded student and the charismatic athlete she knows too well for easy fantasy. Their banter, shared history, and constant proximity make them best friends in public, even as private attraction grows harder to ignore. The central conflict turns on the “friend zone” itself: crossing that line could lead to intimacy, but it could also destroy the one relationship each relies on. Campus parties, training schedules, locker-room scrutiny, and family expectations keep pressure on every choice. Humor and sharp dialogue offset scenes of vulnerability as the novel explores friendship, sexual tension, trust, body image, and the risk of wanting more than either person feels safe admitting.
book-7816: Set in the kingdom of Melengar after Royce Melborn and Hadrian Blackwater have begun working together as Riyria, this fantasy adventure follows the pair into a web of noble secrets, church politics, and street violence. Hired for what appears to be a discreet domestic inquiry, the thief and the swordsman are drawn from manor houses and abbeys into alleys, brothels, and court intrigue as murders and blackmail point to a larger conspiracy. The novel balances investigation, swordplay, and travel through a secondary world shaped by feudal rank, religious authority, and uneasy royal power. Central tensions grow from trust between partners, the gap between rich and poor, and the way private sins become public danger. Themes include loyalty, corruption, justice, and the making of an unlikely friendship.
book-7817: Moscow’s hidden supernatural bureaucracy returns to the front line as the uneasy truce between the Night Watch and the Day Watch begins to strain. Anton Gorodetsky, a Light magician, investigates a chain of incidents involving a teenage prophet, a mysterious book, and long-buried secrets about the Twilight, the shadow realm from which all Others draw power. His inquiry moves from apartment blocks and vampire encounters to training camps and historical revelations, showing how private choices ripple through a rigid system of treaties, surveillance, and magical law. The novel blends urban fantasy, horror, and speculative mystery while examining fate, free will, moral compromise, and the cost of preserving balance between Light and Dark in post-Soviet Moscow.
book-7818: A series of brutal killings in the Yukon pulls werewolf Elena Michaels and Clayton Danvers into a winter investigation far from their usual territory. Traveling through isolated towns, forests, and snowbound settlements, they search for the predator responsible while also facing political tensions within the werewolf Pack and threats from rogue mutts. The novel combines urban fantasy, horror, and romance as Elena balances her role as investigator, mate, and mother-to-be under increasingly dangerous conditions. Suspicion falls on both human and supernatural suspects, and the frozen northern setting heightens the sense of confinement, secrecy, and physical vulnerability. Themes of loyalty, family, survival, and the strain between domestic life and violent supernatural duty shape a story centered on pack bonds and the cost of protecting them.
book-7819: In the hidden society of Caldwell’s Black Dagger Brotherhood world, a new training program for vampire recruits brings together young fighters from very different ranks and loyalties. Paradise, the sheltered daughter of the king’s First Advisor, resists aristocratic expectations and enters the program to claim a life beyond marriage politics and the strict codes of the glymera. There she is drawn to Craeg, a common-born trainee marked by grief, anger, and the pressure to prove himself. Their growing attachment unfolds amid brutal combat lessons, class prejudice, family control, and the constant threat of the Lessening Society, the brotherhood’s human enemies. The novel combines paranormal romance with dark fantasy, focusing on duty, social hierarchy, trauma, desire, and the cost of choosing one’s own future.
book-782: Set in late nineteenth-century New Orleans and the Louisiana Gulf coast, this novel follows Edna Pontellier, a married woman who begins to question the duties of wifehood and motherhood that define her social world. After a summer at Grand Isle stirs new desires, she grows increasingly aware of her emotional, artistic, and sexual longings, even as family expectations and Creole society press her toward obedience. Her shifting attachments to her husband, children, and the men and women around her expose a central conflict between individual freedom and rigid convention. The narrative examines marriage, female identity, sensuality, solitude, and the cost of self-discovery within a culture that grants women little independent space. Its historical setting grounds a sharp study of gender, class, and social restraint.
book-7820: Magic saturates the land of Xanth, where every creature and citizen possesses a singular talent, but danger enters through dreams as much as through forests and castles. The story centers on a night mare, a black horse from the realm of nightmares, whose rides carry sleepers into fear and prophecy. When political unrest and threats to Xanth’s magical boundaries begin to spread, her path intersects with Princess Irene and the court around Castle Roogna. Their journey moves through dreamscapes, demon-haunted regions, and the pun-filled geography of Xanth, balancing comic wordplay with genuine peril. Beneath the jokes and quest structure, the novel examines duty, identity, loyalty, and the uneasy border between illusion and waking reality.
book-7821: Years after her older sister is murdered on the night of a family wedding, Bellamy Lyston Price turns the unsolved crime into a bestselling novel that changes names but preserves the central mystery. Publication brings the old case back into public view and draws Bellamy into a new danger when anonymous messages suggest that the killer is still watching. Returning to her wealthy Southern family and to the people who were present that night, she confronts conflicting memories, protective silences, and long-buried resentments. A wary alliance with a former police detective adds romantic tension as the investigation circles through alibis, class privilege, and family loyalty. The novel combines domestic suspense, murder investigation, and romance while examining trauma, secrecy, and the stories people tell to survive.
book-7822: On a storm-beaten island off the coast of Maine, a buried pirate fortune draws together a salvage crew, a treasure hunter, and a team of experts determined to open a lethal pit known as the Water Pit. The excavation revives a centuries-old legend tied to Captain Kidd and a long history of failed attempts, disappearances, and violent deaths. As tides, unstable tunnels, and hidden mechanisms turn the dig into a deadly puzzle, old family obsessions and rival interests sharpen the danger above ground as well. Set among fog, granite cliffs, and the ruins of an isolated estate, the novel combines maritime history, engineering, and suspense. Its central conflict pits greed, inheritance, and scientific method against superstition, deception, and the physical hazards of the sea.
book-7823: Set between 1948 and the years after the 1967 war, this short historical novel follows a Palestinian couple who return to Haifa after decades of displacement and confront the apartment, streets, and memories they were forced to leave behind. Their visit becomes a search for the infant son lost during the chaos of the Nakba, and the encounter that follows turns private grief into a political and moral reckoning. Through spare scenes and charged dialogue, the narrative examines exile, occupation, parenthood, identity, and the cost of survival under colonial violence. Haifa appears not only as a city but as contested ground where personal history collides with national catastrophe, and where belonging, responsibility, and resistance are painfully redefined.
book-7824: After the mountain people of the Orosini are massacred, a surviving boy is taken in by the secretive Conclave of Shadows and trained for a single purpose: vengeance. In the divided realm of Midkemia and the neighboring kingdom of Olasko, he receives a new identity, courtly education, and lethal skills, then enters a world far removed from his lost village—ducal politics, mercenary violence, gambling houses, and noble intrigue. Operating under the name Talon of the Silver Hawk, he hunts the powerful man responsible for his tribe’s destruction while learning how revenge is complicated by loyalty, deception, and the demands of statecraft. The novel combines quest fantasy, espionage, and coming-of-age themes within a feudal political setting.
book-7825: Retired Justice Department operative Cotton Malone, now a Copenhagen bookseller, is drawn into an international hunt tied to Charlemagne, a vanished Nazi expedition, and clues that point toward Antarctica. The search begins with old wartime records and family secrets, then widens into a contest involving intelligence operatives, wealthy patrons, and rivals with personal stakes in the mystery. As Malone follows evidence from European archives and monuments to remote polar waters, the central conflict turns on whether a buried discovery could reshape modern power and historical understanding. The novel combines espionage, coded documents, archaeological speculation, and violent pursuit across Denmark, Germany, and the Antarctic. Major themes include imperial ambition, the manipulation of history, inherited loyalty, and the danger of turning legend into geopolitical leverage.
book-7826: In a small unnamed town in northern Europe during the Second World War, an invading army seizes control with the expectation of quick obedience. Instead, the occupation exposes a tense struggle between military power and civilian conscience. The mayor, local officials, miners, soldiers, and laborers all confront choices about duty, collaboration, fear, and resistance as daily routines turn into instruments of control and defiance. Steinbeck presents the occupiers not as abstractions but as men shaped by hierarchy, fatigue, and ideology, while the townspeople discover political courage in ordinary acts. The narrative centers on how authority is enforced, how communities respond under surveillance, and how violence alters public life. Themes of freedom, moral responsibility, national identity, and the limits of conquest drive this wartime novella.
book-7827: Growing up in Alexandra, a Black township outside Johannesburg, a boy comes of age under South Africa’s apartheid system, where pass laws, police raids, hunger, and overcrowded shacks shape daily life. The memoir follows his childhood in a family strained by poverty, violence, and fear, while his mother struggles to keep her children alive and in school. Tennis and education gradually open a path beyond the township, placing personal ambition against the rigid racial barriers of the state. Written for young adult and adult readers, the narrative examines systemic racism, survival, family loyalty, masculinity, and the emotional cost of oppression. It also records the textures of township life, making political history tangible through streets, classrooms, train stations, and the constant threat of arrest.
book-7828: A Baltimore editor of small-format “Beginner’s” manuals struggles through the aftermath of his wife’s sudden death when her presence begins to reappear in ordinary places around the city. Aaron Woolcott, physically limited since childhood and emotionally dependent on routines, remembers a marriage marked by affection, irritation, class differences, and constant negotiation over household life. As he moves between his sister’s oversight, work obligations, and encounters with Dorothy that feel both impossible and intimate, the novel examines grief not as pure devotion but as a tangle of memory, guilt, resentment, and longing. Domestic spaces, city streets, and quiet conversations become the setting for a study of bereavement, marriage, and the unsettling work of letting a dead partner remain fully human rather than idealized.
book-7829: Drawing on Sir Thomas Malory’s medieval prose, this selection gathers episodes from the Arthurian cycle in a legendary Britain of castles, forests, abbeys, and battlefields. King Arthur’s rise to the throne, the fellowship of the Round Table, quests undertaken by Lancelot, Gareth, Gawain, and other knights, and the kingdom’s eventual fracture shape the narrative. Chivalric vows, tournaments, enchantments, feuds, and acts of loyalty and betrayal drive the action, while Arthur’s court stands as both political center and moral ideal. The tales examine knighthood, honor, love, Christian faith, violence, and the tension between personal desire and public duty. Presented as selected tales, the volume emphasizes the enduring patterns of adventure, courtly conflict, and tragic decline within the Matter of Britain.
book-783: Tulsa’s House of Night becomes the center of a supernatural crisis as fledgling vampyre Zoey Redbird faces the aftermath of betrayal, fractured friendships, and a dangerous rise in dark power. An ancient winged being, Kalona, enters the mortal world, drawing followers through beauty, fear, and violence, while the High Priestess Neferet’s influence grows more threatening. Zoey must rely on her circle of friends, her bond with warrior Stark, and uneasy ties to Stevie Rae and the secret red fledglings beneath the city. The novel mixes boarding-school drama with vampyre ritual, Cherokee myth, and horror imagery as it explores loyalty, grief, temptation, and the struggle to recognize manipulation behind charisma and authority.
book-7830: A cluster of unexplained sinkings in the Pacific sends marine engineer and investigator Dirk Pitt toward a remote island near Australia, where a brilliant and ruthless industrialist is building a private empire behind a facade of environmental philanthropy. As Pitt traces sabotaged research, vanished ships, and a dead scientist’s warning, he uncovers a plan that links advanced oceanographic technology to mass destruction and political coercion. The action ranges across coral seas, hidden laboratories, luxury compounds, and underwater wrecks, with clues emerging from engineering anomalies and carefully staged accidents. Blending maritime adventure, mystery, and techno-thriller suspense, the novel centers on deception, ecological manipulation, corporate power, and the race to stop a catastrophic attack before it reshapes the balance of nations.
